title: 'PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang sebelum disewakan
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menerusi makluman tambahan kepada Bursa Malaysia, ia berkata anak syarikat tidak langsung milik penuhnya, PTT Assets Sdn Bhd, akan memperoleh empat bidang tanah bersama unit kilang yang sedang atau akan dibina dengan jumlah pertimbangan tunai RM31.997 juta. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat. - DagangNews.com

title: 'A trader’s guide to navigating Budget 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia’s consumer and construction stocks may emerge as beneficiaries of next year’s spending plan as Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim seeks to ease living costs while maintaining fiscal prudence. Anwar, who also serves as finance minister, is expected to announce measures to support households and sustain infrastructure spending when he unveils the annual budget on Friday. Investors will also be on watch for any update on a potential minimum-wage revision, which may boost consumption but add to earnings risk for companies. While Malaysia’s economy remains resilient, a renewed climb in oil prices is driving up fuel-subsidy costs, potentially weighing on the fiscal outlook and investor confidence. The spending plan ahead of a national election due early 2028 comes as Anwar seeks to rebuild public support following recent state poll setbacks. “Given the proximity to the 16th general election or GE16, this will be a people’s budget,” said Alexander Chia, analyst at RHB Research. “Social protection initiatives targeted at the lower and mid-income groups will be positive for the consumer, property, transport and healthcare sectors.” The country’s stock benchmark has fallen nearly 3% this year, lagging some South-East Asian peers including Thailand and Vietnam, as fiscal and political risks weigh. Moreover, foreign funds have sold US$1.59bil of local shares on a net basis so far in 2026. Several key areas warrant close attention in the Budget 2027 announcement. Budget 2027 is poised to include targeted assistance and measures to boost wages as the government seeks to temper the prospect of rising inflation on the cost of living. A likely increase in cash handouts to around RM17bil from RM15bil in 2026 should support mass-market consumption, according to Apex Securities analyst Wong Kai Heng. That should benefit retailers such as 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd and Padini Holdings Bhd, as well as food and beverage companies including Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd, CCK Consolidated Holdings Bhd and Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd. Analysts expect a modest increase in the development expenditure, which would provide continued support for infrastructure investment. Key projects that could feature under Budget 2027 include the light rail transit in Penang, the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme and basic infrastructure projects in Sabah and Sarawak. “Potential beneficiaries of development expenditure expansion would be concentrated among contractors and suppliers exposed to water infrastructure and pipe replacement, flood mitigation, rural infrastructure, grid investment, and projects in Sabah and Sarawak,” Ivy Ng Lee Fang, an analyst at CIMB Securities, wrote in a report. That may boost firms in the construction industry, including Gamuda Bhd, IJM Corp Bhd and Malayan Cement Bhd. The government may allocate funds to upgrade the national grid and water infrastructure to support rising demand from data centres, according to Max Koh, an analyst at RHB Research. Greater funding, along with efforts under the National Energy Transition Roadmap, may benefit energy firms like YTL Power International Bhd and Tenaga Nasional Bhd. Meanwhile, Samaiden Group Bhd and Solarvest Holdings Bhd may also gain from new solar tenders. Investors in the bond market will be focused on the fiscal deficit target, as well as the debt supply for 2027 amid higher energy costs. Any further subsidies that could impact the government’s fiscal consolidation efforts may weigh on investor sentiment. “Prudent fiscal policy is increasingly appreciated by markets,” said Winson Phoon, head of fixed‑income research at Maybank Securities. “We expect further progress toward the government’s medium-term fiscal target of 3% of gross domestic product (GDP), potentially setting a target of 3.3% of GDP.” — Bloomberg

title: 'IOI Properties Gets Bursa Securities Approval for RM7.58b REIT Listing
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) said Bursa Malaysia Securities has approved the listing of its proposed RM7.58 billion IOIPG Malaysia Real Estate Investment Trust (IOIPG REIT) on the Main Market. In a filing on Thursday, the property developer said Bursa Malaysia Securities had, via a letter dated Sept 30, approved the admission of IOIPG REIT to the Official List of Bursa Securities, and the listing and quotation of its 5.5 billion units under the REITs sector. Bursa Malaysia Securities also approved the listing and quotation of up to 300 million new units to be issued as payment of management fees to IOI REIT Management Sdn Bhd — the REIT’s manager. The approval marks another step forward for the listing of IOIPG REIT. IOI Properties received approval from the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) last month for listing of the trust that will house RM7.58 billion worth of retail, office and hotel assets. The target was to complete the listing before the year ends. Other assets include the IOI City Towers and PFCC Towers, as well as six hotels — Putrajaya Marriott Hotel, Le’ Meridien Putrajaya, Moxy Putrajaya, Four Points by Sheraton Puchong, W Kuala Lumpur and Courtyard by Marriott Penang. It also plans to pay out at least 90% of its distributable income on a quarterly basis. The RM7.58 billion acquisition will be satisfied through the issuance of 5.5 billion units at 90 sen each, alongside RM2.65 billion in cash to be funded through sukuk issuance. As part of the proposed offering, 715.61 million units will be offered under the retail portion, including 550.61 million units through a restricted offer for sale to existing IOI Properties shareholders. Eligible shareholders will be entitled to one REIT unit for every ten IOI Properties shares held on an entitlement date to be announced later. Another 55 million units will be allocated to eligible persons, while 110 million units will be made available to the Malaysian public. The institutional offering, meanwhile, will comprise up to 1.48 billion units, including 687.5 million units for Bumiputera investors approved by the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti), with up to 796.89 million units allocated to other Malaysian and foreign institutional and selected investors. On Sept 14, the company revised the planned use of proceeds. It cut the allocation for debt repayment to RM1.53 billion, or 32.9%, from RM3.04 billion, or 65.6%. It raised the allocation for project development, property investment and related activities to RM3.07 billion, or 66%, from RM1.55 billion, or 33.6%. Total proceeds were put at RM4.66 billion, assuming the over-allotment option is not exercised, compared with RM4.62 billion previously. Shares of IOI Properties were down by five sen or 1.5% to RM3.41 at Thursday’s trading day break, giving it a market value of RM18.8 billion. Year to date, its shares have increased by 28.68%. title: 'Bursa Malaysia Key Index Continues Uptrend at Midday
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia's key index maintained its upward trend, increasing by 0.33 percent at midday due to bargain hunting in selected heavyweights. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose by 5.44 points to 1,635.80 from the previous day's close of 1,630.36. The index opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87, fluctuating between 1,630.63 and 1,640.78 during the morning trading session. Across the broader market, there were more decliners than gainers, with 507 losers compared to 499 gainers. Additionally, 494 counters remained unchanged, 1,273 were untraded, and 24 were suspended. The market saw a turnover of 2.24 billion shares worth RM1.26 billion. Hong Leong Investment Bank noted that the barometer index might continue its risk-off consolidation amid high oil prices and bond yields. It also highlighted persistent foreign outflows, US-Iran tensions, and a hawkish Federal Reserve stance as factors affecting market sentiment. The bank identified immediate resistance levels at 1,667-1,682, followed by 1,705-1,720. Among the heavyweights, Maybank rose by nine sen to RM10.04, Public Bank added four sen to RM4.71, Tenaga Nasional increased 16 sen to RM13.06, and IHH Healthcare expanded by 11 sen to RM7.81. However, CIMB eased by one sen to RM7.68. In active trading, Jaks Resources firmed by half a sen to 18.5 sen, JCY International advanced 10 sen to 65.5 sen, V.S Industry ticked up two sen to 29 sen, and Top Glove inched up 3.5 sen to 77 sen, while Zetrix AI decreased 2.5 sen to 14 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries surged 84 sen to RM41.96, UWC gained 36 sen to RM7.46, United Plantations advanced 36 sen to RM31.32, and both Vitrox and UMS Integration climbed 34 sen to RM10.34 and RM8.99, respectively. Kuala Lumpur Kepong led the decliners, falling 46 sen to RM20.96. Other notable decliners included Enra, which lost 29 sen to 69 sen, Allianz Malaysia, which fell 28 sen to RM20.72, BLD Plantations, which shed 26 sen to RM14.74, and Dutch Lady Milk Industries, which erased 20 sen to RM29.80. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index rose 115.75 points to 17,474.73, the FBM Emas Index added 51.08 points to 12,194.61, and the FBM Top 100 Index advanced 50.09 points to 11,983.24. The FBM Emas Shariah Index climbed 66.45 points to 12,079.46, while the FBM ACE Index improved 6.33 points to 5,489.30. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.99 of a point to 178.72, the Energy Index gained 1.06 points to 836.07, the Financial Services Index rose 55.60 points to 19,116.51, and the Plantation Index increased by 4.58 points to 9,031.15.

title: 'Daily Newswatch - 30 Sep 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI ended 1.6% lower at 1,644 points on Tuesday, hitting a ninemonth low as broad-based selling pressure weighed on the market. Sentiment was dampened by rising oil prices and bond yields hovering near multi-year highs, as investors braced for interest rates to remain elevated for longer. Financial Services (-1.7%), Transportation & Logistics (-1.5%) and Property (-1.4%) led sectoral declines, dragged by RHB Bank (-3.8%), Tenaga Nasional (-1.5%) and Nestle Malaysia (-1.2%). Market breadth remained weak, with 684 losers against 412 gainers, while 556 counters were unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly lower on Tuesday as elevated oil prices and US Treasury yields weighed on risk appetite. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 0.3% to 6,870.8, Taiwan’s TAIEX declined 0.8% to 47,632, Japan’s Nikkei 225 slipped 0.6% to 65,481.3, and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng eased 0.5% to 24,523.6. In contrast, the Shanghai Composite gained 0.2% to 3,830.5. In South Korea, losses were recorded in LG Energy Solution (-3.30%), Hyundai Motor (-1.55%), Hanwha Aerospace (-2.22%), and Doosan Enerbility (-2.93%), while weaker domestic business sentiment added to the cautious tone as the BOK’s business sentiment index fell for the first time in three months in September. In China, gains were led by Guangzhou Automobile (+10.0%), Greenland Holdings (+6.4%) and China Fortune (+6.2%), supported by expectations of increased government bond issuance in 4Q26 as Beijing steps up fiscal support to shore up slowing economic growth and weak domestic demand. European equities edged higher on Tuesday as easing oil prices reduced inflation concerns and lowered expectations of an imminent ECB rate hike. The STOXX 50 gained 0.3%, while the STOXX 600 was little changed, with technology stocks leading gains. ASML jumped 4%, while energy stocks weakened as Brent crude eased toward USD104/barrel. Julius Baer surged 7%, while Lindt & Sprüngli fell 8.4% after cutting its sales-growth outlook. US stock indices closed mostly lower on Tuesday as rising Treasury yields and elevated oil prices weighed on sentiment. The S&P 500 fell 0.2% and the Dow shed 130 points, while the Nasdaq gained 0.2%. The 10-year yield climbed to levels last seen in 2007, while the 30-year yield hovered near 2004 highs. Tech stocks were mixed, with Alphabet and Nvidia down 0.5% and 0.7%, respectively, while Meta, Oracle, Broadcom and Micron gained 3.2%, 4.0%, 1.6% and 1.0%, respectively, amid optimism following plans for an Anthropic IPO. US: 10 Year Treasury Note Yield to 5.28% on Tuesday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note resumed its climb to 5.28% on Tuesday, holding at 2007 highs, while the 30-year rate surpassed 5.6% to touch a 2002 dot-com bust level. Global government bonds have come under pressure as Middle East-driven oil price gains fuel expectations that central banks, including the Federal Reserve, will raise interest rates further. Swaps traders are pricing in nearly a full percentage point of Fed rate hikes over the coming year. In the US, strong economic activity, along with concerns over large fiscal deficits and rising government debt, is also weighing on the bond market. (Trading Economics) US: Job openings fall in August; layoffs remain low US consumer confidence fell in September to the lowest level since 2014 as pessimism grew about the economy and the labour market. The Conference Board’s gauge of confidence decreased 6.7 points to 81.9 after a downward revision to the prior month, data released Tuesday showed. The median estimate in a Bloomberg survey of economists was 89. (Bloomberg) US: Consumer confidence plunges to lowest level since 2014 Job openings, a measure of labour demand, had dropped by 256,000 to 7.079 million by the last day of August, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said in its Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, or Jolts report, on Tuesday. Data for July was revised higher to show 7.335 million vacancies instead of the previously reported 7.271 million. (Reuters) US: Gold ticks up after hitting over seven-week low; US data in focus Gold prices edged higher on Tuesday after hitting a more-than-seven-week low in the previous session, as investors watch for US economic data that could offer clues on the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) interest rate outlook. Spot gold rose 0.6% to US$4,140.10 (RM16,899.89) per ounce, as of 0856 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since Aug 5 on Monday. US gold futures gained 0.1% to US$4,171.60. (Reuters) US: Bond market is getting closer to sounding alarm on US economy The Eurozone Economic Sentiment Indicator fell to 97.9 in September 2026 from 98.4 in August, below market expectations of 99.0. It marked the first decline in sentiment since April, as consumers became more concerned about rising oil prices and stalled negotiations to end the sixmonth US-Iran war. Consumer confidence deteriorated to -16.5 from -15.5, while inflation expectations rose to 35.2 from 33.0. (Bloomberg) EU: Area Economic Sentiment Indicator The Eurozone Economic Sentiment Indicator fell to 97.9 in September 2026 from 98.4 in August, below market expectations of 99.0. It marked the first decline in sentiment since April, as consumers became more concerned about rising oil prices and stalled negotiations to end the six-month US-Iran war. Consumer confidence deteriorated to -16.5 from -15.5, while inflation expectations rose to 35.2 from 33.0. (European Commission) UK: Set to pay highest yield since 1999 at 10-year bond auction The UK government is set to pay the highest yield since 1999 at an upcoming auction of 10-year debt, as investors demand additional premiums to compensate for persistent inflation and the prospect of spending increases in next month’s budget. Britain’s Debt Management Office is scheduled to sell up to £4.25 billion (US$5.6 billion or RM22.95 billion) of 4.875% coupon bonds maturing in July 2036 on Tuesday. (Bloomberg) UK: Mortgage approvals fall to 32-month low as loan costs bite Demand for home loans unexpectedly fell in August as higher borrowing costs triggered by the Iran war put off prospective homebuyers. The number of mortgage approvals fell for a second consecutive month to 54,918 from a downwardly revised 55,928 in July, the Bank of England said Tuesday. It was the lowest figure since December 2023. Economists expected no change. (Reuters) CN: Said to offer cheap loans to help state firms pay overdue bills China has started offering low-cost funding to help local government-affiliated firms settle unpaid bills, according to people familiar with the matter, expanding efforts to mend corporate balance sheets and remove one of the biggest bottlenecks for investment. The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) set up a new relending facility to provide cheap capital to commercial and policy banks, they said, asking not to be identified discussing a decision that hasn’t been made public. (Reuters) CN: Expands targeted lending to bolster economy, cuts PSL rate China announced several steps to encourage banks to lend to targeted sectors including infrastructure and technology, in an attempt to juice growth after a months-long slowdown in the economy. The People’s Bank of China increased the quota for a relending programme supporting technological innovation and equipment upgrades by 200 billion yuan (US$28 billion or RM114 billion), bringing the total to 1.4 trillion yuan, according to a statement Tuesday. (Bloomberg) CN: Offers mortgage subsidies to boost ailing property sector China will subsidise mortgage interest payments for first-time homebuyers nationwide, as policymakers step up efforts to revive the housing market amid a prolonged property downturn and slowing economic growth. First-home buyers will get subsidies worth an annualised rate of one percentage point of the mortgage principal, according to a Ministry of Finance statement late Tuesday. To qualify, homes must be 120 square meters or smaller and priced at 1.5 million yuan (US$224,000 or RM913,337) or less. (Bloomberg) CN: Signals economic stimulus to counter worsening slowdown China has given its strongest signal yet that it will move with greater urgency to counter a deepening slowdown, as the government promised to introduce new measures to support the economy and study policies to stabilise the reeling property market. The authorities will “put in place a package of practical and effective additional policies” as they seek to “strengthen counter-cyclical adjustments” to achieve this year’s economic and social development goals, according to a statement issued after a Monday meeting of the State Council, China’s cabinet chaired by Premier Li Qiang. (Bloomberg) SK: Monthly Industrial Statistics, August 2026 South Korea’s industrial production unexpectedly dropped 4.8% month-on-month in August 2026, falling well short of market expectations for a 0.5% increase and reversing an upwardly revised 0.5% rise in July. It was the first decline in industrial production in three months and the steepest decline since May 2020, with manufacturing contracting 5.1% (vs 0.4% in July), weighed down by the automobile industry. Manufacturing production contracted for both domestic (-5.5% vs 1.2%) and overseas (-0.2% vs 4.1%) demand. (Statistics Korea) JP: August factory output falls 1.7% month-on-month Japan's factory output fell 1.7% in August from the previous month, versus the median market forecast for a 1.7% rise, government dat showed on Wednesday. Manufacturers surveyed by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry expect seasonally adjusted output to increase 3.2% in September and grow 3.1% in October.(Reuters) JP: Retail Sales Growth Below Forecasts Retail sales in Japan increased 2.7% year-on-year in August 2026, below market expectations for a 3.3% rise and slowing from a downwardly revised 3.7% growth in the previous month. It was the sixth consecutive month of growth in retail activity, mainly boosted by a 17.7% surge in motor vehicle sales. (Ministry of Economy Trade & Industry (METI) MY: Set to land nearly RM90m in film, TV deals through Australia, South Korea co-productions - minister Malaysia is set to tap international opportunities in the creative industry through two co-production projects with industry partners in Australia and South Korea worth a combined US$22 million (about RM89.7 million) over the next two years. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the collaboration, spearheaded by OMG Studios, would involve Australia’s Madman Entertainment and South Korea’s Greenpatch Studio. (The Edge) MY: No decision yet on new minimum wage, says HR minister The government has yet to make a decision regarding the new minimum wage rate, including claims that it would be raised to RM2,000, RM2,100, or RM2,200, said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R Ramanan. He said any announcement concerning the new rate would only be made after obtaining approval from the Cabinet, including Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. (The Edge) MY: Palm oil may gain premium over soyoil in 2027 on supply risks, says industry official Palm oil could trade at a premium to soyoil in 2027 as El Niño threatens production and rising biodiesel demand in top exporter Indonesia tightens supplies, a senior industry official told Reuters on Tuesday. Palm oil supplies are expected to tighten in 2027 as El Niño-induced dry weather weighs on production, potentially lifting prices above rival soyoil, as happened in 2024, Eddy Martono, chairman of the Indonesian Palm Oil Association, said. (Reuters) MY: Needs 25,000 rail sector workers by 2030 - deputy HR minister Malaysia needs 25,000 workers in rail technology and operations by 2030, said Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan. He said the Human Resources Ministry, through the Manpower Department, is developing suitable Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) courses to meet this goal. (Bernama) MY: BNM considering greater risk-taking to support energy transition Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) is considering allowing financial institutions more room to take on higher risks responsibly as part of efforts to support the energy transition, governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said. He said the central bank is reviewing how regulations could be better calibrated to support the transition, including by giving financial institutions greater flexibility to take on higher risks within an acceptable risk appetite. (Bernama) MY: GLICs, GLCs to catalyse economy with RM120b investments under GEAR-uP over 2024-2028 - Amir Hamzah Government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) are stepping up their role in developing the domestic economy, backed by an additional RM120 billion under the GEAR-uP initiative over 2024-2028. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said more than RM20 billion was invested last year, with a similar level expected this year. (Bernama) CRESNDO: 2Q net profit surges over fourfold to RM70.6m, declares 2 sen dividend Crescendo Corp Bhd's net profit more than quadrupled in the second quarter due to the sale of two parcels of land in Johor to data centre developers. In its bourse filing on Tuesday, the property developer said the sale of the parcels in Kota Cemerlang Industrial Park (KCIP) and Nusa Cemerlang Industrial Park (NCIP) made up a bulk of its net profit for the quarter under review. (The Star) MNC: Wireless switches out advisers for RM83m capital reduction exercise MNC Wireless Bhd said on Tuesday it is terminating the services of its advisers for its proposed capital reduction exercise of RM83 million. In a circular on Bursa Malaysia, the mobile and digital solutions company said the termination of Sierac Corporate Advisers Sdn Bhd was based on a mutual agreement between the two parties. It did not elaborate on the reason for the termination. (The Edge) UMSINT: Seeks to raise RM450m via placement for Penang, Vietnam and Singapore expansion UMS Integration Ltd is seeking to raise up to RM450 million through a placement representing 5.63% of its enlarged share capital, to fund projects in Penang, Malaysia, as well as expansion in Vietnam and Singapore. It plans to issue up to 52.94 million new shares at RM8.50 each, the dual-listed integrated high-precision engineering and manufacturing firm said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Tuesday. (The Edge) UMSINT: Shares suspended on Bursa pending announcement Trading in the shares of integrated high-precision engineering and manufacturing firm UMS Integration Ltd (KL:UMSINT) was suspended on Tuesday pending an announcement. The trading suspension took effect from 9am to 5pm on Tuesday at the company’s request, according to its filing with Bursa Malaysia. (The Edge) SNS: 2Q profit down 37% on higher costs and delivery delays, declares 0.25 sen dividend SNS Network Technology Bhd's second-quarter net profit declined 37.3%, weighed down by lower sales and higher expenses. The ICT solutions provider also saw its revenue slashed by half as supplier-side shortages hampered on-time delivery to customers — a trend also observed in the previous quarter (1QFY2027). (The Edge) GAMUDA: SD Guthrie consortium to build solar plant in Perak for US tech firm A consortium between Gamuda Bhd, SD Guthrie Bhd and Gentari Sdn Bhd have inked an agreement with a US-based technology company for a proposed 680-megawatt renewable energy project in Perak. The project, which includes a four-hour battery energy storage system, will achieve commercial operation in 2029 and run for 21 years, according to an exchange filing. The project may generate more than RM10 billion in gross revenue over the offtake period, according to Gamuda’s estimates. (The Edge) SCIENTX: To acquire 70% stake in China plastic packaging maker for RM101.5m Scientex Bhd is acquiring a 70% stake in Hunan Changcheng Mint New Material Technology Co Ltd (Mintpack), a plastic packaging manufacturer in China’s Hunan province, for 167.3 million yuan (RM101.5 million), as it seeks to expand its footprint in China. The packaging manufacturer and property developer said its wholly owned unit Scientex Packaging (Ayer Keroh) Bhd has entered into an equity interest sale and purchase agreement with Mintpack founder Tan Cui Fang and Hunan Changcheng Tianyi Information Technology Co Ltd (Tianyi) to acquire the stake. (The Edge) AEONCR: 2Q net profit drops 18% on higher impairment losses AEON Credit Service (M) Bhd reported a 18% drop in its net profit for the second quarter amid higher impairment losses on financing receivables. Net profit for the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 (2QFY2027) fell to RM59.30 million from RM72.23 million a year earlier, according to the consumer financing provider's exchange filing on Tuesday. (The Edge) VS: Records first full year loss on lower orders VS Industry Bhd posted its first full-year loss since it was listed in 1998, dragged down by lower orders placed by key customers amid weak global consumer sentiment. The electronic manufacturing services provider registered a net loss of RM53.8 million for its financial year ended July 31, 2026 (FY2026), compared with a net profit of RM36.7 million in the previous year, as revenue fell 3.62% to RM3.65 billion from RM3.79 billion. (The Edge) FAIRE: Johor-based Faire files ACE Market IPO to expand into industrial properties Johor-based property developer Faire Bhd is seeking to list on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia in order to raise funds for its expansion into industrial properties. According to its draft prospectus published on Tuesday, Faire said it intends to strengthen its presence in Johor by expanding its project portfolio and broadening into industrial properties. Its existing portfolio comprises terrace, cluster, semi-detached and detached houses, as well as shop units and shop houses. (The Edge) APOLLO: 1Q profit up nearly 10% on strong sales Confectioner Apollo Food Holdings Bhd posted a 9.5% increase in net profit for its first quarter as stronger sales helped offset higher costs. For the three months ended July 31, 2026 (1QFY2027), net profit rose to RM6.96 million from RM6.36 million the previous year, while revenue grew 13.36% to RM73.76 million from RM65.07 million, driven by higher export sales, particularly in its core Indonesian market. (The Edge) GAMUDA: Annual net profit tops RM1b for second straight year, order book hits RM61b Gamuda Bhd closed its financial year ended July 31, 2026 (FY2026) with a net profit topping RM1 billion for the second straight year, as its construction order book reached a record high. Full-year net profit stood at RM1.05 billion, up 5% from RM1 billion a year earlier, Gamuda said in a bourse filing on Tuesday. Revenue rose 15% year on year to RM18.3 billion from RM16 billion. (The Edge) SUPERMX: Co-founders agree to wind up holding firm, to hold stakes directly Supermax Corp Bhd co-founders Datuk Seri Stanley Thai and wife Datuk Wira Cheryl Tan Bee Geok have resolved the legal wrangle over their company that holds their interests in the glove manufacturer. The settleent entitles the pair to a full disbursement of dividends from Supermax Holdings Sdn Bhd (SHSB) according to their shareholdings of 42.5% to Tan and 57.5% to Thai. SHSB holds 40.3% in Supermax Corp, the RM1.2 billion glove maker that the now estranged married couple founded in 1987. (The Edge) VITROX: Rides AI-fuelled complexity to new highs ViTrox Corp Bhd broke earnings record in its latest quarter and the growth momentum will continue. “This year, our numbers will double. We believe strong growth momentum will continue into the next few years,” co-founder and managing director Datuk Chu Jenn Weng tells The Edge in an interview at its campus in Batu Kawan Industrial Park in Seberang Prai, Penang. (The Edge) VITROX: Planting the seeds for Malaysia's tech ecosystem FOR Datuk Chu Jenn Weng, solving Malaysia’s talent shortage in the technology sector means taking steps long before graduates enter the workforce. That conviction led ViTrox Corp Bhd to build an education arm designed to bridge the gap between classroom learning and industry needs, giving students early exposure to real-world manufacturing problems, advanced equipment and working engineers. (The Edge) AAGB: Needs no bailout, says Fernandes, as fuel shock puts liquidity under scrutiny AIRASIA Group Bhd, which is seeking to raise up to US$1 billion (RM4.08 billion) on the international debt market, has dismissed concerns about its liquidity, with co-founder and adviser Tan Sri Tony Fernandes insisting that the low-cost carrier remains financially resilient. “We do not need a rescue, bailout or whatever,” he said, adding that the group was “good at managing cash” and “strong in liquidity” and had more than RM1 billion available. (The Edge) VANTNRG: Stays in the black in 2Q on lower forex losses, finance costs Vantris Energy Bhd remained in the black for a fourth consecutive quarter, helped by lower foreign exchange losses and finance costs following the completion of its restructuring exercise, as well as the absence of a favourable insurance claim recorded a year earlier. These gains were partly offset by lower contributions from its engineering and construction, and drilling segments. (The Edge) NWE: To tap into changing health trends among younger consumers NWE Resources Group Bhd is looking to tap into changing health and wellness trends among younger consumers with six new health food formulations as part of its business expansion for its initial public offering (IPO). Speaking to reporters after the launch of its prospectus on Tuesday, executive director Tan Chor Han said the group had identified areas including sleep deprivation, stress, eye-care, joint health, colon care and gut health, for which younger people are increasingly turning to health food products in order to address these concerns. (The Edge) KGB: Bags RM172m engineering job for Sarawak manufacturing facility Kelington Group Bhd has secured a RM172 million contract for engineering and early-stage infrastructure development works for an advanced data storage manufacturing facility in Kuching, Sarawak. In a bourse filing on Tuesday, the engineering group said its unit, Kelington Technologies Sdn Bhd, accepted the letter of award on Sept 25 from a manufacturing company located at the Sama Jaya Free Industrial Zone. (The Edge) YINSON: Posts 27% rise in 2Q amid absence of refinancing charge Yinson Holdings Bhd said its net profit for the second quarter grew 26.7% year-on-year amid the absence of a one-off charge related to the refinancing of the floating production storage and offloading (FPSO) Maria Quitéria project financing loan. Net profit for the three months ended July 31, 2026 (2QFY2027) rose to RM128 million from RM101 million in the previous year’s corresponding quarter. (The Edge) JFTECH: Partner Shenzhen HFC surges more than eightfold on debut Shenzhen HFC Co Ltd, which operates an advanced thermal and shielding materials manufacturing facility in Malaysia in partnership with Main Market-listed JF Technology Bhd, saw its shares surge more than eightfold in their Shenzhen Stock Exchange debut. Shares of HFC jumped to around 600 yuan from their initial public offering (IPO) price of 76.86 yuan per share at the opening bell, before hitting an intraday high of 630.01 yuan. The stock then retreated to 613 yuan at Tuesday’s noon break. (The Edge) KLK: Coalfields Retail Park scheduled to reach 100% occupancy by 1Q2027 KLK Land Sdn Bhd's newly soft-opened Coalfields Retail Park in Sungai Buloh is scheduled to achieve 100% occupancy by 1Q2027, according to a press statement issued on Tuesday. The lifestyle retail hub, developed by the property development arm of Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd, spans 21 acres with approximately one million square feet of gross built-up area. (The Edge) SERNKOU: To wind down loss-making plywood manufacturing unit Sern Kou Resources Bud said on Tuesday that its will wind down its plywood manufacturing unit due to continuous quarterly losses since the financial year ended June 30, 2024 (FY2024). In its bourse filing on Tuesday, the wood products manufacturer said there was no reasonable expectation that the financial performance of Sern Kou Plywood Sdn Bhd (SKPW), its 51%-owned subsidiary, will improve in the foreseeable future. full_text: 'Daily Newswatch - 30 Sep 2026. 'The FBM KLCI ended 1.6% lower at 1,644 points on Tuesday, hitting a ninemonth low as broad-based selling pressure weighed on the market. Sentiment was dampened by rising oil prices and bond yields hovering near multi-year highs, as investors braced for interest rates to remain elevated for longer. Financial Services (-1.7%), Transportation & Logistics (-1.5%) and Property (-1.4%) led sectoral declines, dragged by RHB Bank (-3.8%), Tenaga Nasional (-1.5%) and Nestle Malaysia (-1.2%). Market breadth remained weak, with 684 losers against 412 gainers, while 556 counters were unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly lower on Tuesday as elevated oil prices and US Treasury yields weighed on risk appetite. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 0.3% to 6,870.8, Taiwan’s TAIEX declined 0.8% to 47,632, Japan’s Nikkei 225 slipped 0.6% to 65,481.3, and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng eased 0.5% to 24,523.6. In contrast, the Shanghai Composite gained 0.2% to 3,830.5. In South Korea, losses were recorded in LG Energy Solution (-3.30%), Hyundai Motor (-1.55%), Hanwha Aerospace (-2.22%), and Doosan Enerbility (-2.93%), while weaker domestic business sentiment added to the cautious tone as the BOK’s business sentiment index fell for the first time in three months in September. In China, gains were led by Guangzhou Automobile (+10.0%), Greenland Holdings (+6.4%) and China Fortune (+6.2%), supported by expectations of increased government bond issuance in 4Q26 as Beijing steps up fiscal support to shore up slowing economic growth and weak domestic demand. European equities edged higher on Tuesday as easing oil prices reduced inflation concerns and lowered expectations of an imminent ECB rate hike. The STOXX 50 gained 0.3%, while the STOXX 600 was little changed, with technology stocks leading gains. ASML jumped 4%, while energy stocks weakened as Brent crude eased toward USD104/barrel. Julius Baer surged 7%, while Lindt & Sprüngli fell 8.4% after cutting its sales-growth outlook. US stock indices closed mostly lower on Tuesday as rising Treasury yields and elevated oil prices weighed on sentiment. The S&P 500 fell 0.2% and the Dow shed 130 points, while the Nasdaq gained 0.2%. The 10-year yield climbed to levels last seen in 2007, while the 30-year yield hovered near 2004 highs. Tech stocks were mixed, with Alphabet and Nvidia down 0.5% and 0.7%, respectively, while Meta, Oracle, Broadcom and Micron gained 3.2%, 4.0%, 1.6% and 1.0%, respectively, amid optimism following plans for an Anthropic IPO. US: 10 Year Treasury Note Yield to 5.28% on Tuesday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note resumed its climb to 5.28% on Tuesday, holding at 2007 highs, while the 30-year rate surpassed 5.6% to touch a 2002 dot-com bust level. Global government bonds have come under pressure as Middle East-driven oil price gains fuel expectations that central banks, including the Federal Reserve, will raise interest rates further. Swaps traders are pricing in nearly a full percentage point of Fed rate hikes over the coming year. In the US, strong economic activity, along with concerns over large fiscal deficits and rising government debt, is also weighing on the bond market. (Trading Economics) US: Job openings fall in August; layoffs remain low US consumer confidence fell in September to the lowest level since 2014 as pessimism grew about the economy and the labour market. The Conference Board’s gauge of confidence decreased 6.7 points to 81.9 after a downward revision to the prior month, data released Tuesday showed. The median estimate in a Bloomberg survey of economists was 89. (Bloomberg) US: Consumer confidence plunges to lowest level since 2014 Job openings, a measure of labour demand, had dropped by 256,000 to 7.079 million by the last day of August, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said in its Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, or Jolts report, on Tuesday. Data for July was revised higher to show 7.335 million vacancies instead of the previously reported 7.271 million. (Reuters) US: Gold ticks up after hitting over seven-week low; US data in focus Gold prices edged higher on Tuesday after hitting a more-than-seven-week low in the previous session, as investors watch for US economic data that could offer clues on the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) interest rate outlook. Spot gold rose 0.6% to US$4,140.10 (RM16,899.89) per ounce, as of 0856 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since Aug 5 on Monday. US gold futures gained 0.1% to US$4,171.60. (Reuters) US: Bond market is getting closer to sounding alarm on US economy The Eurozone Economic Sentiment Indicator fell to 97.9 in September 2026 from 98.4 in August, below market expectations of 99.0. It marked the first decline in sentiment since April, as consumers became more concerned about rising oil prices and stalled negotiations to end the sixmonth US-Iran war. Consumer confidence deteriorated to -16.5 from -15.5, while inflation expectations rose to 35.2 from 33.0. (Bloomberg) EU: Area Economic Sentiment Indicator The Eurozone Economic Sentiment Indicator fell to 97.9 in September 2026 from 98.4 in August, below market expectations of 99.0. It marked the first decline in sentiment since April, as consumers became more concerned about rising oil prices and stalled negotiations to end the six-month US-Iran war. Consumer confidence deteriorated to -16.5 from -15.5, while inflation expectations rose to 35.2 from 33.0. (European Commission) UK: Set to pay highest yield since 1999 at 10-year bond auction The UK government is set to pay the highest yield since 1999 at an upcoming auction of 10-year debt, as investors demand additional premiums to compensate for persistent inflation and the prospect of spending increases in next month’s budget. Britain’s Debt Management Office is scheduled to sell up to £4.25 billion (US$5.6 billion or RM22.95 billion) of 4.875% coupon bonds maturing in July 2036 on Tuesday. (Bloomberg) UK: Mortgage approvals fall to 32-month low as loan costs bite Demand for home loans unexpectedly fell in August as higher borrowing costs triggered by the Iran war put off prospective homebuyers. The number of mortgage approvals fell for a second consecutive month to 54,918 from a downwardly revised 55,928 in July, the Bank of England said Tuesday. It was the lowest figure since December 2023. Economists expected no change. (Reuters) CN: Said to offer cheap loans to help state firms pay overdue bills China has started offering low-cost funding to help local government-affiliated firms settle unpaid bills, according to people familiar with the matter, expanding efforts to mend corporate balance sheets and remove one of the biggest bottlenecks for investment. The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) set up a new relending facility to provide cheap capital to commercial and policy banks, they said, asking not to be identified discussing a decision that hasn’t been made public. (Reuters) CN: Expands targeted lending to bolster economy, cuts PSL rate China announced several steps to encourage banks to lend to targeted sectors including infrastructure and technology, in an attempt to juice growth after a months-long slowdown in the economy. The People’s Bank of China increased the quota for a relending programme supporting technological innovation and equipment upgrades by 200 billion yuan (US$28 billion or RM114 billion), bringing the total to 1.4 trillion yuan, according to a statement Tuesday. (Bloomberg) CN: Offers mortgage subsidies to boost ailing property sector China will subsidise mortgage interest payments for first-time homebuyers nationwide, as policymakers step up efforts to revive the housing market amid a prolonged property downturn and slowing economic growth. First-home buyers will get subsidies worth an annualised rate of one percentage point of the mortgage principal, according to a Ministry of Finance statement late Tuesday. To qualify, homes must be 120 square meters or smaller and priced at 1.5 million yuan (US$224,000 or RM913,337) or less. (Bloomberg) CN: Signals economic stimulus to counter worsening slowdown China has given its strongest signal yet that it will move with greater urgency to counter a deepening slowdown, as the government promised to introduce new measures to support the economy and study policies to stabilise the reeling property market. The authorities will “put in place a package of practical and effective additional policies” as they seek to “strengthen counter-cyclical adjustments” to achieve this year’s economic and social development goals, according to a statement issued after a Monday meeting of the State Council, China’s cabinet chaired by Premier Li Qiang. (Bloomberg) SK: Monthly Industrial Statistics, August 2026 South Korea’s industrial production unexpectedly dropped 4.8% month-on-month in August 2026, falling well short of market expectations for a 0.5% increase and reversing an upwardly revised 0.5% rise in July. It was the first decline in industrial production in three months and the steepest decline since May 2020, with manufacturing contracting 5.1% (vs 0.4% in July), weighed down by the automobile industry. Manufacturing production contracted for both domestic (-5.5% vs 1.2%) and overseas (-0.2% vs 4.1%) demand. (Statistics Korea) JP: August factory output falls 1.7% month-on-month Japan's factory output fell 1.7% in August from the previous month, versus the median market forecast for a 1.7% rise, government dat showed on Wednesday. Manufacturers surveyed by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry expect seasonally adjusted output to increase 3.2% in September and grow 3.1% in October.(Reuters) JP: Retail Sales Growth Below Forecasts Retail sales in Japan increased 2.7% year-on-year in August 2026, below market expectations for a 3.3% rise and slowing from a downwardly revised 3.7% growth in the previous month. It was the sixth consecutive month of growth in retail activity, mainly boosted by a 17.7% surge in motor vehicle sales. (Ministry of Economy Trade & Industry (METI) MY: Set to land nearly RM90m in film, TV deals through Australia, South Korea co-productions - minister Malaysia is set to tap international opportunities in the creative industry through two co-production projects with industry partners in Australia and South Korea worth a combined US$22 million (about RM89.7 million) over the next two years. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the collaboration, spearheaded by OMG Studios, would involve Australia’s Madman Entertainment and South Korea’s Greenpatch Studio. (The Edge) MY: No decision yet on new minimum wage, says HR minister The government has yet to make a decision regarding the new minimum wage rate, including claims that it would be raised to RM2,000, RM2,100, or RM2,200, said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R Ramanan. He said any announcement concerning the new rate would only be made after obtaining approval from the Cabinet, including Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. (The Edge) MY: Palm oil may gain premium over soyoil in 2027 on supply risks, says industry official Palm oil could trade at a premium to soyoil in 2027 as El Niño threatens production and rising biodiesel demand in top exporter Indonesia tightens supplies, a senior industry official told Reuters on Tuesday. Palm oil supplies are expected to tighten in 2027 as El Niño-induced dry weather weighs on production, potentially lifting prices above rival soyoil, as happened in 2024, Eddy Martono, chairman of the Indonesian Palm Oil Association, said. (Reuters) MY: Needs 25,000 rail sector workers by 2030 - deputy HR minister Malaysia needs 25,000 workers in rail technology and operations by 2030, said Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan. He said the Human Resources Ministry, through the Manpower Department, is developing suitable Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) courses to meet this goal. (Bernama) MY: BNM considering greater risk-taking to support energy transition Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) is considering allowing financial institutions more room to take on higher risks responsibly as part of efforts to support the energy transition, governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said. He said the central bank is reviewing how regulations could be better calibrated to support the transition, including by giving financial institutions greater flexibility to take on higher risks within an acceptable risk appetite. (Bernama) MY: GLICs, GLCs to catalyse economy with RM120b investments under GEAR-uP over 2024-2028 - Amir Hamzah Government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) are stepping up their role in developing the domestic economy, backed by an additional RM120 billion under the GEAR-uP initiative over 2024-2028. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said more than RM20 billion was invested last year, with a similar level expected this year. (Bernama) CRESNDO: 2Q net profit surges over fourfold to RM70.6m, declares 2 sen dividend Crescendo Corp Bhd's net profit more than quadrupled in the second quarter due to the sale of two parcels of land in Johor to data centre developers. In its bourse filing on Tuesday, the property developer said the sale of the parcels in Kota Cemerlang Industrial Park (KCIP) and Nusa Cemerlang Industrial Park (NCIP) made up a bulk of its net profit for the quarter under review. (The Star) MNC: Wireless switches out advisers for RM83m capital reduction exercise MNC Wireless Bhd said on Tuesday it is terminating the services of its advisers for its proposed capital reduction exercise of RM83 million. In a circular on Bursa Malaysia, the mobile and digital solutions company said the termination of Sierac Corporate Advisers Sdn Bhd was based on a mutual agreement between the two parties. It did not elaborate on the reason for the termination. (The Edge) UMSINT: Seeks to raise RM450m via placement for Penang, Vietnam and Singapore expansion UMS Integration Ltd is seeking to raise up to RM450 million through a placement representing 5.63% of its enlarged share capital, to fund projects in Penang, Malaysia, as well as expansion in Vietnam and Singapore. It plans to issue up to 52.94 million new shares at RM8.50 each, the dual-listed integrated high-precision engineering and manufacturing firm said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Tuesday. (The Edge) UMSINT: Shares suspended on Bursa pending announcement Trading in the shares of integrated high-precision engineering and manufacturing firm UMS Integration Ltd (KL:UMSINT) was suspended on Tuesday pending an announcement. The trading suspension took effect from 9am to 5pm on Tuesday at the company’s request, according to its filing with Bursa Malaysia. (The Edge) SNS: 2Q profit down 37% on higher costs and delivery delays, declares 0.25 sen dividend SNS Network Technology Bhd's second-quarter net profit declined 37.3%, weighed down by lower sales and higher expenses. The ICT solutions provider also saw its revenue slashed by half as supplier-side shortages hampered on-time delivery to customers — a trend also observed in the previous quarter (1QFY2027). (The Edge) GAMUDA: SD Guthrie consortium to build solar plant in Perak for US tech firm A consortium between Gamuda Bhd, SD Guthrie Bhd and Gentari Sdn Bhd have inked an agreement with a US-based technology company for a proposed 680-megawatt renewable energy project in Perak. The project, which includes a four-hour battery energy storage system, will achieve commercial operation in 2029 and run for 21 years, according to an exchange filing. The project may generate more than RM10 billion in gross revenue over the offtake period, according to Gamuda’s estimates. (The Edge) SCIENTX: To acquire 70% stake in China plastic packaging maker for RM101.5m Scientex Bhd is acquiring a 70% stake in Hunan Changcheng Mint New Material Technology Co Ltd (Mintpack), a plastic packaging manufacturer in China’s Hunan province, for 167.3 million yuan (RM101.5 million), as it seeks to expand its footprint in China. The packaging manufacturer and property developer said its wholly owned unit Scientex Packaging (Ayer Keroh) Bhd has entered into an equity interest sale and purchase agreement with Mintpack founder Tan Cui Fang and Hunan Changcheng Tianyi Information Technology Co Ltd (Tianyi) to acquire the stake. (The Edge) AEONCR: 2Q net profit drops 18% on higher impairment losses AEON Credit Service (M) Bhd reported a 18% drop in its net profit for the second quarter amid higher impairment losses on financing receivables. Net profit for the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 (2QFY2027) fell to RM59.30 million from RM72.23 million a year earlier, according to the consumer financing provider's exchange filing on Tuesday. (The Edge) VS: Records first full year loss on lower orders VS Industry Bhd posted its first full-year loss since it was listed in 1998, dragged down by lower orders placed by key customers amid weak global consumer sentiment. The electronic manufacturing services provider registered a net loss of RM53.8 million for its financial year ended July 31, 2026 (FY2026), compared with a net profit of RM36.7 million in the previous year, as revenue fell 3.62% to RM3.65 billion from RM3.79 billion. (The Edge) FAIRE: Johor-based Faire files ACE Market IPO to expand into industrial properties Johor-based property developer Faire Bhd is seeking to list on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia in order to raise funds for its expansion into industrial properties. According to its draft prospectus published on Tuesday, Faire said it intends to strengthen its presence in Johor by expanding its project portfolio and broadening into industrial properties. Its existing portfolio comprises terrace, cluster, semi-detached and detached houses, as well as shop units and shop houses. (The Edge) APOLLO: 1Q profit up nearly 10% on strong sales Confectioner Apollo Food Holdings Bhd posted a 9.5% increase in net profit for its first quarter as stronger sales helped offset higher costs. For the three months ended July 31, 2026 (1QFY2027), net profit rose to RM6.96 million from RM6.36 million the previous year, while revenue grew 13.36% to RM73.76 million from RM65.07 million, driven by higher export sales, particularly in its core Indonesian market. (The Edge) GAMUDA: Annual net profit tops RM1b for second straight year, order book hits RM61b Gamuda Bhd closed its financial year ended July 31, 2026 (FY2026) with a net profit topping RM1 billion for the second straight year, as its construction order book reached a record high. Full-year net profit stood at RM1.05 billion, up 5% from RM1 billion a year earlier, Gamuda said in a bourse filing on Tuesday. Revenue rose 15% year on year to RM18.3 billion from RM16 billion. (The Edge) SUPERMX: Co-founders agree to wind up holding firm, to hold stakes directly Supermax Corp Bhd co-founders Datuk Seri Stanley Thai and wife Datuk Wira Cheryl Tan Bee Geok have resolved the legal wrangle over their company that holds their interests in the glove manufacturer. The settleent entitles the pair to a full disbursement of dividends from Supermax Holdings Sdn Bhd (SHSB) according to their shareholdings of 42.5% to Tan and 57.5% to Thai. SHSB holds 40.3% in Supermax Corp, the RM1.2 billion glove maker that the now estranged married couple founded in 1987. (The Edge) VITROX: Rides AI-fuelled complexity to new highs ViTrox Corp Bhd broke earnings record in its latest quarter and the growth momentum will continue. “This year, our numbers will double. We believe strong growth momentum will continue into the next few years,” co-founder and managing director Datuk Chu Jenn Weng tells The Edge in an interview at its campus in Batu Kawan Industrial Park in Seberang Prai, Penang. (The Edge) VITROX: Planting the seeds for Malaysia's tech ecosystem FOR Datuk Chu Jenn Weng, solving Malaysia’s talent shortage in the technology sector means taking steps long before graduates enter the workforce. That conviction led ViTrox Corp Bhd to build an education arm designed to bridge the gap between classroom learning and industry needs, giving students early exposure to real-world manufacturing problems, advanced equipment and working engineers. (The Edge) AAGB: Needs no bailout, says Fernandes, as fuel shock puts liquidity under scrutiny AIRASIA Group Bhd, which is seeking to raise up to US$1 billion (RM4.08 billion) on the international debt market, has dismissed concerns about its liquidity, with co-founder and adviser Tan Sri Tony Fernandes insisting that the low-cost carrier remains financially resilient. “We do not need a rescue, bailout or whatever,” he said, adding that the group was “good at managing cash” and “strong in liquidity” and had more than RM1 billion available. (The Edge) VANTNRG: Stays in the black in 2Q on lower forex losses, finance costs Vantris Energy Bhd remained in the black for a fourth consecutive quarter, helped by lower foreign exchange losses and finance costs following the completion of its restructuring exercise, as well as the absence of a favourable insurance claim recorded a year earlier. These gains were partly offset by lower contributions from its engineering and construction, and drilling segments. (The Edge) NWE: To tap into changing health trends among younger consumers NWE Resources Group Bhd is looking to tap into changing health and wellness trends among younger consumers with six new health food formulations as part of its business expansion for its initial public offering (IPO). Speaking to reporters after the launch of its prospectus on Tuesday, executive director Tan Chor Han said the group had identified areas including sleep deprivation, stress, eye-care, joint health, colon care and gut health, for which younger people are increasingly turning to health food products in order to address these concerns. (The Edge) KGB: Bags RM172m engineering job for Sarawak manufacturing facility Kelington Group Bhd has secured a RM172 million contract for engineering and early-stage infrastructure development works for an advanced data storage manufacturing facility in Kuching, Sarawak. In a bourse filing on Tuesday, the engineering group said its unit, Kelington Technologies Sdn Bhd, accepted the letter of award on Sept 25 from a manufacturing company located at the Sama Jaya Free Industrial Zone. (The Edge) YINSON: Posts 27% rise in 2Q amid absence of refinancing charge Yinson Holdings Bhd said its net profit for the second quarter grew 26.7% year-on-year amid the absence of a one-off charge related to the refinancing of the floating production storage and offloading (FPSO) Maria Quitéria project financing loan. Net profit for the three months ended July 31, 2026 (2QFY2027) rose to RM128 million from RM101 million in the previous year’s corresponding quarter. (The Edge) JFTECH: Partner Shenzhen HFC surges more than eightfold on debut Shenzhen HFC Co Ltd, which operates an advanced thermal and shielding materials manufacturing facility in Malaysia in partnership with Main Market-listed JF Technology Bhd, saw its shares surge more than eightfold in their Shenzhen Stock Exchange debut. Shares of HFC jumped to around 600 yuan from their initial public offering (IPO) price of 76.86 yuan per share at the opening bell, before hitting an intraday high of 630.01 yuan. The stock then retreated to 613 yuan at Tuesday’s noon break. (The Edge) KLK: Coalfields Retail Park scheduled to reach 100% occupancy by 1Q2027 KLK Land Sdn Bhd's newly soft-opened Coalfields Retail Park in Sungai Buloh is scheduled to achieve 100% occupancy by 1Q2027, according to a press statement issued on Tuesday. The lifestyle retail hub, developed by the property development arm of Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd, spans 21 acres with approximately one million square feet of gross built-up area. (The Edge) SERNKOU: To wind down loss-making plywood manufacturing unit Sern Kou Resources Bud said on Tuesday that its will wind down its plywood manufacturing unit due to continuous quarterly losses since the financial year ended June 30, 2024 (FY2024). In its bourse filing on Tuesday, the wood products manufacturer said there was no reasonable expectation that the financial performance of Sern Kou Plywood Sdn Bhd (SKPW), its 51%-owned subsidiary, will improve in the foreseeable future. title: 'CIMB Scheduled Downtime for Debit Card Users
body: '14th September 2026 - 2 min read You won’t be able to pay with your CIMB debit card for a few hours on 19, 22, and 23 September 2026. CIMB will be doing scheduled maintenance on its debit card system during the early morning on each of these days. The break covers debit cards from both CIMB Bank and CIMB Islamic. CIMB shared the dates in a notice to cardholders on 9 September 2026. All three maintenance breaks start at midnight. The first break starts when Friday night (18 September) turns into Saturday. The next two start straight after Monday night and Tuesday night. The longest break is on Tuesday, 22 September, when your card won’t work until 7.30am. If you usually pay for breakfast or your morning commute with your debit card, you’ll need another way to pay that morning. During these hours, you can’t make any purchases with your CIMB debit card. This includes tapping or inserting your card at a payment terminal in a shop, and entering your card details to pay on a website or app. It applies whether your card uses MyDebit, Visa, or Mastercard. So if you tap your card at a convenience store after midnight or pay for a late night food order with a saved card, the payment will fail. The card will work as usual again once each break ends. Paying through FPX, where you log in to your online banking to pay a website, doesn’t use your debit card. Neither do DuitNow transfers or scanning a DuitNow QR code with your banking app. CIMB’s notice only lists debit card purchases, so FPX and DuitNow payments aren’t included in this maintenance. If you need to buy something during these hours, pay for it earlier in the evening, or use FPX or DuitNow QR if the shop or website accepts them. If you’re unsure whether a specific payment will be affected, you can check with CIMB directly before the maintenance dates. For more information, you can read CIMB’s full notice [PDF]. title: 'Batu Kawan’s Takeover of MKH Crosses 95%
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 30): Batu Kawan Bhd’s (KL:BKAWAN) unconditional mandatory takeover of MKH Bhd (KL:MKH) has crossed the 95% threshold, paving the way for the property developer’s delisting. As at market close on Wednesday, Batu Kawan and its wholly owned unit Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd, together with parties acting in concert, held 548.85 million MKH shares, representing a 95.16% stake, according to a statement issued on their behalf by Maybank Investment Bank Bhd. With the offeror having received valid acceptances of not less than nine-tenths in the nominal value of the offer shares, Batu Kawan and Whitmore will invoke Section 222(1) of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 to compulsorily acquire the remaining MKH shares from dissenting shareholders, the statement said. The takeover offer, it said, will remain open until Oct 8, following an extension from the original Sept 17 closing date. Bursa Malaysia Securities will suspend trading of MKH shares upon the expiry of five market days from Oct 8. Thereafter, Batu Kawan and Whitmore will procure MKH to take the necessary steps to withdraw its listing status from Bursa Malaysia. Two weeks ago, minority shareholders of MKH and its separately listed plantation arm, MKH Oil Palm (East Kalimantan) Bhd (KL:MKHOP), were given contrasting recommendations regarding Batu Kawan's dual takeover play. Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd, the independent adviser appointed by MKH, deemed the RM2 cash buyout “not fair but reasonable”, noting that the offer price undervalues the property developer’s fair asset worth. On the other hand, Mainstreet Advisers Sdn Bhd urged MKH Oil Palm shareholders to reject the related 66.26 sen per share buyout offer, labelling it "not fair and not reasonable". Mainstreet emphasised that the offer represents a steep 47% discount to MKH Oil Palm's net asset value, and noted that Batu Kawan intends to maintain the plantation unit's listing. The takeover was initiated in May, when Batu Kawan, through Whitmore, agreed to acquire a combined 47.7% stake in MKH from members of the Chen family for RM549.8 million, or RM2 per share. The RM2 offer valued the total cost of taking MKH private at up to RM1.15 billion, including the initial stake purchase. Batu Kawan's share price closed unchanged at RM20.52 on Wednesday, with a market capitalisation of RM8.2 billion. MKH also settled unchanged at RM1.99 with a market value of RM1.17 billion, while MKH Oil Palm closed unchanged at 64.5 sen, valuing the group at RM660 million. title: 'Smoky Singapore gears up to talk money ahead of F1
body: 'SINGAPORE, Oct 5 (Reuters) - Regional, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are meeting in Singapore for a slew of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Grand Prix as haze continues to shroud the city-state. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, famed investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, co-founder of the family-backed cryptocurrency business, are expected, while hundreds of thousands of Formula 1 fans will converge on the island. The night race through the city streets and some 40 sideline events are typically a global showcase for Singapore and hotel room rates have soared. The Fullerton Bay Hotel next to the race track is charging S$5,030 ($3,933) a night for a room that typically costs $1,460. This year the pall from Indonesia's most intense fires in more than a decade will probably form part of the backdrop. Air quality was forecast at the "high moderate to low unhealthy" range on Monday by Singapore's environment agency. No longer-range forecast was provided for Sunday's Grand Prix. Singapore's tourism board said F1 and its surrounding events had "strong momentum" reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. Jitters in financial markets where bond prices are slumping and sentiment around on AI is shifting from euphoric to cautious will occupy investors and business chiefs at the Forbes CEO Conference andMilken Asia Summit, which runs from Wednesday. Trump, a co-founder of crypto venture World Liberty Financial, is due to speak at the TOKEN2049 cryptocurrency event with digital asset markets fragile following a bruising 12 months. A hoped-for regulatory framework failed last month to clear the US Senate, in part as President Donald Trump's personal crypto dealings became a flashpoint for Democrats. Despite a recent bounce, the total value of the cryptocurrency market is down about a quarter over the last 12 months to $3 trillion, according to data aggregator CoinGecko. Still, organisers say their event is nearly sold out with 25,000 attendees expected, the same as last year. The Straits Times reported that about 90,000 "c-suite," or top ranking, executives will be in town. F1 generates around S$145 million in incremental tourism receipts for Singapore each year, according to official estimates. Maybank economistChua Hak Bin expects it to hit S$160 million this year, along with "wider economic benefits" from deals struck at sideline events. ($1 = 1.2794 Singapore dollars) (Reporting by Xinghui Kok and Tom Westbrook; Editing by Kim Coghill)

title: 'Pesara tolak tawaran RM9,799 Maybank, tuntut semula RM48,999
body: 'KUCHING: Seorang pesara menolak tawaran Maybank sebanyak RM9,799.99 sebagai penyelesaian penuh dan muktamad selepas kehilangan RM48,999.99 menerusi lima transaksi tanpa kebenaran daripada akaunnya.  Ahli Dewan Undangan Negeri (ADUN) Padungan, Chong Chieng Jen, berkata mangsa yang hanya dikenali sebagai Encik Lo kehilangan wang berkenaan antara 2 dan 3 Ogos lalu tanpa pengetahuannya.  Menurut beliau, lima transaksi berkenaan melibatkan RM3,000 melalui FPX pada 12.12 tengah hari, 2 Ogos; RM3,000 ke akaun Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN) pada 12.18 tengah hari; RM3,000 kepada RYT Bank melalui FPX pada 12.31 tengah hari; RM999.99 kepada seorang individu bernama Joanne Johan pada 12.35 tengah hari dan RM39,000 ke akaun Alliance Bank pada 3.12 pagi, 3 Ogos.  Chong berkata, Lo hanya menyedari kehilangan wang tersebut selepas pergi ke bank pada pagi 3 Ogos.  “Encik Lo kehilangan RM48,999.99 daripada akaun Maybank walaupun beliau tidak melakukan sebarang kesalahan. Kini, Maybank menawarkan RM9,799.99 kepadanya dengan syarat beliau menggugurkan tuntutannya terhadap bank.  “Ini tidak boleh diterima,” katanya dalam kenyataan hari ini.  Beliau berkata, pihak bank dimaklumkan mengenai transaksi tanpa kebenaran itu dalam tempoh 24 jam selepas kejadian, manakala transaksi terakhir berjumlah RM39,000 dilaporkan kurang daripada tujuh jam selepas ia berlaku.  “Walaupun bank dimaklumkan mengenai transaksi tanpa kebenaran itu dalam tempoh 24 jam, dan transaksi terakhir dilaporkan kurang daripada tujuh jam selepas ia berlaku, bank mendakwa ia tidak dapat menyekat transaksi berkenaan.  “Bank juga dikatakan tidak mempunyai mekanisme tempoh bertenang bagi akaun dan transaksi Maybank,” katanya.  Menurut Chong, sekiranya Maybank melaksanakan tempoh bertenang seperti yang disarankan oleh Bank Negara Malaysia pada 2022, transaksi berkenaan berkemungkinan dapat disekat dan kerugian Lo dapat dielakkan.  Beliau berkata, susulan campur tangannya dalam kes itu, Maybank minggu lalu menawarkan RM9,799.99, bersamaan 20 peratus daripada jumlah kerugian, sebagai penyelesaian penuh dan muktamad.  “Encik Lo ialah seorang pesara. RM48,999 merupakan wang simpanan hasil titik peluhnya.  “Bagi Maybank, jumlah itu mungkin tidak besar, tetapi bagi Encik Lo, ia amat besar dan memberi kesan serius kepadanya,” katanya.  Chong berkata, Lo tetap dengan pendiriannya untuk menolak tawaran berkenaan kerana jumlah tersebut hanya meliputi 20 peratus daripada keseluruhan kerugiannya.  Beliau turut menggesa polis menjalankan siasatan menyeluruh terhadap kes berkenaan, termasuk meneliti sistem Maybank serta bank-bank penerima yang terlibat dalam transaksi tersebut.  Pada masa sama, Chong menggesa agar keseluruhan jumlah kerugian Lo dibayar balik dan berkata beliau akan terus mengikuti perkembangan kes berkenaan bagi membantu pesara tersebut.

title: 'RHB Group maintains Malaysia's 2026 growth forecast at 5.4 pct
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 - Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) for 2026 is projected at 5.4 per cent, underpinned by resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in electric and electronic (E&E) exports, said RHB Group. Its group chief economist and head of market research Barnabas Gan said the bank revised the headline inflation forecast to 1.9 per cent for 2026 from 2.1 per cent previously, reflecting softer-than-expected price pressures. For the first eight months of the year, inflation averaged 1.8 per cent, alongside the restoration of the BUDI95 monthly quota and an increase in the diesel subsidy quota from September. "For the rest of 2026, the inflation trajectory will be shaped by global commodity price movements, changes in domestic policies, as well as potential upside from food inflation," he said in RHB’s Global Economics Outlook for 4Q 2026 today. Gan added that domestic policy measures, such as RON95 and diesel subsidies, stable food prices, stable demand conditions, and a relatively stable ringgit, as well as gradual pass-through to consumer prices, should help keep inflation contained. Meanwhile, the overnight policy rate is expected to remain unchanged at 2.75 per cent at the upcoming November Monetary Policy Committee meeting amid manageable inflation. Moving forward, RHB Bank expects Bank Negara Malaysia to deliver a token 25 basis points (bps) hike in the first half of 2027 (1H 2027) as a normalisation move towards a more neutral policy setting rather than a response to significant inflationary pressures. He also expects the 2026 fiscal deficit to remain broadly on track towards the government’s 3.5 per cent of GDP target, although risks are tilted towards a modest overshoot given the relatively high deficit in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026) and uncertainties surrounding fuel subsidy expenditure. At the same time, the bank is maintaining its current account surplus forecast at 2.4 per cent of GDP for 2026, versus a 2.5 per cent surplus in 1H 2026. "The goods surplus should remain supported by resilient E&E exports amid the global technology cycle, while robust tourism receipts and information and communication technology services exports should underpin the services account. "Together, these should sustain Malaysia’s current account surplus," Gan said.

Moving forward, RHB Bank expects Bank Negara Malaysia to deliver a token 25 basis points (bps) hike in the first half of 2027 (1H 2027) as a normalisation move towards a more neutral policy setting rather than a response to significant inflationary pressures. He also expects the 2026 fiscal deficit to remain broadly on track towards the government’s 3.5 per cent of GDP target, although risks are tilted towards a modest overshoot given the relatively high deficit in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026) and uncertainties surrounding fuel subsidy expenditure. At the same time, the bank is maintaining its current account surplus forecast at 2.4 per cent of GDP for 2026, versus a 2.5 per cent surplus in 1H 2026. "The goods surplus should remain supported by resilient E&E exports amid the global technology cycle, while robust tourism receipts and information and communication technology services exports should underpin the services account. body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ditutup rendah pada Khamis dalam keadaan tekanan jualan yang berterusan, sejajar dengan prestasi Wall Street semalaman yang bercampur-campur dan berhati-hati. Pada 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) menurun 20.81 mata atau 1.26 peratus kepada 1,630.36 daripada 1,651.17 semasa ditutup pada Rabu. Indeks petunjuk pasaran yang dibuka rendah 1.30 mata kepada 1,649.87 bergerak antara 1,630.10 dan 1,649.87 sepanjang sesi dagangan. Pasaran secara menyeluruh negatif, dengan kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung sebanyak 750 berbanding 342 manakala 495 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,186 tidak diniagakan dan 12 yang lain digantung.
