title: 'Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi disokong peningkatan penerimaan risiko
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi sedikit hari ini sejajar dengan prestasi positif di pasaran serantau susulan penerimaan risiko yang bertambah baik. Peningkatan penerimaan risiko ini disokong oleh data lemah pasaran buruh Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang meredakan jangkaan Rizab Persekutuan AS mengetatkan dasarnya serta tekanan ke atas hasil bon. Pada 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 0.88 mata kepada 1,631.75 daripada paras penutup 1,630.87 pada Jumaat minggu lepas. Indeks petunjuk pasaran yang dibuka tinggi naik 2.55 mata kepada 1,633.42, bergerak antara paras 1,630.95 dan 1,640.46 sepanjang sesi dagangan. Bagaimanapun, di keseluruhan pasaran, kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung sebanyak 599 berbanding 564, manakala 523 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,087 tidak diniagakan dan 24 digantung. Jumlah dagangan meningkat kepada 4.78 bilion unit bernilai RM2.89 bilion daripada 4.23 bilion unit bernilai RM2.70 bilion pada Jumaat minggu lepas. Naib presiden penyelidikan ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata kaunter teknologi merupakan antara saham yang meraih keuntungan tinggi. Di Wall Street semalaman, indeks S&P 500 meningkat 0.73 peratus kepada 7,722.72 dan Nasdaq Composite naik 1.19 peratus kepada 27,190.86. Beliau berkata pasaran saham tempatan dijangka kekal positif dalam tempoh terdekat ini memandangkan FBM KLCI masih berada dalam kedudukan terlebih jual susulan penurunan ketara minggu lepas yang mana keadaan ini dijangka terus menarik minat pembelian pada harga rendah khususnya bagi saham mewah terpilih. “Kecairan domestik juga terus menyokong, dengan institusi tempatan merekodkan pembelian bersih sebanyak RM352.4 juta pada minggu lepas, walaupun aktiviti penjualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing kekal menjadi faktor hambatan,” katanya kepada Bernama. Justeru, Thong menjangkakan indeks petunjuk pasaran akan mencatatkan pemulihan secara beransur-ansur namun kekal tidak menentu, dengan FBM KLCI berkemungkinan diniagakan dalam jajaran 1,620-1,650 pada minggu ini. Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Public Bank meningkat lima sen kepada RM4.71, CIMB naik lapan sen kepada RM7.73, Tenaga Nasional menokok empat sen kepada RM13.00, Maybank susut dua sen kepada RM10.00, dan IHH Healthcare turun empat sen kepada RM7.76. Dalam kalangan saham aktif, V.S Industry meningkat tiga sen kepada 32 sen, Zetrix AI susut lima sen kepada 6.5 sen, Jaks Resources turun sedikit sebanyak satu sen kepada 17 sen, Excel Force MSC merosot empat sen kepada 17 sen, manakala NationGate tidak berubah pada RM1.83. Dalam kalangan kaunter paling untung, Malaysian Pacific Industries meningkat RM1.00 kepada RM43.40, UMS Integration melonjak 37 sen kepada RM9.40, Kelington naik 49 sen kepada RM9.12, Nestle menokok 48 sen kepada RM90.00, dan Samaiden menambah 35 sen kepada RM3.19. Dalam kalangan saham paling rugi, Batu Kawan susut RM1.48 kepada RM18.98, United Plantations turun 32 sen kepada RM31.06, Hengyuan Refining Company berkurangan 18 sen kepada RM3.46 manakala Kuala Lumpur Kepong dan YTL Power International menyusut 14 sen masing-masing kepada RM20.86 dan RM5.54. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 meningkat 61.56 mata kepada 17,543.49, Indeks FBM Emas menambah 19.78 mata kepada 12,190.35, Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 15.70 mata kepada 11,973.38, Indeks FBM Emas Shariah menokok 8.69 mata kepada 12,069.01 dan Indeks FBM ACE melonjak 77.15 mata kepada 5,606.61. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian naik sedikit sebanyak 0.45 mata kepada 178.97 dan Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan menambah 99.63 mata kepada 19,140.14, manakala Indeks Tenaga susut 3.09 mata kepada 829.94 dan Indeks Perladangan turun 125.52 mata kepada 8,931.03. Jumlah dagangan Pasaran Utama meningkat kepada 3.13 bilion unit bernilai RM2.41 bilion daripada 2.67 bilion unit bernilai RM2.34 bilion pada Jumaat minggu lepas. Jumlah dagangan waran naik kepada 1.04 bilion unit bernilai RM208.20 juta daripada 973.40 juta unit bernilai RM160.21 juta sebelumnya. Jumlah dagangan Pasaran ACE menokok kepada 611.02 juta unit bernilai RM267.66 juta daripada 593.05 juta unit bernilai RM205.21 juta. Sementara itu, kaunter produk dan perkhidmatan pengguna menyumbang sebanyak 248.10 juta saham di Pasaran Utama, diikuti produk dan perkhidmatan perindustrian (439.37 juta), pembinaan (183.56 juta), teknologi (1.76 bilion), perkhidmatan kewangan (49.02 juta), hartanah (106.95 juta), perladangan (22.08 juta), amanah pelaburan hartanah (10.76 juta), dana tertutup (152,900), tenaga (106.66 juta), penjagaan kesihatan (103.20 juta), telekomunikasi dan media (22.11 juta), pengangkutan dan logistik (40.92 juta), utiliti (38.48 juta), serta amanah perniagaan (162,200). -- BERNAMA

title: 'Bella, Syed Saddiq’s love story to feature in reality series
body: 'Kuala Lumpur: Singer-actress Bella Astillah and Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman will share their journey towards marriage and life as a couple through an upcoming eight-episode reality series. Titled "Walimatul Urus Bella Astillah & Syed Saddiq", the series will document their wedding preparations, family moments and journey into married life. Bella, whose full name is Dayang Nabellah Awang Astillah, said the series would give fans a more personal glimpse into their relationship and how they first got to know each other. Syed Saddiq said he was looking forward to their wedding on Oct 10 at Menara Merdeka Maybank in Kuala Lumpur and sharing the occasion with family, friends and supporters. The series will also feature the couple’s wedding reception in Kota Kinabalu on Nov 17, to showcase behind-the-scenes moments from their Sabah celebration. title: 'Maybank falls below RM10 for first time in nine months, rising bond yields hurt banking stocks
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields. Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. Banks will also have to increase their rates to attract depositors, leading to higher funding costs. That would weigh on banks’ near term non-interest income as well as their capital ratios, Affin Hwang Investment Bank flagged in a note on Thursday. Maybank, the country’s top bank in terms of assets, fell for the third straight day and closed down 0.4% at RM9.95. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) and Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL:HLBANK) each declined over 1%. The Bursa Malaysia Financial Services Index, which also tracks non-bank firms such as insurers and stockbrokers, fell to its lowest level in 10 months. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating. A growing number of economists expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the overnight policy rate in November during the final scheduled monetary policy review for the year. Rising yields tend to lead to higher corporate bond yields, which also tie-in to capital raising decisions both for banks and other corporates and, subsequently, fee income to the banks, Affin Hwang said. Maybank and Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (KL:ABMB) have on their books the longest bond duration — the length of time for a bond to repay its cost in cash flows while also being a measure of sensitivity to changes in interest rates — according to the research house’s analysis. Public Bank Bhd (KL:PBBANK) and Hong Leong Bank, meanwhile, have the shortest duration. In terms of capital ratios, Maybank, RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) and CIMB could see the largest drops, while Public Bank and Hong Leong Bank would see the least due to their portfolios’ shorter duration, the house added.

title: 'Why is Malaysia sending back Rohingya refugees to Myanmar?
body: 'They sought refuge in Malaysia nearly a decade ago, fleeing persecution and war in Myanmar. But thousands of Rohingya refugees are being sent back to a nation still plagued by violence. The Malaysian government is facing accusations of forcibly deporting the refugees – a charge the goverment denies. It says the process is voluntary and coordinated with Myanmar’s government. But human rights groups say this process violates international law by sending refugees to countries where they risk facing prosecution or torture. So, will this concern stop the Rohingya being sent back to Myanmar? title: 'Stock Today: Maybank Falls 1.2% After RM1.56 Billion AT1 Sukuk Redemption
body: 'Maybank shares fell 12 sen or 1.18% to RM10.04 at 3.35pm, with the banking counter trading below its previous close amid broader caution in the financial sector.  The stock opened at RM10.16 and rose to an intraday high of RM10.20 before easing to a low of RM10.02. Some 7.9 million shares changed hands based on the reported volume of 79,022 (’00).  The counter’s previous close was RM10.16, while the current best bid stood at RM10.02 for 642,000 shares and the best offer at RM10.04 for 494,700 shares.  The share price movement comes after Maybank fully redeemed its RM1.56 billion Additional Tier 1 (AT1) Sukuk Mudharabah on Sept 25, its first call date seven years after the securities were issued.  The sukuk was originally issued on Sept 25, 2019 and formed part of Maybank’s AT1 capital instruments.  Meanwhile, Bank Negara Malaysia Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the central bank was reviewing whether financial institutions could be given greater flexibility to take on higher risks within acceptable limits to support Malaysia’s energy transition.  The move could have implications for how banks assess and finance green energy projects, particularly those that are technically feasible but not yet commercially viable.  At the time of writing, Maybank remained 1.18% lower for the session.

title: 'The Ladies 2026: 42 pemain mulakan saingan pusingan pertama - Portal Berita RTM
body: 'SERI KEMBANGAN, 1 Oktober – Pusingan pertama Kejohanan Golf Wanita The Ladies 2026 menyaksikan 42 pemain mula beraksi seawal pukul 7.30 pagi tadi. Saingan kali ini turut menampilkan gandingan pemain profesional serta amatur seperti Allycia Gan, Liyana Durisic, Durriyah Damian dan Kelly Tan. Menurut The Mines Resort & Golf Club, matlamat utama kejohanan tersebut adalah untuk melahirkan lebih ramai pemain berwibawa tempatan. Kejohanan tersebut juga sebagai batu loncatan penting sebelum saingan bertaraf antarabangsa menjelang kejohanan Maybank Championship tidak lama lagi. Penganjuran itu membawa mesej yang jelas kepada generasi muda bahawa kerjaya dalam bidang sukan golf profesional bukan mustahil untuk dicapai oleh wanita Malaysia. Kejohanan golf wanita, The Ladies 2026 rasmi membuka tirai menerusi acara Pro-Am Diraja di The Mines Resort and Golf Club, kelmarin. Kejohanan tersebut kembali buat kali kedua dengan menyasarkan visi menjadi antara kejohanan wanita berprestij di rantau ini, sebelum melangkah ke pentas antarabangsa. Kejohanan yang berlangsung di Kelab Golf The Mines dari 1 hingga 3 Oktober itu menawarkan jumlah hadiah wang tunai sehingga RM100,000.

title: 'Construction Firm SLGC Ends First Trading Day Below IPO Price
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): SLGC Bhd (KL:SLG) ended its first trading day on the ACE Market below its initial public offering (IPO) price. The construction firm’s shares closed at 25 sen on Tuesday, three sen or 10.71% lower than the IPO price of 28 sen per share, after hitting an intraday low of 24 sen as more than 83 million shares exchanged hands. At the closing price, the company based in Johor had a market capitalisation of RM140 million. Ahead of the listing, SLGC shares were oversubscribed by just over three times by retail investors, while a portion of the IPO was undersubscribed and had to be reallocated to other investors. “Now that SLGC is a listed company, the priority for us is to continue strengthening the business while staying disciplined in how we grow and we intend to keep improving on how we deliver,” managing director Yong Zheng Lin said in his speech at the listing ceremony. SLGC is a building construction contractor with G7 grade and got its start in 2009 under the name SLG Construction Sdn Bhd before being incorporated in 2024. The company also has an operations office in Taman Gembira, Kuala Lumpur. The company is mainly involved in design and building construction services for residential and non-residential works. SLGC's customers include property developers and building owners in Malaysia. The IPO raised about RM29.4 million for the company and another RM17.64 million for four selling shareholders that include Yong and his wife Chew Ka Yan. Liong Yang Herng, the company’s project director, and contract director Loo Chun Kok are also cashing out part of their stake in SLGC. The company has allocated RM9.2 million of the IPO proceeds towards acquisition of construction machinery and equipment, RM7.6 million to repay bank borrowings, and RM7.5 million for general working capital. The rest will cover software upgrades and listing expenses. M&A Securities Sdn Bhd acted as the principal adviser, sponsor, underwriter, and placement agent for the IPO. title: 'DNB Completes RM5.2 Bil Syndicated Islamic Financing Ahead of Ownership Transition
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, which it said will strengthen its financial position and support its next phase of growth. In a statement, DNB said the financing, the largest syndicated loan facility arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia, includes the refinancing of its Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on Sept 29, 2026, and provides longer-term funding. The exercise comes as DNB prepares to transition from a government-backed structure to equal ownership among its three mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders — CelcomDigi Bhd (KL:CDB) through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd (KL:YTLPOWR) — expected in early fourth quarter of 2026. Minister of Finance Inc will exit as an ordinary shareholder but retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and oversee key strategic matters. DNB said the financing was completed alongside the award of the full 100MHz of the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz (F0) spectrum and the conversion of its entire 240MHz spectrum holding into a spectrum assignment. The spectrum assignment takes effect from Oct 1, 2026, following its issuance by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission. DNB said the spectrum assignment will increase network capacity, efficiency and performance, while supporting technologies such as massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities. Chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said in the statement the financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate independently, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and make use of its expanded spectrum assets. DNB was established in March 2021 to accelerate Malaysia’s 5G roll-out and operate as the country’s sole wholesale 5G network provider. In May 2023, the government announced a shift to a dual 5G network model. U Mobile Sdn Bhd was selected to develop Malaysia’s second 5G network in November 2024 and was subsequently offboarded from DNB’s network on June 30, 2026. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger, with AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd as joint mandated lead arrangers for the financing. AmInvestment Bank was the financial adviser to DNB. title: 'Four Sikh scholars show the opportunities beyond SPM
body: 'By Manjit Singh | Malaysia | Four Malaysian Sikh students have secured fully funded scholarships for overseas studies in 2026, showing how strong academic results, co-curricular involvement and persistence can open doors to leading universities abroad. Dilpreet Kaur, Gurmansimran Kaur, Priety Kaur and Satishver Singh all began their scholarship journeys after completing the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM), the national public examination taken by all Form 5 secondary school students in Malaysia at the end of their 11th year of formal education. Their scholarships supported their progression through pre-university studies and on to undergraduate programmes overseas. SEE ALSO: Malaysian Sikh Education Aid Fund (MSEAF) Dilpreet will pursue a BSc in Chemistry at Imperial College London, while Gurmansimran will study Accounting and Finance at the University of Manchester. Priety will pursue an MEng in Electrical and Electronic Engineering, also at Manchester, while Satishver is pursuing Data Science at the University of California, Berkeley. Beyond their academic achievements, the four say scholarship applicants should start preparing early and recognise that selectors often look beyond examination grades. Leadership roles, competitions, volunteering, research, internships, community activities and other experiences can help students develop the skills and interests that strengthen an application. Their other key advice: apply widely. Scholarship applications can involve setbacks and rejection, they say, but students should continue looking for opportunities instead of allowing one unsuccessful application to end the journey. They also encourage students to seek internships or research experience connected with their intended university courses. Such exposure can help applicants better understand their chosen fields while demonstrating genuine interest beyond the classroom. Maintaining balance is equally important. The scholars say academic ambition need not come at the expense of friendships, community involvement or personal wellbeing. Co-curricular activities can build confidence, social skills and networks while helping students discover interests they may eventually pursue professionally. WHAT DO THEY SAY Dilpreet’s message to other students is simple: “You are more capable than you think. Believe in yourself.” Gurmansimran stresses the lasting value of education, while Priety encourages students moving away from home to remain independent but grounded and positive. Satishver advises youngsters not to allow setbacks to define their journey: “It is never too late to turn the page, rewrite the plot or begin a new chapter.” Collectively, the four encourage students to look seriously at scholarship opportunities after SPM. Major scholarship programmes available to Malaysian students include those offered by JPA, PETRONAS, Bank Negara Malaysia, Yayasan Khazanah, Yayasan Tenaga Nasional, Yayasan Telekom Malaysia, Yayasan Sime Darby, Shell Malaysia, Yayasan UEM, CIMB ASEAN and Yayasan Gamuda. Application periods, eligibility requirements and funding terms vary, so students should regularly check the respective organisations’ official scholarship pages. Their common message to younger students is to aim high, ask questions, seek opportunities and apply — even when a scholarship appears highly competitive. “We hope to see more Sikh students pursuing their ambitions on a global stage,” they said. title: 'Oct 23 ruling on bid to restrain RHB from closing Maritime Network's accounts
body: 'Oct 23 ruling on bid to restrain RHB from closing Maritime Network's accounts KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 24): The High Court here on Thursday fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company's bid to restrain RHB Bank Bhd (LK:RHBBANK) from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit. Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank's counsel, Gan Khong Aik. Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts. He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care. Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer is that of debtor and creditor. In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company's application for a full injunction. According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005. On Oct 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated Oct 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines. The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines were allegedly breached. The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025. The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application. The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its minimum due diligence guidelines governing foreign-exchange transactions to the company within 45 days. Maritime Network further alleged that the bank's vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself. This conduct, the company asserted, amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights. It also claimed that the bank's conduct demonstrated an intention to oppress rather than protect its legitimate banking interests. Uploaded by Tham Yek Lee The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'Pelabur asing jual RM799.9 juta ekuiti Bursa Malaysia untuk minggu kedua - MBSB Research - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt – Pelabur asing terus mengurangkan pegangan dalam pasaran saham Malaysia apabila mencatatkan jualan bersih RM799.9 juta bagi minggu berakhir 2 Oktober 2026, menurut MBSB Research. Jualan bersih itu menjadikan aliran keluar dana asing di Bursa Malaysia berterusan untuk minggu kedua berturut-turut dengan pelabur asing menjadi penjual bersih pada kesemua lima hari dagangan sepanjang minggu berkenaan. “Jualan paling tinggi direkodkan pada Rabu sebanyak RM228.4 juta, diikuti Khamis RM187.9 juta, Selasa RM172.4 juta, Isnin RM142.1 juta dan Jumaat RM69.1 juta,” kata MBSB Research dalam nota kajiannya. Pelabur tempatan ambil peluang Berbeza dengan pelabur asing, institusi tempatan meneruskan trend pembelian bersih untuk minggu kedua berturut-turut dengan aliran masuk RM352.4 juta. Pelabur runcit pula meneruskan pembelian bersih bagi minggu keenam berturut-turut dengan jumlah aliran masuk sebanyak RM447.5 juta. Ini menunjukkan tekanan jualan daripada pelabur asing sebahagiannya diimbangi oleh penyertaan pelabur tempatan. Dari segi aktiviti dagangan, purata dagangan harian pelabur runcit meningkat 3.7%, manakala institusi tempatan susut 7.9%. Penyertaan pelabur asing pula meningkat 8.6%. Sektor teknologi, tenaga jadi pilihan pelabur asing Walaupun pelabur asing secara keseluruhan mencatatkan jualan bersih, terdapat beberapa sektor yang masih menerima aliran masuk dana. Sektor teknologi menerima aliran masuk asing tertinggi sebanyak RM131 juta, diikuti sektor tenaga sebanyak RM93.2 juta dan pembinaan sebanyak RM78.4 juta. Sebaliknya, sektor perkhidmatan kewangan mencatatkan aliran keluar asing terbesar sebanyak RM460.6 juta, diikuti utiliti RM339.8 juta dan penjagaan kesihatan RM163.1 juta. Dari sudut saham pula, antara kaunter yang menerima aliran masuk bersih asing tertinggi ialah Gamuda sebanyak RM86.2 juta, Solarvest Holdings RM65.4 juta, Westports Holdings RM55.1 juta dan Southern Cable Group RM53.4 juta. Dalam tempoh sama, Tenaga Nasional Berhad mencatatkan aliran keluar asing terbesar sebanyak RM278.1 juta, diikuti Malayan Banking RM159.3 juta dan RHB Bank RM135.9 juta. September turut menyaksikan jualan pelabur asing Trend tersebut turut dapat dilihat sepanjang September apabila pelabur asing menjual bersih saham Malaysia sebanyak RM1.69 bilion. Dalam tempoh sama, institusi tempatan mencatatkan pembelian bersih RM205.7 juta, manakala pelabur runcit membeli bersih RM1.48 bilion. Bagi September, sektor perladangan menjadi penerima aliran masuk asing terbesar sebanyak RM290.6 juta, diikuti tenaga RM230.2 juta serta pengangkutan dan logistik RM204.4 juta. Sebaliknya, sektor perkhidmatan kewangan merekodkan aliran keluar terbesar sebanyak RM1.48 bilion, diikuti utiliti RM642.2 juta dan produk serta perkhidmatan perindustrian RM310.8 juta. Aliran dana Asia kembali negatif Trend jualan asing di Malaysia berlaku ketika pelabur asing secara keseluruhan kembali mengeluarkan dana dari pasaran saham Asia. MBSB Research berkata, kesemua lapan pasaran Asia yang dipantau mencatatkan aliran keluar asing pada minggu berkenaan dengan jumlah keseluruhan AS$10.89 bilion, selepas mencatatkan pembelian bersih pada minggu sebelumnya. Korea Selatan merekodkan aliran keluar terbesar sebanyak AS$6.20 bilion, diikuti India AS$2.91 bilion dan Thailand AS$796.4 juta. Ekonomi Malaysia turut beri isyarat bercampur Dalam perkembangan ekonomi domestik, Indeks Pengurus Pembelian sektor pembuatan Malaysia susut kepada 49.9 pada September daripada 50.2 pada Ogos, menunjukkan kemerosotan keadaan operasi buat kali pertama sejak Mei 2026. MBSB Research berkata tempahan baharu merosot buat kali pertama dalam tempoh empat bulan, manakala pertumbuhan pengeluaran perlahan ke paras terendah dalam tempoh tujuh bulan. Keyakinan perniagaan turut jatuh ke paras terendah dalam tempoh lima bulan. Pada masa sama, inflasi harga pengeluar Malaysia meningkat 10.7% tahun ke tahun pada Ogos, iaitu peningkatan bagi bulan keenam berturut-turut dan kadar tertinggi sejak Jun 2022. Pasaran global kekal berhati-hati Di Amerika Syarikat, pertumbuhan pekerjaan yang lebih perlahan serta kadar inflasi yang masih melebihi sasaran menimbulkan ketidakpastian terhadap hala tuju dasar monetari negara itu. Dalam tempoh sama, dolar Amerika Syarikat meningkat 0.3% berbanding ringgit kepada RM4.0842, manakala harga minyak mentah Brent turun 2% kepada AS$102.25 setong dan minyak sawit mentah susut 2.9% kepada RM4,535 setan. Weekly Fund Flow-Week Ended 2 O… Secara keseluruhan, laporan MBSB Research menunjukkan Bursa Malaysia masih berdepan tekanan daripada pengeluaran dana asing, namun aktiviti pembelian oleh pelabur tempatan dan runcit membantu mengimbangi sebahagian tekanan tersebut ketika sentimen pelabur serantau turut dipengaruhi oleh perkembangan ekonomi global dan petunjuk ekonomi domestik yang bercampur. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Three Banks Lose Buy Ratings as Bond Yields Rise; Hong Leong Names PBBANK Its 4Q Top Pick
body: 'Hong Leong Investment Bank analyst Raymond Ng Ing Yeow downgraded AMMB Holdings, CIMB Group Holdings and RHB Bank to “Hold” from “Buy” in a banking-sector review. He cut their target prices to RM6.70 from RM7.80, RM8.10 from RM8.70 and RM8.00 from RM9.50, respectively. In contrast, he upgraded Public Bank to “Buy” from “Hold” and raised its target price to RM5.30 from RM4.90, naming it his top banking pick for 4Q26. Raymond Ng Ing Yeow is ranked No.10 among 17 financial services analysts on StockTipRatings, based on data since 2023. He holds a 66% expert rating, with a 7% average return and a 56% success rate across stocks he covered over the one-year period following his calls. The changes come as the yield on 10-year Malaysian Government Securities rose to 3.94% on September 25 from 3.60% at end-June. Higher yields reduce the market value of bonds already held by banks, potentially weighing on treasury-related non-interest income before the benefit of reinvesting at higher yields emerges. Raymond said the immediate impact appears manageable, but repeated increases in yields could make earnings less predictable and limit further gains in bank valuations. Under his hypothetical 30-basis-point yield-rise scenario, the estimated gross mark-to-market impact for AMMB Holdings and Bank Islam Malaysia is equivalent to about 10% of their projected annual non-interest income, compared with 4.5% for CIMB Group Holdings and 3.2% for RHB Bank. Public Bank’s direct earnings sensitivity is lower at 1.3%. These are pre-tax estimates that exclude hedging and other offsets—not cuts to earnings forecasts. Raymond said the three downgrades reflect weaker visibility over non-interest income and a higher hurdle for bank-share valuations to rise further. He favours Public Bank for its exceptionally low impaired-loan ratio, resilient earnings and relatively limited direct earnings exposure to the bond-market sell-off, although its bond holdings could still affect book value. He maintained a “Neutral” sector view, noting that foreign investors sold a net RM1.3 billion of Malaysian banking shares between July 1 and September 25, while higher bond yields have made fixed-income investments more competitive. As of 2:09 p.m. on September 29, the Bursa Malaysia Financial Services index dropped 1% to 19,394.6 points. title: 'RHB Could Face Earnings Pressure From Elevated Bond Yields
body: 'Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) has maintained its HOLD call on RHB Bank Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM8.00, saying the lender’s earnings outlook remains broadly stable despite pressure on non-interest income from the recent spike in Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields.  Following a recent meeting with RHB Bank’s management, HLIB said weaker trading income is likely to weigh on 3Q26 non-interest income (NOII), with limited time left in the quarter for market conditions to recover.  However, the research house said the impact should be viewed mainly as foregone trading upside rather than significant trading losses, given RHB’s relatively small trading book.  Management has also been tactically reducing securities exposure and crystallising gains where possible. HLIB said the outlook for 4Q26 is less negative, as RHB would have more time to reposition its portfolio should bond yields stabilise or decline.  Despite the NOII headwinds, RHB has retained its 10.8% to 11.0% return on equity target, although HLIB believes the group is now more likely to achieve the lower end of that range.  With securities trading becoming a less dependable earnings driver, greater reliance will fall on core operations.  Loan growth remains on track at around 6%, while management has reset cost growth guidance to 1% or below, potentially supporting better operating leverage.  Credit costs are also tracking near the lower end of RHB’s 13 to 14 basis point guidance, with management comfortable at around 13bps and seeing potential for around 12bps if recoveries materialise.  Other fee-based businesses are showing stronger momentum. Wealth sales increased 35% year-on-year as at June 2026, while bancassurance and takaful, brokerage, investment banking and loan-related fees have continued to improve.  HLIB said these areas should partially cushion the weaker trading contribution, although elevated bond yields have made the upper end of the ROE target more difficult to achieve.  HLIB said RHB’s asset quality outlook remains manageable, with management seeing no significant corporate credit concerns at present.  Gross impaired loan formation continues to come mainly from the SME and community banking segments, but the deterioration has been gradual rather than broad-based.  Potential recoveries could emerge from the corporate, commercial and Singapore portfolios, although management is not assuming substantial write-backs.  RHB is also maintaining underwriting discipline, remaining selective in mortgages and SME lending and avoiding aggressive pricing where risk-adjusted returns are unattractive.  Deposit competition remains manageable, while initiatives such as RHB Pay are aimed at capturing operating balances and structurally improving current and savings account deposits and funding costs.  HLIB said capital management remains one of RHB’s more important medium-term catalysts, with the bank targeting greater clarity on its capital and dividend policy by 1Q27.  A roughly 100-basis-point uplift in the CET1 ratio, equivalent to around RM2 billion, could potentially emerge following Basel III reforms in January 2028.  Management’s priority, however, remains ensuring that normal operations and targeted growth can be adequately funded while maintaining CET1 around current levels.  Any excess capital could potentially be returned to shareholders if future growth requirements do not absorb the surplus.  The stock currently offers a projected FY27 dividend yield of more than 6.5%, while a possible normalisation in the Overnight Policy Rate from 2.75% to 3.00% in 2027 could provide another earnings lever.  HLIB maintained its RM8.00 target price, based on an implied 1.0 times CY2027 price-to-book multiple, saying current valuations already reflect most near-term positives and that stronger catalysts are needed before it adopts a more constructive stance.

title: '马股闭市微升1.60点  顶级手套飙11.46% - 财经 - 即时财经
body: '马股闭市微升1.60点 顶级手套飙11.46% （吉隆坡6日讯）中东石油出口增加，促使国际油价回落，带动区域股市普遍上涨，马股周二盘中曾升至1641.20点，上升9.45点，可惜午盘之后回吐部分涨幅，最终只升1.60点，以1633.35点挂收。 反映大盘走势的富时全股指数上扬42.52点，至12232.87点，创业板指数也起52.31点，至5658.92点。  其他马股各大指数普遍上涨，当中科技和医疗保健指数涨势凌厉，全日猛涨超过3%，金融服务、产业和交通物流指数下跌介于0.08%至0.38%。 全场股项涨多跌少，有667只上升股，超过456只下跌股，另有551只平盘。全场有41亿7664万1900股，总值29亿4950万1489令吉。 综指成分股方面，上升、下跌和平盘各报14只、14只和2只。 上涨的综指股包括国油化学（PCHEM,5183,主板工业产品服务组）起17仙，至4令吉30仙；IHH医保（IHH,5225,主板医疗保健组)涨15仙，收于7令吉91仙；森牙直利（SDG,5285,主板种植组)升10仙，至6令吉12仙。 银行股表现逊色，大众银行（PBBANK,1295,主板金融服务组)下跌4仙，收报4令吉67仙；马来亚银行（MAYBANK,1155,主板金融服务组)和联昌集团（CIMB,1023,主板金融服务组)各降3仙，分别跌至9令吉97仙和7令吉70仙。 顶级手套（TOPGLOV,7113,主板医疗保健组)第四季业绩亮眼，加上派发每股1.5仙终期股息，驱动股价午盘走势越战越勇，收盘上扬9仙或11.46%，至87.5仙，并以1亿6513万3800股的成交量，位居热门榜亚军。 近期跌跌不休的ZETRIX公司(ZETRIX,0138,主板科技组) 周二止跌回扬，闭市上涨2.5仙或38.46%，至9仙，成交量高达9亿6279万零400股，冲上热门榜榜首。 国际油价回落，以及美国科技股走稳，带动全球股市普遍上涨。 美国隔夜股市3大指数全面收高，收盘时，道琼斯工商指数起0.18%，标普500指数升0.66%，纳斯达克综指涨至历史新高，收盘上扬1.05%。 亚太股市大部分走高，印尼雅加达综指上涨1.21%，日本日经指数起1.05%，香港恒生指数上扬1.00%，台湾加权指数上升0.22%，新加坡海峡时报指数起0.40%，泰国曼谷综指升0.37%。 不过，菲律宾马尼拉综指和韩国首尔综指各跌1.15%和0.89%。中国股市今天休市。 马币方面，联储局升息的概率增加，带动美元指数走高，马币兑美元和新元双双下滑。 根据《彭博社》行情，马币兑美元全日游走于4.0848至4.0880之间，截至下午5时报4.0852，周一收于4.0845；马币兑新元全日在3.1915至3.1968之间徘徊，截至下午5时收报3.1951，低于周一的3.1941。 棕油需求增加，带动大马衍生产品交易所12月指标期货上扬4令吉，至每公吨4582令吉。  热门新闻 百格视频

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Kembali Menghijau, Saham Wajaran Tinggi Jadi Tumpuan
body: 'Bursa Malaysia meneruskan kenaikan pada tengah hari Jumaat, dengan indeks utama disokong oleh aktiviti belian ketika harga rendah dalam beberapa saham wajaran tinggi terpilih. Pada jam 12.30 tengah hari, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 5.44 mata kepada 1,635.80, berbanding paras penutupan 1,630.36 pada Khamis. Indeks dibuka 3.51 mata lebih tinggi pada 1,633.87 dan bergerak dalam julat 1,630.63 hingga 1,640.78 sepanjang sesi dagangan pagi. Saham Wajaran Tinggi Sokong Kenaikan Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Tenaga Nasional meningkat 16 sen kepada RM13.06, Maybank menambah sembilan sen kepada RM10.04, Public Bank naik empat sen kepada RM4.71 dan IHH Healthcare menokok 11 sen kepada RM7.81. CIMB pula susut satu sen kepada RM7.68. Kenaikan saham-saham terpilih ini membantu menyokong FBM KLCI walaupun tekanan jualan masih kelihatan dalam pasaran secara keseluruhan. Kaunter Rugi Masih Mengatasi Kaunter Untung Sentimen pasaran lebih luas kekal bercampur apabila kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung sebanyak 507 berbanding 499. Sebanyak 494 kaunter tidak berubah, manakala 1,273 tidak diniagakan dan 24 lagi digantung dagangan. Jumlah dagangan mencecah 2.24 bilion saham bernilai RM1.26 bilion setakat tengah hari. JCY International Antara Kaunter Aktif Dalam dagangan aktif, JCY International meningkat 20 sen kepada 65.5 sen, V.S Industry menambah dua sen kepada 29 sen, Jaks Resources naik setengah sen kepada 18.5 sen dan Top Glove menokok 3.5 sen kepada 77 sen. Zetrix AI pula susut 2.5 sen kepada 14 sen. Malaysian Pacific Industries mencatat kenaikan terbesar dalam kalangan kaunter untung yang disenaraikan, meningkat 84 sen kepada RM41.96. UWC dan United Plantations masing-masing naik 36 sen kepada RM7.46 dan RM31.32, manakala Vitrox serta UMS Integration menambah 34 sen setiap satu kepada RM10.34 dan RM8.99. Sebaliknya, Kuala Lumpur Kepong susut 46 sen kepada RM20.96, diikuti Enra yang merosot 29 sen kepada 69 sen dan Allianz Malaysia yang turun 28 sen kepada RM20.72. Kebanyakan Indeks Sektor Mencatat Kenaikan Di papan indeks, FBM Mid 70 meningkat 115.75 mata kepada 17,474.73, manakala FBM Emas menambah 51.08 mata kepada 12,194.61. FBM Top 100 pula naik 50.09 mata kepada 11,983.24. FBM Emas Shariah meningkat 66.45 mata kepada 12,079.46, sementara FBM ACE menambah 6.33 mata kepada 5,489.30. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan meningkat 55.60 mata kepada 19,116.51, Indeks Tenaga naik 10.6 mata kepada 836.07 dan Indeks Perladangan menambah 4.58 mata kepada 9,031.15. Indeks Produk Perindustrian dan Perkhidmatan pula meningkat 0.99 mata kepada 178.72. Hasil Bon Tinggi Hadkan Sentimen Pasaran Hong Leong Investment Bank menjangkakan FBM KLCI meneruskan fasa pengukuhan ketika pelabur mengurangkan risiko susulan kenaikan harga minyak dan hasil bon. Aliran keluar dana asing yang berterusan, ketegangan Amerika Syarikat-Iran serta pendirian Rizab Persekutuan (Fed) yang cenderung mengekalkan kadar faedah tinggi turut menjadi faktor yang mempengaruhi sentimen pelabur. Dari sudut teknikal, bank pelaburan itu mengenal pasti zon rintangan terdekat pada 1,667 hingga 1,682 mata, diikuti kelompok purata bergerak pada 1,705 hingga 1,720 mata. – Bernama HUSTLE24HOUR kini dibuka! title: 'Maybank Kini Perkenal Saving+, Bolehkan Pengguna Melabur Serendah RM10 – Menerusi MAE
body:
'

Bagi memastikan pengguna dapat menjana potensi pulangan daripada lebihan tunai tanpa perlu menggunakan platform atau aplikasi pelaburan lain – Maybank kini perkenalkan Saving+ pada aplikasi MAE yang membolehkan pengguna melabur serendah RM10. 

Menariknya menerusi ciri Saving+ ini pengguna boleh melabur dalam dana pasaran wang patuh syariah yang diuruskan oleh Maybank Asset Management. Berdasarkan pengenalan itu, tawaran potensi pulangan dilaraskan sehingga 3.32% setahun.

Di bawah ciri ini juga dijelaskan tiada tempoh penguncian dikenakan bagi tindakan pelaburan dan pengeluaran dapat diproses dalam tempoh purata 2 hari bekerja.

Namun seperti kebanyakkan pelaburan, potensi pulangan kekal tidak dijamin dan tertakluk kepada persekitaran pasaran serta prestasi dana. Dengan pengenalan ciri tersebut, ia sekali gus melengkapkan kitaran MAE – tidak hanya membolehkan pengguna miliki akaun, laksana simpanan tetapi turut merancakkan lagi segmen pelaburan pada pasaran semasa.

title: 'Maybank perkukuh pendidikan digital di SMK Santubong
body: 'KUCHING, 17 Sept: Keperluan pembelajaran yang seiring dengan perkembangan teknologi mendorong Maybank Wilayah Sarawak memperkasa kemudahan digital di Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Santubong menerusi sumbangan empat unit televisyen (TV) pintar.  Pengarah Wilayah Maybank Sarawak, Abang Jamili Abang Julai berkata, sumbangan itu merupakan sebahagian daripada inisiatif Program Cahaya Kasih Maybank yang dilaksanakan bagi tempoh dua tahun khususnya bagi membantu sekolah menangani kekangan kemudahan teknologi dan komunikasi.  Menurutnya, perubahan dalam sistem pendidikan dan perkembangan teknologi memerlukan semua pihak menyesuaikan diri dengan keadaan semasa bagi memastikan pelajar mendapat pengalaman pembelajaran yang bersesuaian dengan keperluan masa kini.  “Kita akan berusaha untuk bersama membantu anak-anak, lebih-lebih lagi tentang pembelajaran ataupun pendidikan.  “Zaman dah berubah, zaman bukan seperti zaman saya sekolah dulu ataupun zaman Yang Berhormat (Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri) pergi sekolah dulu. Jadi kita kena menyesuaikan diri dalam keadaan semasa,” katanya.  Beliau berkata demikian ketika berucap pada program Maybank Global Corporate Responsibility (CR) Day 2026 dan Program Cahaya Kasih Challenge 2026-2027 di SMK Santubong, hari ini.  Abang Jamili menjelaskan, penyediaan kemudahan digital itu diharap dapat meningkatkan pengalaman pembelajaran pelajar, selain memberi peluang kepada mereka memanfaatkan teknologi dalam proses pendidikan.  Menurutnya, transformasi digital merupakan satu keperluan yang tidak dapat dielakkan memandangkan ekonomi dan kehidupan masyarakat kini semakin bergantung kepada teknologi.  Tambahnya, sumbangan empat unit TV pintar itu turut mencerminkan komitmen Maybank untuk memberikan impak positif kepada masyarakat melalui inisiatif tanggungjawab korporat.  “Program Cahaya Kasih bukan sekadar program kesukarelawanan, malah melibatkan perkongsian masa, tenaga dan kepakaran warga Maybank bagi membantu memenuhi keperluan sebenar komuniti,” ujarnya.  Antara perkongsian yang diberikan kepada warga sekolah termasuk pengetahuan berkaitan teknologi serta platform digital Maybank yang dapat memberi pendedahan kepada pelajar mengenai perkembangan dunia digital.  Dalam pada itu, Abang Jamili berharap lebih banyak pihak korporat tampil membantu sekolah berkenaan dalam memperkukuh kemudahan pendidikan dan teknologi.  “Saya harap ada juga pihak-pihak korporat yang lain mungkin sama-sama membantu sekolah ini juga,” jelasnya.  Beliau berkata, usaha itu selari dengan komitmen Maybank untuk memberikan impak positif kepada masyarakat menerusi pelbagai inisiatif di bawah strategi Road to POTI sehingga 2030.  Menurutnya, sebanyak 93 inisiatif dilaksanakan Maybank tahun ini bagi menyokong agenda berkenaan, dengan tumpuan antaranya kepada pemerkasaan komuniti, kesukarelawanan dan kelestarian.  Abang Jamili berkata, Maybank turut menyasarkan 150,000 jam kerja sukarelawan tahun ini di seluruh kumpulan, dengan pendekatan lebih besar kepada kesukarelawanan berasaskan kemahiran.-TVS

title: 'Nanta titip pesanan buat Syed Saddiq, Bella-‘Perkahwinan umpama jalan raya’
body: 'MENTERI Kerja Raya Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi berkongsikan pertemuannya dengan bakal pengantin Ahli Parlimen Muar, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman dan selebriti Bella Astillah.  Namun, apa yang lebih menarik nasihat dititipkan Nanta terhadap pasangan dua sejoli itu yang sedang menghitung hari untuk bergelar raja sehari.  Pesanan Nanta kepada pasangan berkenaan agak menarik apabila menyifatkan perkahwinan “seumpama jalan raya”.  “Bila berjumpa orang muda yang bakal melangkah ke alam perkahwinan, sempatlah saya kongsi sedikit pesanan.  “Saya kata, perkahwinan ni umpama jalan raya — mesti dua hala, tak boleh sehala. Kena saling memberi, saling menerima dan sama-sama bertolak ansur.  “Dalam rumah tangga, bukan soal siapa betul atau siapa menang. Yang penting, dua-dua kena tahu bila nak jalan, bila nak berhenti, dan kadang-kadang bila kena bagi laluan,” katanya dalam hantaran di Facebooknya.  Nanta turut mendoakan agar segala urusan Syed Saddiq dan Bella dipermudahkan dan semoga perjalanan yang bakal ditempuh bersama nanti sentiasa diberkati dan dipenuhi kebahagiaan.  Syed Saddiq dan Bella dijadualkan akan melangsungkan akad nikah pada 10 Oktober ini di aras 118, Menara Merdeka Maybank, Kuala Lumpur.- MalaysiaPost

title: 'Banking Sector - FBM KLCI 50: Lower Bank Weight, Limited Passive Impact
body: 'The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) will expand from 30 to 50 constituents in December, reflecting the significant growth in Bursa Malaysia's market capitalisation and the broader depth of its listed universe. While the FBM KLCI remains the country's flagship equity benchmark, its current 30 constituents represent only about 60% of the market's total capitalisation, below the approximately 70% coverage typically achieved by major global large-cap indices. The expansion aims to provide a broader representation of the Malaysian equity market while enhancing sector diversification through greater exposure to Technology, Energy and Industrials. To facilitate a smooth transition and minimise potential market disruption, the 20 additional constituents will be introduced in two stages. In the first phase, effective 21 December 2026, the new entrants will be included at 50% of their eventual index weights. The selection cut-off date will be 23 November 2026, with the final list of constituents announced on 3 December 2026. The second phase, effective 21 June 2027, will increase these constituents to their full index weights, completing the transition. Concurrently, the FBM Mid 70 Index will be streamlined to 50 constituents and rebranded as the FBM Mid Cap Index, while the overall FBM Top 100 Index universe remains unchanged at 100 stocks. The expansion is expected to create a more diversified and less concentrated benchmark. Based on market data as at 30 June 2026, the weight of the largest constituent is projected to decline from 13.2% to approximately 11.1% upon completion of Phase 2. Similarly, the combined weighting of the top five constituents is expected to fall from 50.0% to 42.1%, while the top 10 stocks will account for 57.2% of the index versus 67.9% under the current composition. The expanded FBM KLCI will also better represent non-financial sectors. Technology stocks will enter the benchmark for the first time, with an estimated 2.4% weighting upon full implementation. Industrials is expected to increase from 6.2% to 9.1%, Consumer Discretionary from 0.9% to 2.9%, Real Estate from 3.1% to 4.0%, and Energy from 1.0% to 2.0%. For the banking sector, the key implication is a structural dilution in index representation rather than a change in fundamentals. Financials' weighting is expected to decline from 42.7% currently to 39.4% in Phase 1 and 36.6% after Phase 2 is completed. In contrast, financial stocks will be more represented in the revamped FBM Mid Cap Index, with the sector's weighting projected to increase from 8.8% to 14.3%. In this report, we assess the implications of the FBM KLCI expansion for financial stocks and the broader banking sector. The reduction in Financials' index weight could result in passive selling of existing banking constituents. However, we believe the actual flow impact should remain modest given the relatively small pool of assets tracking the FBM KLCI. Based on our estimate of approximately RM3.0bn in KLCI-tracking passive assets under management (AUM), we estimate gross passive selling of around RM202mn across the six existing banking constituents, partly offset by around RM22mn of potential passive buying into Alliance Bank if it is included in the expanded benchmark. This would result in net estimated passive outflows of approximately RM180mn from the seven affected banking stocks. Importantly, the estimated RM180mn net outflow represents only around 0.06% of the combined free-float market capitalisation of approximately RM280bn across the seven affected banks. This suggests that the headline reduction in the Financials weighting is unlikely to translate into material selling pressure on banking stocks. Rather, we view the rebalancing primarily as a potential source of temporary stock-specific volatility and portfolio repositioning around the implementation dates. The relatively modest flow impact is also supported by the phased implementation. Assuming the RM3.0bn passive AUM and underlying index weights remain unchanged, approximately half of the estimated flow would occur during Phase 1 in December 2026, with the remaining adjustment taking place when the new constituents reach their full weights in June 2027. This should reduce the immediate impact of the rebalancing on banking stocks. While we estimate KLCI-tracking passive AUM at approximately RM3.0bn, the actual pool could differ depending on how much is benchmarked to the index. To assess the sensitivity of our conclusion, we estimate the potential net banking-sector outflows under different passive AUM assumptions Even under a higher RM5.0bn passive-AUM assumption, estimated net selling would amount to approximately RM300mn, equivalent to only around 0.1% of the combined free-float market capitalisation of the affected banks. As such, we believe the conclusion that the index expansion represents a relatively modest direct flow event remains intact across a reasonable range of passive-AUM assumptions. Alliance Bank has been identified as one of the 20 indicative candidates for inclusion in the expanded FBM KLCI. If selected, we estimate that the bank could receive approximately RM21.8mn of incremental passive demand based on its potential 0.73% increase in index weighting and our RM3.0bn passive-AUM assumption. body: 'The local market drifted lower on Wednesday, weighed down by profit-taking among selected index heavyweights, with declines led by the transportation and banking sectors. The FBM KLCI shed 7.07 points to end at 1,676.43, off an early high of 1,685.37 and low of 1,675.15, as losers narrowly beat gainers 549 to 519, on lower turnover of 3.2bn shares worth RM2.99bn. The local benchmark index is expected to remain rangebound as investors await clearer policy signals from the ongoing U.S.-China talks, while the lack of meaningful domestic catalysts is likely to keep market direction subdued. Immediate resistance for the index remains at the June 2026 high (1,722), followed by tougher upside hurdles at the 123.6%FP (1,759) and 138.2%FP (1,805) ahead. Meanwhile, immediate support is maintained at the June 2026 low (1,655), with stronger support coming from the 76.4%FR (1,610) and 61.8%FR (1,564). CIMB need to reinforce support above the 61.8%FR (RM7.43) to enhance recovery potential to the 27/01/26 peak (RM8.50), with next upside hurdles at the 123.6%FP (RM9.17) and 138.2%FP (RM9.58) ahead, while stronger retracement support is found at the 50%FR (RM7.10). Meantime, RHB Bank is attractive to bargain for oversold rebound towards the 50- day ma (RM8.28), with a convincing breakout above the 10/08/26 high (RM8.77) to target the 123.6%FP (RM9.14). Crucial support comes from the 61.8%FR (RM7.36) and 50%FR (RM7.02). Asian markets traded mixed on Wednesday, as regional sentiment remained subdued while investors monitored ongoing geopolitical developments ahead of key U.S.-China talks. Oil prices extended their decline as traders weighed comments from President Donald Trump saying that U.S. officials had a “very good” meeting with an Iranian delegation on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, although he also threatened to “annihilate” the country if a deal was not reached. Investors also awaited further direction from the upcoming meeting between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, with market participants watching for a possible extension of the trade truce and potential cooperation on AI between the two countries. Nevertheless, AI-linked stocks in the region extended their winning streak underpinned by renewed optimism over chip demand, amid strong consumer take up of Meta's new AI agent. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 edged higher 0.09% to 8,765.30, while South Korea’s Kospi gained 0.90% to 7,080.92. In the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index fell 0.39% to 3,936.52, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index slumped 1.01% to 24,834.12. Markets in Japan were closed for a public holiday. Wall Street’s major indexes ended lower overnight as a spike in Treasury yields revived inflation concerns, while investors tracked U.S. diplomatic developments involving Iran and China. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.68% to 51,511.59. The S&P 500 slipped 0.75% to 7,706.03, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.13% to 26,936.03. The 10-year Treasury yield surged past 5.11%, reaching its highest level since 2007, as rising oil prices and stronger- than-expected U.S. business activity fueled inflation concerns. Oil prices also moved higher following Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s address to the UN, a day after U.S. President Donald Trump warned that he could “annihilate” Iran. The shift in market expectations raised the likelihood of another Federal Reserve rate hike this year, following comments from Governor Michael Barr that “further policy adjustments” would be necessary to push inflation lower. Separately, President Trump is expected to receive Chinese President Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews, marking Xi’s first visit to Washington, D.C., in more than a decade. The leaders are expected to discuss extending last year’s trade truce, along with AI regulation and U.S. weapons sales to Taiwan. title: 'TNB share price up on Kenyir project's outlook
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd's share price rose in early trading on Friday with its Kenyir Hydrogen Hybrid Fuel System (HHFS) project expected to generate a high single-digit equity internal rate of return. As at 9.57 am, TNB's share price rose eight sen to RM12.98 with 889,300 shares traded. According to MBSB Investment Bank (MBSB IB), electricity demand is also expected to remain strong, with growth projected at 5.4 per cent in calendar year 2026. "We continue to view TNB as a key beneficiary and enabler of Malaysia's energy transition, supported by rising regulated grid capex, growing battery energy storage system requirements and sizeable renewable energy opportunities through initiatives such as HHFS. As such, MBSB IB has maintained its "Buy" recommendation on TNB, with an unchanged discounted cash flow (DCF)-derived target price of RM16.31. CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd has also maintained its "Buy" recommendation, with an unchanged DCF-based target price of RM15.90.

title: 'The Legacy of Great Towers
body: 'Passport to Nature, Heritage and Culture After five hectic days of talking about towers, visitor experiences and the future of some of the world’s most iconic landmarks, what does a tower person do to chill out? Climb another tower? Get close to nature? Or immerse themselves in a different culture? For the delegates of the World Federation of Great Towers (WFGT) Conference, which ended at the Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur on Sept 18, the answer was — all three. But not necessarily in that order. First, they went looking for elephants About 20 WFGT delegates, accompanied by their Malaysian hosts, left Kuala Lumpur after the five-day conference for a post-conference journey into Pahang. Their first stop was the National Elephant Conservation Centre (NECC), Kuala Gandah. And suddenly, the language of towers gave way to the language of nature. There were no observation decks, city skylines or glass elevators. Instead, there was jungle, water and the unmistakable presence of elephants. About a dozen delegates ventured down to the river and had a splashing great time bathing with a young elephant. Some got wet. Some got wetter. And almost everyone came away with a broad smile. The delegates were also given a video presentation, briefing and tour of the centre by Perhilitan personnel, gaining a closer understanding of Malaysia’s elephant conservation efforts. NECC head Muhammad Fadlli bin Ab Yazi and also his team also played a video of Perhilitan's conservation, research and elephant translocation efforts. It was perhaps the moment when everyone truly let their hair down after five intensive days of conference sessions. Kuala Lumpur Tower CEO Khairil Faizal came all the way to join in the fun Even Jean-Yves Ghazi, executive director of the World Federation of Great Towers, joined in the experience. At one point, he fed sugar cane to an elephant — with his back facing the animal. It was one of those moments that could never be fully captured in a conference room. It had to be experienced. Video 1: CELEBRATION OF CULTURE: WFGT delegates even joined the performers for joget as they sampled warm Malaysian hospitality at the Garden Terrace of Kuantan 188. Hyperlink: https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/g1smui/AGtS8XXEWhOeZpLwpOS3WbW-9FciXuJn0GGimgXVPIt8-0eoVSV1r7YO7nd7=s294-w294-h294-k-p-v1-no Pahang for nature, culture and hospitality If the elephants had provided the delegates with a taste of Malaysia’s natural side, Pahang and Kuantan 188 delivered culture and warm Malaysian hospitality. At the Sky Terrace overlooking the Kuantan River, the evening turned into a garden party. The delegates were treated to cultural performances by Anak Kayan Pahang, with performers spanning three generations. The delegates joined the performers for a joget, turning the evening into an informal celebration of friendship and Malaysian hospitality. Before that, there was singing at the restaurant deck where dinner was hosted. After some urging, Dato Zulkifli Mohamad — WFGT member and managing director of Kuantan 188 — took to the floor and sang the Bee Gees classic To Love Somebody. The irrepressible Dato “One More” Zul Zulkifli soon called on Randy Stancik, general manager of Willis Tower Skydeck in Chicago, to join him on stage with the emcee. And no one wore a broader smile than Zul when everything turned out splendidly well. He had stitched the evening together — including lobbying the WFGT to host the conference in Kuala Lumpur. The WFGT duly presented an Appreciation Award to him with these fondly crafted words: “To Dato ‘One More’ Zul for being Dato Zul” — with love from Your Distinguished Guest. Zul, being his warm and jovial self, joked: “Now, please tell me, how do I say ‘one more’ to my wife?” And everyone erupted in laughter. The Dato Bandar Kuantan Dato Zaliza bin Zulkipli and members of Majlis Bandaraya Kuantan, Tourism Pahang and MOTAC Pahang also turned up to support this event and extend their hospitality. The trio who made the climb As for climbing, Miguel Amerlink and Mariana Ferruzca of Torre Latino México, together with Daniel Cecetka of UFO Bratislava in Slovakia, made it a point to scale the antenna of Kuantan 188. Not by lift. Not by stairs. But with ropes and safety harnesses, with the help of climbing guides. For people whose professional lives revolve around great towers, perhaps this was the ultimate way to start the morning. Three tower people, looking down from above, before the rest of the group headed on to the next destination. It was another reminder that a tower can be experienced in more ways than simply looking out from its observation deck. Visiting the historic royal town of Pekan From Kuantan, the delegates continued to Pekan, the historic royal town, where they were introduced to history, craftsmanship, music and royal tradition. At Perkampungan Kraf Diraja Tunku Azizah, they watched a weaving demonstration at Pusat Tenun Che Minah Sayang. They also visited the birthplace of Malaysia’s second prime minister, Tun Abdul Razak, the Pahang Silk Weaving Centre, Karyaneka Centre and Serambi House Pahang. Then came the music. A gamelan performance filled the space with the calming and distinctive sounds of traditional Pahang music. Caryn Stancik from the United States, who tried her hand at playing the gamelan, said: “It’s like a cultural awakening. I just love the music. It feels so nice and relaxing like the rustling of wind chimes. “When I go back to the US, I will definitely look out for gamelan music CDs to explore it further.” That is perhaps what a meaningful travel experience does. It leaves you curious enough to continue the journey after you have gone home. A sumptuous lunch beside the river at Gerabak Jaman Tory completed the Pekan experience before the delegates began their journey back to Kuala Lumpur. Trinidad Hospitality Group CEO Dato Sri Naresh Mohan and YB Leong Yu Man, Pahang Exco for Unity, Tourism and Culture took time off to greet and host the delegates. Building a towering experience for visitors In his closing remarks, Zul said he hoped that the staging of the WFGT conference in Kuala Lumpur would leave something meaningful behind. “Every tower has its unique offering,” said Zul, who had also thoughtfully arranged a WFGT visit to Menara Merdeka Maybank. “Each tower not only offers its unique view of the city but also connects to people, landscape, businesses, surroundings and nature in different ways.” A visitor could climb a tower, discover nature, cruise a river, experience local food, listen to traditional music or explore heritage and culture — thus creating a much richer journey around the country’s towers. In many ways, the WFGT delegates had already experienced the concept before they left for home. At the opening of the WFGT conference, Ghazi had reminded delegates: “Our responsibility is not simply to operate great towers.” “It is to ensure that these extraordinary places continue to inspire, educate, connect and create memorable experiences for generations to come.” That was precisely what had happened during their journey to Malaysia. The towers had not been left behind after all. They had simply become gateways to something much bigger. Zul hopes that the proposed Malaysian Tower Passport can carry that idea forward as one of the meaningful outcomes of the WFGT conference in Kuala Lumpur, in line with the aspirations of Visit Malaysia 2026. Before they left for home, a bus full of WFGT delegates sang Rasa Sayang, urged on by award-winning guide Jasmine Leow, who incidentally holds both City and Nature guide badges. After five days of talking about towers, everyone had discovered that a great tower can be much more than a place to look at a city. It can be a gateway to the city, nature, its people, its heritage, its culture — and to experiences visitors remember long after they have gone home. The Euro STOXX 50 rose 0.2% to 6,332, while the STOXX Europe 600 gained 0.3% to 643.6. (The Edge) MY: Regulations on cross-border e-commerce platforms being finalised, says Teo The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is still in discussions with the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, the Finance Ministry and the Customs Department on the regulatory framework for cross-border e-commerce platforms. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the rules governing e-commerce platforms were being finalised, and MCMC, which is under her ministry, is the body that licensed such platforms. Speaking to reporters at the launch of the Asean-China Cross Border E-Commerce Expo 2026 (CBE 2026), she said MCMC was ready to proceed once it received directions from the two ministries. (The Edge) OIB: Applies to withdraw draft circular, listing application for RM280m related party deal to make 'essential updates' Property developer Oriental Interest Bhd has applied to withdraw its draft circular and listing application filed more than a month ago for its proposed RM280 million share‑based related party acquisition that would have marked its entry into the motorcycle financing and retail business. In a Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday, the company said it had submitted a letter to the regulator to withdraw the documents filed on Aug 18 to facilitate essential updates to the documents. (The Edge) MAYBULK: To expand into industrial property business with Klang land buy Transportation and logistics group Maybulk Bhd has proposed to buy a freehold industrial property in Bandar Bukit Raja, Klang for RM35.5 million cash. The property comprises 8,346 sq m of land together with a single-storey industrial building, an annexed office and a warehouse block, the group said in an exchange filing on Tuesday. (The Edge) MMAG: Proposes RM130 mil capital reduction to pare accumulated losses Loss-making MMAG Holdings Bhd, a company which counts NexG Bhd as a substantial shareholder, has proposed a RM130 million share capital reduction to wipe out part of the company’s accumulated losses. NexG is the company’s second largest shareholder with a 9.925% stake, while Future Star Sdn Bhd is its largest shareholder with a 19.904% interest. (The Edge) L&G: Targets RM1.5b GDV for first phase of Lembah Beringin industrial park Land & General Bhd plans to launch the first phase of its Lembah Beringin industrial park in Selangor in the first quarter of next year, with an estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM1.5 billion. The first phase of the project, which marks the property developer's expansion into the industrial segment, covers 240 acres of the group's 2,500-acre land bank in Lembah Beringin. (The Edge) GBBOND: Reports 8.22 times IPO oversubscription ahead of ACE Market debut GB Bond Holdings Bhd announced that its initial public offering (IPO) has been oversubscribed by 8.22 times, ahead of its planned listing on Bursa Malaysia’s ACE Market on Oct 1. In a bursa filing on Tuesday, the industrial adhesive maker said it received 5,333 applications from the Malaysian public for 190.02 million new shares, against 20.62 million shares offered. title: 'Bursa dibuka tinggi pada pagi ini
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR,. Bursa Malaysia dibuka tinggi pada Selasa, seiring dengan momentum positif Wall Street semalaman, memandangkan harga minyak yang terkawal susulan pemulihan eksport minyak mentah dari Asia Barat, mengimbangi trend penjualan berterusan dalam pasaran bon Perbendaharaan AS. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 7.14 mata atau 0.44 peratus kepada 1,638.89 berbanding paras 1,631.75 ketika ditutup pada Isnin. Indeks utama itu dibuka 4.63 mata lebih tinggi kepada 1,636.38. Sentimen pasaran secara keseluruhan positif dengan kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 272 berbanding 202, sebanyak 364 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,944 tidak diniagakan dan 13 digantung dagangan. Jumlah dagangan berjumlah 440.19 juta saham bernilai RM164.76 juta. Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd memaklumkan bahawa prestasi positif Wall Street semalaman menyaksikan Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 dan Nasdaq Composite masing-masing meningkat sebanyak 0.2 peratus, 0.7 peratus dan 1.1 peratus, manakala harga minyak mentah Brent dan hasil Perbendaharaan 10 tahun masing-masing mencecah US$100.3 setong dan 5.3 peratus. “Di peringkat tempatan, kami menjangkakan pelabur akan terus bersikap selektif menjelang pengumuman Belanjawan 2027, dengan tumpuan diberikan kepada sektor-sektor yang berpotensi mendapat manfaat. “Syarikat-syarikat dalam sektor mekanikal dan elektrikal mungkin terus menyaksikan minat belian, disokong oleh penekanan kerajaan terhadap infrastruktur kecerdasan buatan (AI) serta projek tulang belakang Grid Nasional 500-kilovolt Tenaga Nasional Bhd, yang memberi kelebihan kepada syarikat seperti MN Holdings Bhd, Southern Cable Group Bhd dan Powerwell Holdings Bhd,” menurut firma itu dalam nota penyelidikan hari ini. Selain itu, Malacca Securities menyatakan bahawa usaha mengurangkan air tanpa hasil (NRW) juga mungkin kekal menjadi tumpuan, berpotensi memberi manfaat kepada syarikat seperti ISF Group Bhd dan Ranhill Utilities Bhd. “Akhir sekali, 99 Speed Mart Retail mungkin menyaksikan minat belian baharu susulan jangkaan peruntukan bantuan pengguna lebih tinggi di bawah Sumbangan Asas Rahmah dan Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah,” menurut kenyataan itu. HeiTech Padu mendahului saham rugi, susut tujuh sen kepada 88 sen, Thong Guan Industries, Sunway Construction Group dan Allianz Malaysia merosot enam sen masing-masing kepada RM1.44, RM7.55 dan RM20.74, dan UMS Integration menguncup empat sen kepada RM9.36. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 bagaimanapun naik 41.29 mata kepada 17,584.78, Indeks FBM Emas meningkat 44.30 mata kepada 12,234.65, Indeks FBM Top 100 menokok 46.09 mata kepada 12,019.47, Indeks FBM Emas Syariah bertambah 39.24 mata kepada 12,108.25, manakala Indeks FBM ACE melonjak 7.73 mata kepada 5,614.34. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian naik 0.16 mata kepada 179.13, Indeks Tenaga meningkat 1.78 mata kepada 831.72, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan melonjak 56.47 mata kepada 19,196.61, manakala Indeks Perladangan naik 73.78 mata kepada 9,004.81. — BERNAMA

body: 'The local market drifted lower on Wednesday, weighed down by profit- taking among selected index heavyweights, with declines led by the transportation and banking sectors. The FBM KLCI shed 7.07 points to end at 1,676.43, off an early high of 1,685.37 and low of 1,675.15, as losers narrowly beat gainers 549 to 519, on lower turnover of 3.2bn shares worth RM2.99bn. The local benchmark index is expected to remain rangebound as investors await clearer policy signals from the ongoing U.S.-China talks, while the lack of meaningful domestic catalysts is likely to keep market direction subdued. Immediate resistance for the index remains at the June 2026 high (1,722), followed by tougher upside hurdles at the 123.6%FP (1,759) and 138.2%FP (1,805) ahead. Meantime, RHB Bank is attractive to bargain for oversold rebound towards the 50- day ma (RM8.28), with a convincing breakout above the 10/08/26 high (RM8.77) to target the 123.6%FP (RM9.14). Crucial support comes from the 61.8%FR (RM7.36) and 50%FR (RM7.02). title: 'PN Challenging Suspension in Court, Seeks Expedited Hearing as Melaka Polls Loom
body: 'PUTRAJAYA (Oct 5): Perikatan Nasional on Monday filed a legal challenge against its suspension and potential deregistration by the Registrar of Societies (RoS), and is seeking an expedited hearing to resolve the matter before the Melaka election. PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the coalition wants to quash notices issued by RoS under Sections 13(2) and 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966. Section 13(2) requires PN to explain its actions within 30 days or be deregistered. The Section 13(2A) notice informs PN that it must suspend its activities until it has responded to the matter. The suspension means PN cannot use its logo during the state polls. “The only reason given [for the notice and suspension] was that we did not invite Bersatu leaders for a meeting on July 16. But the official complaint by Bersatu was never given to us,” Takiyuddin, who is also secretary-general of PAS, said at a press conference on Monday. PN's application names RoS director-general Datuk Muhammad Zulfikar Ahmad and Home Minister Datuk Seri Datuk Sri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail as respondents. The Election Commission (EC) is expected to announce the date of the Melaka election after a meeting on Wednesday. The state polls must be held within 60 days of the Sept 23 dissolution of the Melaka assembly. Given the urgency, Takiyuddin said the coalition has also made a filing requesting that the case be expedited. “We want to ask the court to hear this case urgently because we need the court’s determination before the Melaka election is held,” he said. Takiyuddin said the coalition had engaged with the EC on this matter but the final word lay with the RoS. Asked whether PN component parties would use their own logos in the Melaka polls, Takiyuddin said: “These five parties, PAS, Wawasan, Gerakan, MIPP and Pejuang, have been negotiating that matter in view of all possibilities.” The suspension of PN comes after PAS said on June 8 it had ended political cooperation with Bersatu, the previously the dominant party in PN. However, the now beleaguered Bersatu was never expelled from the coalition. On Aug 11, Bersatu filed a complaint with RoS concerning its status in PN, as well as its exclusion from a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16. RoS sent the show-cause notice to PN on Sept 22, and the suspension order the next day as the Melaka assembly was dissolved. Takiyuddin said PN sent a letter to RoS on Sept 24 to obtain an explanation on the notice and suspension, but has yet to receive a response. He said Bersatu was excluded from the July 16 meeting due to the party's breaches of its own constitution earlier that week. Takiyuddin claimed that a Bersatu Supreme Council meeting had decided to use the party logo instead of the PN logo for the Negeri Sembilan polls, but that meeting had insufficient quorum as per the party’s constitution. He said PN feared that its deliberations would be invalid if Bersatu took part in the coalition’s supreme council meeting while in breach of its own party constitution. In the coalition's court filing, it argues that suspension order violated procedural fairness and the rules of natural justice, as PN was neither provided with details of Bersatu’s complaint nor granted an opportunity to be heard. PN said the suspension order impedes its ability to endorse candidates and its use of its registered name and symbol during the state election, thereby infringing upon rights under Articles 4(1), 8(1), 10(1)(a), 10(1)(c), and 119 of the Federal Constitution. Apart from quashing the RoS notices, PN wants the regulator to furnish all complaint documents and communications related to Bersatu within three days, as well as a stay on the suspension pending the disposal of the judicial review. Case management was fixed for Oct 13 before High Court Judge Datuk Azizan Arshad. title: 'JBPM sasar pelantikan 24,000 FSM dan FSO, perkukuh keselamatan kebakaran premis | Sinar Harian
body: 'JBPM sasar pelantikan 24,000 FSM dan FSO, perkukuh keselamatan kebakaran premis KUALA LUMPUR - Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia (JBPM) menyasarkan pelantikan 24,000 Pengurus Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSM) dan Pegawai Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSO) menjelang tahun 2030 sebagai langkah perkukuh kawal selia serta aspek keselamatan kebakaran di premis. Ini sekali gus menjadi kompenan penting dalam penubuhan Organisasi Keselamatan Kebakaran (OKK). Ketua Pengarah Bomba, Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad berkata, bagi pelantikan FSM, jumlahnya dijangka seramai 6,000 orang, manakala pelantikan FSO seramai 18,000 orang. Menurutnya, JBPM melihat sasaran ini sebagai satu keperluan strategik dan setakat ini seramai 498 lantikan telah dibuat membabitkan 174 peserta FSM dan 324 peserta FSO. "Ini merupakan sebahagian daripada keperluan untuk mematuhi Seksyen 27A Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba 1988 (Pindaan 2025) yang mensyaratkan bagi mana-mana premis yang dikenakan penguatkuasaan Perakuan Bomba perlu menubuhkan OKK. "OKK itu perlu ada jumlah yang minimum untuk dilantik dan dalam kalangan itu perlu ada seorang FSM dan tiga orang FSO," katanya dalam sidang akhbar selepas Majlis Pelancaran FSM dan FSO di Menara Merdeka Maybank, di sini pada Selasa. Tambahnya, sebagai persediaan ke arah OKK, JBPM telah melaksanakan pelbagai program libat urus bersama pihak berkepentingan. Katanya, Malaysia mempunyai sekitar 9,451 premis yang ditetapkan dengan profil dan tahap risiko keselamatan kebakaran yang berbeza. "Asasnya ialah bangunan yang telah kita kategorikan di bawah Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba," ujarnya. Jelas beliau, penguatkuasaan OKK secara penuh ini dijadualkan bermula 1 April 2027 sekali gus memberikan tempoh persediaan kepada pihak industri untuk membangunkan kompetensi, struktur organisasi dan tahap pematuhan yang diperlukan. "FSM dan FSO tidak akan mengambil alih peranan JBPM, tetapi melengkapkan ekosistem keselamatan kebakaran melalui pengurusan risiko secara berterusan di peringkat premis," ujarnya. Nor Hisham berkata, salah satu fungsi FSM ialah mengurangkan beban kepada penguatkuasaan berkaitan Perakuan Bomba. "Kalau pada amalan semasa ini berdasarkan prosedur-prosedur semasa kita periksa setiap tahun untuk kita keluarkan Sijil Perakuan Bomba. Tetapi di masa hadapan, tempoh itu akan kita jarakkan lagi. "Laporan pemeriksaan akan disediakan oleh FSM sebelum kita menilai dan membuat pembaharuan," ujarnya. Nor Hisham sebelum itu menyerahkan sijil perakuan kepada kumpulan pertama FSM serta FSO yang memenuhi syarat kelayakan ditetapkan. Muat turun aplikasi Sinar Harian. Klik di sini!

title: 'Bursa Malaysia opens higher on positive Wall Street momentum
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Tuesday, in sync with Wall Street's positive overnight momentum, as muted oil prices following a recovery in West Asia crude exports offset a continued sell-off in US Treasuries. At 9.21am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 7.14 points, or 0.44 per cent, to 1,638.89 from Monday's close of 1,631.75. The index opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38. On the broader market, gainers outpaced losers 272 to 202, with 364 counters unchanged, 1,944 untraded and 13 suspended. Turnover stood at 440.19 million shares worth RM164.76 million. Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd said Wall Street's positive overnight performance saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite advance by 0.2 per cent, 0.7 per cent and 1.1 per cent, respectively, while the Brent crude oil and 10-year Treasury yield reached US$100.3 per barrel and 5.3 per cent, respectively. "Locally, we expect investors to remain selective ahead of the Budget 2027 announcement, with attention centred on potential beneficiary sectors. "Mechanical and electrical players could continue to see buying interest, supported by the government's emphasis on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and Tenaga Nasional Bhd's 500-kilovolt National Grid Backbone project, favouring companies such as MN Holdings Bhd, Southern Cable Group Bhd, and Powerwell Holdings Bhd," it said in a research note today. title: 'Benign inflation keeps OPR outlook intact: CIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's inflation may remain benign despite firmer monthly price increases and rising food and electricity costs, according to CIMB Securities.   The research house said headline inflation rose to 1.9 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in August from 1.8 per cent in July, while core inflation eased to 1.7 per cent from 1.8 per cent, largely due to favourable base effects in information and communication.   However, both headline and core prices rose 0.3 per cent month-on-month (MoM), compared with no change in July, indicating firmer sequential price momentum.
