title: 'UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking and Maybank execute landmark MYOR-based transaction
body: 'PETALING JAYA: UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking Group and Malayan Banking (Maybank) recently executed the first Malaysia Overnight Rate-based three-month interbank money market transaction in the country, incorporating a two-day lookback calculation convention through an interbank money market broker. The landmark transaction was anchored by UOB Malaysia and executed with RHB and Maybank, marking a significant milestone in the evolution of Malaysia’s money market and supporting industry efforts towards the adoption of risk-free rate-based market conventions. The transaction enhances transparency and price discovery by making funding levels and spreads visible to a broader network of market participants. This contrasts with bilateral transactions, where pricing information is limited to the counterparties involved. By helping establish a transparent Malaysia Overnight Rate (MYOR) funding curve and an observable reference point for three-month interbank funding, the transaction improves visibility into funding spreads over MYOR and banks’ cost of borrowing, supporting more efficient pricing across the wider market. UOB Malayia corporate and investment banking country head Christina Cheah said, “The successful execution of this money market transaction reflects the strong collaboration between UOB Malaysia, RHB and Maybank in supporting the evolution of the country’s financial markets. By establishing a transparent benchmark for MYOR-based funding, we are contributing to greater price discovery and helping to build confidence in the adoption of risk-free rate conventions. “As a leading foreign bank in the country, UOB Malaysia remains committed to partnering local market participants, sharing regional expertise and supporting initiatives that strengthen market resilience and align the domestic financial ecosystem with global standards.” The transaction references MYOR compounded in arrears with a two-day lookback mechanism, providing operational certainty in interest calculations while remaining anchored to actual market transactions. RHB Banking Group wholesale banking managing director Nurjesmi Mohd Nashir said, “This transaction demonstrates how market participants can work together to put MYOR-based conventions into practice and support the continued development of Malaysia’s money market. “As the industry progresses towards the transition from KLIBOR to MYOR, it is important that we build practical market experience and develop conventions that can be adopted more widely. RHB is committed to supporting Bank Negara Malaysia’s efforts to develop a deeper and more efficient MYOR market, and to playing an active role in the continued development of Malaysia’s financial markets.” Farid Kairi, deputy group CEO of global banking and managing director of global markets said: “Maybank is pleased to have played an integral role in this inaugural MYOR-based money market transaction. It marks an important first step in establishing the foundation for deeper liquidity, while setting the stage for widening the aperture for more MYOR-linked solutions and supporting robust price discovery for market participants. “This achievement reflects the collective efforts of industry participants and Bank Negara Malaysia in strengthening Malaysia’s financial market infrastructure.” Bank Negara Malaysia introduced MYOR in September 2021 as Malaysia’s Alternative Reference Rate (ARR). MYOR is calculated as the volume-weighted average rate of actual unsecured overnight ringgit interbank transactions, providing a robust benchmark grounded in deep and liquid overnight funding markets. The transition towards MYOR aligns Malaysia with other major financial markets that have adopted overnight risk-free rates including Singapore, Japan, Switzerland, the United States and the United Kingdom.

title: 'Syed Saddiq & Bella Astillah Pilih ‘Kenduri Rakyat’ Untuk Kongsi Hari Bahagia
body: 'MAJLIS perkahwinan selalunya menjadi momen untuk diraikan bersama keluarga dan kenalan terdekat, namun Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman dan Bella Astillah memilih untuk membuka ruang lebih luas untuk berkongsi hari bahagia mereka. Bukan satu, malah dua majlis resepsi bertemakan ‘Kenduri Rakyat’ bakal diadakan di kampung halaman masing-masing iaitu di Muar, Johor dan Kota Kinabalu, Sabah. Pasangan ini merancang untuk mengadakan Kenduri Rakyat di Muar pada 25 Oktober, sebelum meneruskan sambutan di Kota Kinabalu pada 31 Oktober. Menurut Syed Saddiq, 34, konsep tersebut dipilih sebagai tanda penghargaan kepada mereka yang selama ini menitipkan doa, sokongan dan dorongan buat mereka berdua. Baginya, perkahwinan bukan sekadar tentang penyatuan dua individu, sebaliknya turut menjadi kesempatan untuk berkongsi kebahagiaan dengan mereka yang sentiasa memberikan sokongan. “Dari awal kalau ikut dari sudut tanggungjawab hakiki adalah nikah untuk menghalalkan hubungan kami berdua. “Namun pada masa yang sama, saya selalu kongsikan kepada bakal isteri saya (Bella), kebahagiaan itu perlu dikongsikan kepada semua juga. “Ini kerana tanpa doa, sokongan, dorongan mungkin hari ini tidak akan terjadi. Dan ‘the chapter of our future journey’ itu mungkin tidaklah semudah seperti hari ini,” ujarnya. Rewang Jadi Nadi Kenduri Rakyat Tidak mahu majlis sekadar berlangsung sebagai acara resepsi biasa, kedua-dua Kenduri Rakyat itu akan membawa konsep rewang dengan penduduk setempat turut dijemput untuk bersama-sama menyediakan juadah. “Bila namanya Kenduri Rakyat, tentunya kita akan buat rewang juga. Maksudnya orang kampung semua akan dijemput untuk sertai masak sekali. “Orang kampung semua dijemput hadir supaya kita dapat membumikan majlis perkahwinan ini untuk dinikmati oleh semua di luar sana,” katanya. Antara cabaran utama yang dihadapi adalah mendapatkan lokasi bersesuaian, selain memastikan keperluan kenduri dapat disediakan untuk jumlah tetamu yang dijangka ramai. Beberapa penaja turut tampil membantu menyediakan keperluan, termasuk beras, santan dan roti. Dengan jumlah kehadiran yang dijangka besar, pasangan itu juga memilih pendekatan yang lebih terbuka untuk tetamu yang hadir. “Kalau sebelum ini sambutan Hari Raya di Muar saja sudah mencecah 10,000 orang, jadi kita menjangkakan untuk kenduri kami nanti lebih ramai yang akan datang. “Jadi majlis itu nanti berkonsepkan siapa cepat dia dapat. Sekiranya makanan habis sekalipun, kami berdua akan tetap berada di sana untuk bersalam dan bersama dengan tetamu yang hadir,” katanya. Perkara itu dikongsikan Syed Saddiq ketika ditemui pada sidang media Walimatulurus Bella Astillah dan Syed Saddiq di Kuala Lumpur pada petang Jumaat. Dalam kesempatan sama, pasangan tersebut turut memaklumkan sebanyak 10,000 cenderahati istimewa disediakan untuk tetamu yang hadir ke kedua-dua majlis berkenaan. Bagi sambutan di Sabah pula, Bella atau nama lengkapnya, Dayang Nabellah Awang Astillah, 32, menjelaskan bahawa Kenduri Rakyat di Kota Kinabalu akan mengangkat tema pakaian tradisional Sabah sebagai penghormatan kepada kepelbagaian budaya negeri tersebut. Menariknya, kisah menuju hari bahagia mereka turut bakal dikongsi menerusi kerjasama bersama Astro. Program khas berkenaan akan membawa penonton mengikuti beberapa episod yang merakam persiapan menjelang akad nikah, kehidupan selepas bergelar suami isteri serta kemeriahan majlis resepsi di Muar dan Sabah. Pasangan popular ini bakal melangsungkan majlis pernikahan di aras 118, Menara Merdeka Maybank, Kuala Lumpur pada 10 Oktober ini. Kedua-duanya sebelum ini mengikat tali pertunangan pada 28 Mac lalu. Bella sebelum ini pernah mendirikan rumah tangga dengan penyanyi dan pelakon Aliff Aziz pada September 2016 sebelum bercerai pada 16 Mei 2019. Pasangan tersebut kemudian kembali rujuk, namun berpisah buat kali kedua pada 13 Jun 2024. Hasil perkahwinan itu, mereka dikurniakan dua cahaya mata, Ayden, 9, dan Ara, 6. - 7KLIK ARTIKEL LAIN:

title: 'Import Duty On Minted Gold Bars Drops To 0% From 1 November 2026
body: 'Small gold bars of 1g, 5g, or 10g have become a common way for people to put money aside a little at a time. Since 8 June 2026, though, anyone buying imported minted bars may have been paying for a 10% import duty included in the price. The Customs Duties (Amendment) Order 2026, P.U. (A) 350, cuts that duty from 10% to 0% from 1 November 2026. Gold Bars Covered By The Cut The cut applies to minted (stamped) gold bars, the small bars people buy to save. The most common sizes are 1g to 50g. The duty only ever applied to imported bars, so bars minted in Malaysia were never taxed and their prices have no duty to lose. Bank Muamalat sells imported bars, and it told customers in May that these bars would cost more once the duty applied. According to Tomei Consolidated group managing director Datuk Ng Yih Pyng, large cast bars, which weigh 1kg and up and are used by manufacturers, are classed differently and were already duty-free. Jewellery isn’t affected either. So this matters to you if you buy imported minted bars, or if you convert gold in your account into an imported physical bar. Possible Savings On An Imported Bar The duty is 10% of what a bar is worth when it arrives in Malaysia. So a bar worth RM100 costs the seller RM110 once the duty is added. When the duty is removed, RM110 drops back to RM100. That’s a saving of RM10 out of RM110, or about 9.1% off what the seller paid for the bar. On 5 October, Bank Muamalat sold a gold bar at RM605.02 a gram and gold in its account at RM584.53 a gram, according to its own price board. If the account price has no duty in it, the RM20.49 difference is the most the duty could be adding to each gram of the bar. The table below shows what that means for each bar size Bank Muamalat sells. RinggitPlus worked out these amounts using Bank Muamalat’s bar and account prices on 5 October 2026. Prices will change with the gold price. The real saving will be less than this, because part of the difference pays for making and packaging the bar, and that cost stays. Buying Now Or Waiting Until November If you buy gold every month through a gold account or gold savings plan, you probably don’t need to change anything. The Malaysia Gold Association’s president, Datuk Seri Louis Ng, said in September that the duty applies to minted bars in finished, packaged form, and not to kilobars and cast bars. So gold held in an account may not be affected, but check with your bank. If you’re planning to buy an imported minted bar in October, ask the seller two things. Did they pay the import duty on this bar, and will the price change after 1 November? Then work out how much more the bar costs than the seller’s gold account price, per gram. Do this now, and then again in the first week of November. If that difference shrinks, the duty removal has made the bar cheaper. If it doesn’t, any price drop is just the gold price moving. Do note that some sellers have already paid the duty on bars they have in stock now. They may keep their prices the same until those bars are sold, so prices may not drop straight away on 1 November. The gold price also changes every day. If the gold price goes up in November, it could cancel out what you save from the duty removal. Waiting makes the most sense if you were already planning to buy a 50g or 100g bar, and the seller confirms the duty is included in its price. Gold doesn’t earn interest, and gold accounts aren’t protected by PIDM the way savings accounts are. If you’re looking at gold accounts, see how Maybank Islamic’s MIGA-i works. title: 'World-Class Field Set to Illuminate Maybank Championship 2026 | Sports247
body: 'The Tiger Trophy is up for grabs: defending champion Miyu Yamashita, World No. 2 Jeeno Thitikul and a world-class field of Major champions and LPGA Tour winners set the stage for four days of high-stakes competition at KLGCC. Five ASEAN Qualifiers and four Malaysian Sponsor’s Invitations bring regional talents to one of Asia’s biggest stages. The Maybank Championship is set for another star-studded chapter when Asia’s premier ladies’ golf event returns to Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC) this October 29-November 1. With a USD3 million prize purse, the fourth edition brings together Major champions, LPGA Tour winners and Southeast Asia’s emerging talents for four days of world-class competition at KLGCC. A World-Class Line-Up The competition for the coveted Tiger Trophy has never been more intense. Defending champion and Major winner Miyu Yamashita of Japan is one of the most in-form players this season, highlighted by a dominant nine-stroke victory at the CPKC Women’s Open in Canada in August, and a playoff win at the Sony JLPGA Championship in Japan in September. Having claimed a dramatic three-way playoff victory at last year’s Maybank Championship, she will have every intention of becoming the tournament’s first repeat champion. Crowd favourite and World No. 2 Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand is also on a rich vein of form, having already claimed three LPGA Tour victories in 2026 to take her total title tally to ten. She returns for a fourth consecutive year in pursuit of the elusive Tiger Trophy, having narrowly missed out in each of her last appearances. Thitikul’s close friend Ruoning Yin of China, the 2024 Maybank Championship winner and a Major champion, will also return to Malaysia in winning mode having triumphed at the FM Championship in August. The spotlight will also firmly be turned on Korean ace Haeran Ryu, who is currently second on the LPGA Tour’s Race to CME Globe ranking on the back of successive Major victories in 2026 at the KPMG Women’s PGA Championship and the Amundi Evian Championship. title: 'Era of Cheap Debt Is Over as Corporates Face Tightening Credits — BIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 28): The era of cheap debt is over and rising global bond yields will squeeze earnings, pushing some corporates towards bank loans, BIMB Securities said. Credit conditions are tightening, hurting firms with unhedged floating rate debts, large refinancing needs and those facing upcoming maturities, the research house said. Capital-intensive and highly leveraged companies face greater earnings risk, amplified by weaker credit quality, the house noted. “In contrast, we see tech as one of the outlier sectors — where most stocks are actually net cash,” BIMB Securities said in a note. Unlike true artificial intelligence firms or data centre operators grappling with intensive capital expenditure plans, Malaysian tech stocks is a key rotation sector for the coming era of elevated rates, the house noted. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rate earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating. Bond issuances hit record highs in 2025 and corporates have continued to sell more debt this year tapping into the relatively inexpensive markets. “But this is likely to change as global rates outlook shifts to higher for longer,” BIMB Securities said. The house’s view is for the yield on 10-year government bonds to hold around 3.90% till end of the year but shift towards 4.00% by end-2027. Among the top 100 firms by market capitalisation, utilities, property, telecommunications, construction, healthcare and real estate investment trusts are the most exposed sectors, BIMB Securities flagged. The house also singled out IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) for its high floating rate debt exposure. Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) and Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) were also highlighted as both companies will have to come to the market to refinance substantial debt with sizeable maturities over the next 12 months. Banking stocks, meanwhile, could benefit from the shift, especially those with strong corporate lending franchises, the research house said. Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK), CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK), in particular, could benefit from the temporary migration of borrowers from the bond market to bank loans, the house said. title: 'Hilang Sumber Pendapatan Sejak Suami Sakit, Ibu Anak Empat Niaga Dalam Bonet Kereta Demi Sesuap Nasi
body: 'Diuji suami sakit secara tiba-tiba kerana sakit buah pinggang tahap empat dan kanser limfoma, ibu anak empat ini tetap gigih berdiri di bawah payung kecil yang dipacak di tepi bonet kereta demi mencari sesuap nasi dan selesaikan komitmen bulanan. Hilang Sumber Pendapatan Sejak Suami Sakit Kalau sebelum ini suaminya bekerja sebagai pemandu lori, sekarang hanya mampu duduk di atas kerusi dan terbaring di katil. Sesekali dia akan ulang-alik ke hospital untuk rawatan sakitnya. Dari beratnya 78kg, susut kepada 54kg disebabkan hilang selera makan. Beban mencari rezeki dan mengurus rumah tangga kini tergalas di atas bahu Puan Norin Sah binti Md Rejab selepas suaminya, Shaiful Bahari bin Muhamad Saad, 50, hanya terlantar di atas katil sejak disahkan menghidap penyakit kanser limfoma sejak bulan Januari tahun 2025. Ibu Anak Empat Niaga Dalam Bonet Kereta Demi Sesuap Nasi Setiap kali pelajar sekolah keluar dari pintu pagar, setiap kali itu lah wajah wanita berusia 44 tahun ini akan tersenyum dek kerana akan ada rezekinya masuk apabila jualan aiskrim Malaysia dan buah potongnya dibeli. Nampak kecil tetapi nilainya cukup besar bagi ibu yang gigih mencari rezeki demi anak-anak tersayang. Ibu kepada empat anak itu berkata, sejak suaminya disahkan menghidap kanser, kehidupan keluarganya berubah apabila suaminya tidak lagi dapat bekerja seperti sebelum ini. Tidak berharap lebih, tetapi cukuplah jika dapat bantu selesaikan apa yang patut dan suapkan anak-anak dengan rezeki yang halal. “Saya sendiri buntu memikirkan di mana hendak mencari duit selepas ini kerana perlu membuat bayaran macam-macam. Jual Makanan dalam bonet kereta tidak lah dapat banyak mana. tapi alhamdulillah, lepas lah buat beli lauk” katanya. Apabila keluar berniaga, Puan Norin atau lebih mesra dipanggil Kak Sya terpaksa tinggal suaminya di rumah sekejap. Dari segi sumbangan, ada dapat sedikit daripada kejiranan dan kebajikan sekitar taman. Orang ramai yang berhasrat membantu meringankan beban Kak Sya, boleh terus memberikan sumbangan menerusi nombor akaun ini: Maybank: 152116003190 Nama: Norin Sah binti Md Rejab Nilainya tak banyak tak mengapa, yang penting ikhlas untuk meringankan beban ibu ini. Semoga dengan sedikit pemberian kita hari ini dapat membuatkan wajah seseorang yang diuji kembali tersenyum dan rasa masih ada harapan untuk melangkah ke depan.

title: 'Bursa Appoints Former Maybank Technology Head As Group Tech Director
body: 'Bursa Malaysia Bhd has appointed Ravinder Singh Bachan Singh as Director, Group Technology, effective Sept 28, 2026.  The stock exchange operator said Ravinder, 45, will also be designated as a Principal Officer of the company upon assuming his new role.  Ravinder brings more than 20 years of experience in the domestic and international financial services industry, spanning investment banking, asset management, wealth management and transaction banking.  Prior to joining Bursa Malaysia, he served as Head of Technology for Maybank Investment Banking Group, where he oversaw technology functions across its investment banking and asset management businesses.  His expertise includes technology strategy and transformation, digital platforms, cybersecurity, operational resilience and technology governance across multiple markets.  Ravinder holds a Degree in Computing from Staffordshire University in the United Kingdom and is TOGAF 9 certified by The Open Group, a professional qualification in enterprise architecture.

body: 'Other achievements include Best Company in IR by Sector, Best Financial Reporting and Best CEO in IR Maybank, one of ASEAN’s leading financial services institutions, achieved a landmark recognition at Bursa Malaysia’s inaugural Investor Relations Awards 2026, securing four awards across company and leadership categories. Leading the Group’s achievements is its recognition as Best Company in IR (Overall), setting a strong standard for investor relations excellence. It highlights Maybank’s clear equity story and consistent engagements with its stakeholders, underpinned by a strong track record of delivery. As we execute ROAR30 and support the aspirations of MYValueUp, we remain focused on strengthening market confidence, enhancing investability and delivering long term value through disciplined execution, while ensuring our growth translates into impactful outcomes for all stakeholders,” said Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia dijangka bergerak mendatar minggu ini
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Bursa Malaysia dijangka bergerak secara mendatar dan tidak menentu pada minggu ini dengan aktiviti penggiliran minat pelabur mengikut sektor. Remisier Maybank Investment Bank, Jeffry Azizi Jaafar berkata, tekanan utama terhadap pasaran dijangka datang daripada pendirian Rizab Persekutuan (Fed) Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang lebih ketat, peningkatan hasil bon negara itu serta pengukuhan dolar AS. Katanya, sentimen pasaran masih disokong harga minyak yang tinggi dan pemulihan saham semikonduktor di Wall Street. “Fed baru menaikkan kadar faedah, manakala hasil bon AS 10 tahun telah melepasi lima peratus, menyebabkan pelabur global lebih berhati-hati terhadap aset berisiko. “Justeru itu, Indeks Komposit Kuala Lumpur (FBM KLCI) dijangka bergerak dalam julat tertentu dan bukannya mencatatkan kenaikan menyeluruh. “Minat belian berkemungkinan tertumpu kepada sektor yang mempunyai pemangkin khusus, manakala saham berharga tinggi dan sensitif terhadap kadar faedah berpotensi mengalami pengambilan untung,” katanya kepada Utusan Malaysia. Beliau berkata, pergerakan ringgit, harga minyak dan aliran dana asing akan menjadi petunjuk penting kepada pasaran. “Penutupan positif Nasdaq pada Jumaat boleh membantu sentimen terhadap saham teknologi pada awal minggu, tetapi kenaikan hasil bon mengehadkan ruang kenaikan,” katanya. Mengulas lanjut, beliau berkata, sektor perbankan berpotensi menjadi antara penentu utama arah FBM KLCI minggu ini berikutan pemberatnya yang besar dalam indeks. Katanya, antara kaunter yang boleh diberi perhatian ialah Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank), CIMB Group Holdings Berhad, Public Bank Berhad dan RHB Bank Berhad. “Jika bank-bank besar kekal stabil, FBM KLCI boleh bertahan walaupun prestasi keseluruhan pasaran bercampur. “Bagaimanapun, kenaikan kadar faedah AS tidak semestinya meningkatkan keuntungan bank Malaysia secara langsung kerana kadar domestik masih ditentukan oleh Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM),” katanya. Beliau berkata, dalam keadaan pasaran tidak menentu, sektor utiliti dan saham defensif turut berpotensi menerima pengaliran dana berikutan pendapatan yang lebih stabil. “Antara kaunter yang boleh diperhatikan termasuk Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), Telekom Malaysia Berhad, Maxis Berhad dan YTL Power International Berhad. “Dalam pada itu, sektor minyak dan gas dijangka menjadi antara sektor paling aktif minggu depan berikutan harga minyak mentah Brent yang masih melebihi AS$100 (RM408.21) setong walaupun mengalami sedikit penurunan. “Keadaan ini dijangka mengekalkan minat terhadap kaunter minyak dan gas termasuk Hibiscus Petroleum Berhad, Bumi Armada Berhad, Dialog Group Berhad, Dayang Enterprise Holdings Berhad dan Velesto Energy Berhad. “Sektor ini mempunyai pemangkin paling jelas, tetapi pelabur perlu mengelak daripada mengejar harga sekiranya kaunter terus mencatatkan kenaikan mendadak pada pembukaan Isnin,” katanya. Sementara itu, Jeffry berkata, sektor teknologi dan semikonduktor berpotensi mencatatkan pemulihan secara terpilih selepas Nasdaq ditutup lebih tinggi pada Jumaat, dibantu saham semikonduktor. “Pelancaran global produk baharu Apple turut berpotensi mengekalkan perhatian terhadap rantaian bekalan elektronik. “Antara kaunter yang boleh diberi perhatian termasuk Inari Amertron Berhad, Malaysian Pacific Industries Berhad, Unisem (M) Berhad, Frontken Corporation Berhad dan ViTrox Corporation Berhad. “Bagaimanapun, sektor teknologi masih sensitif terhadap hasil bon AS. Oleh itu, kenaikan mungkin bersifat terpilih dan bukan semua saham teknologi akan meningkat secara serentak,” katanya. – UTUSAN

title: 'Man freed of RM108,500 cheating charge
body: 'Kota Kinabalu: A 50-year-old self-employed was freed from a charge of cheating a man involving a sum of RM108,500 over several projects in Kinabatangan and Semporna. Magistrate Wan Farrah Farriza Wan Ghazali discharged and acquitted Abdillah Hamzah without his defence being called after ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against him. Abdillah was accused of cheating one Chong Kong Fah by deceiving him into believing that Abdillah had managed the following projects namely, to build a concrete road to SMK Bukit Garam, Kinabatangan, to upgrade the drainage system at Bukit Permata Housing Estate, Kinabatangan, to repair the floating Jetty at Dataran Lepa-Lepa, Semporna, to upgrade the road in the Dolton Town area, Semporna and to repair houses in Semporna. The charge stated that Chong had banked-in the money into a company account under the name of Dilwani Enterprise, which he would not have done had he not been so deceived. The offence allegedly took place between June 23, 2016 and Dec 5, 2018 at the Maybank in Semporna branch. The offence under Section 420 of the Penal Code carries a jail term of up to 10 years and whipping, and liable to a fine, on conviction. The prosecution had called six witnesses during the hearing. Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Noor Hafizah Anggu standing in for DPP Arfa Anchal Khan while counsel Nurul Rafeeqa Afdul Mutolip defended Abdillah. Meanwhile, a 64-year-old man pleaded guilty to causing grievous injury to another man with a machete. However, Sessions Court Judge Marlina Ibrahim deferred Paul Akang’s sentencing to Oct 28 this year pending medical and forensic reports. Pending the date, Paul was further remanded. Paul is accused of causing serious injury to the 45-year-old man by using the weapon at 5pm on Sept 21 this year in front of a house in Kg Kelansatan, Kuala Penyu. DPP Ronnie Antony prosecuted the case. Man freed of RM108,500 cheating charge Daily Express Daily Express Online (Malaysia) is Sabah's top-ranked & most viewed English news site. It is also Sabah's leading & most circulated daily English newspaper.

body: 'Helen”s Kitchen 的炸鱼排 Fish and Chips，的确好吃，绝不输给它家的招牌 Chicken Chop（海南鸡扒）。 古有孟母三迁、今有老板“两年五搬”。经过5次搬迁后，没想到这次的炸鱼排反而像获得“神助攻”，比以前更好吃。难怪老板一直叫我一定要试试 Fish and Chips。 当然，海南鸡扒依然是熟悉的味道，外脆内嫩再配上传统海南式茄汁，简单、就是好吃。 说回炸鱼排，鱼肉鲜嫩、不腥，炸衣薄脆、不会厚厚一层粉，入口香脆，鱼肉的鲜味也吃得出来。尤其趁热吃，一口接一口、还真的停不了。 我个人更喜欢抹上浓郁的塔塔酱，Creamy的口感，鱼香、酱香一起入口，满口都是香。 - Advertisement - 除了招牌西餐，Helen”s Kitchen 还有炸鱼肉或大虾青冬炎，以及红豆冰、煎蕊两款甜品都做得很好。 老板说，因为摊档空间不大，目前就先卖这几样，往后可能还会再增加几道拿手好菜。 Helen”s Kitchen 其实并没有“躲”起来，只是一说破就知道……它就在丹绒武雅著名路边炸香蕉糕，“上面”的咖啡店里。 从坡底上来，过了MayBank再转进左边的BARAKATH 扁担饭，看过去对面的咖啡店内就是。 若还是找不到？地址直接给你： 1-0-8, Jalan Chan Siew Teong, Tanjung Bungah, 11200 George Town, Pulau Pinang。 营业时间：上午9时30分至下午5时，逢周二休息。 - Advertisement - › 立即申请 - GMBB Part Timer - Event - Kuala Lumpur - MYR 110.00 /Month › 立即申请

title: 'Maybank, UPSI santuni komuniti menerusi pendidikan dan kreativiti
body: 'TANJONG MALIM – Hampir 200 warga Maybank dari seluruh Perak berganding bahu dengan Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI) menjayakan program kesukarelawanan berteraskan pendidikan, kreativiti dan pemerkasaan komuniti menerusi Maybank Group Global Corporate Responsibility (CR) Day 2026.  Program yang berlangsung di Kampus Sultan Azlan Shah itu merupakan kerjasama pertama Maybank Group Global CR Day dengan UPSI menerusi Pusat Pembangunan Akademik dan SULAM@UPSI.  Timbalan Naib Canselor (Akademik dan Antarabangsa) UPSI, Prof Dr Raja Nor Safinaz Raja Harun berkata, program bertemakan “Impacting Society Positively, Enabling Well-Being for All” itu mencerminkan komitmen bersama sektor industri dan institusi pendidikan tinggi dalam menghasilkan impak positif kepada masyarakat.  “Pendekatan ini selari dengan aspirasi UPSI untuk menghubungkan ilmu, pendidikan dan kepakaran universiti dengan keperluan sebenar komuniti,” katanya.  Menurut beliau, dua modul SULAM@UPSI yang mempunyai elemen keusahawanan dan kelestarian serta menyasarkan golongan berkeperluan khas dipilih bagi program berkenaan.  Ia membabitkan SULAM Sen-Care daripada Fakulti Pembangunan Manusia (FPM) dan Creative Heritage For Good daripada Fakulti Seni, Kelestarian dan Industri Kreatif (FSKIK).  Raja Nor Safinaz berkata, UPSI berharap program itu menjadi pemangkin kepada kerjasama strategik lebih luas bersama Maybank, khususnya dalam pembangunan bakat, pendidikan, keusahawanan, inovasi, kesukarelawanan dan pemerkasaan komuniti.  “UPSI berharap penganjuran ini bukan sekadar program sehari, sebaliknya menjadi titik permulaan kepada lebih banyak kerjasama strategik pada masa hadapan,” katanya. title: 'RHB Bank sees more upside for 4Q26 | KLSE Screener
body: 'PETALING JAYA: RHB Bank Bhd’s management has shared that there is sufficient runway to reposition the bank’s portfolio and capitalise on market opportunities for the fourth quarter ending Dec 31, 2026 (4Q26) after surging Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields weigh on non- interest income (NOII) in 3Q26. Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research said the bank’s near-term outlook faces pressure from elevated MGS yields, which could weigh on its 3Q26 NOII, but that management appears less downbeat on the 4Q26 outlook should MGS yields stabilise or retrace. The research house, which recently met with the bank’s management, maintained a “hold” call and target price of RM8 based on implied one time 2027 price to book, as most near-term drivers have been baked in, with no stronger immediate catalyst. “We came away from a recent meeting with RHB’s management feeling neutral on its earnings trajectory and asset quality outlook,” it said, with weaker trading income largely inevitable given the limited runway for recovery during 3Q26. ...

title: 'BERNAMA - Malaysia Entering More Supportive Water Investment Cycle  -- CIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 (Bernama) -- Malaysia is entering a more supportive water investment cycle as ageing infrastructure, high water losses and rising industrial and data centre demand, as well as greater climate variability are increasing the urgency to improve water efficiency, reliability, and resilience. In a note today, CIMB Securities said the federal government had approved RM1.7 billion under the 13th Malaysia Plan to replace about 1,800 kilometres of critical pipes from 2026 to 2030, alongside a multi-year National Non-Revenue Water (NRW) Programme. It said sizeable projects including Langat 2 Phase 2, Rasau Phase 2, and the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme should further strengthen water security and provide a visible pipeline for contractors, pipe manufacturers and ancillary solution providers. CIMB Securities said Malaysia’s NRW rate stood at 37.1 per cent in 2024. “Persistently high NRW, ageing distribution networks, and rising climate variability result in unnecessary raw water extraction, higher treatment and pumping requirements, weaker utility economics, and supply disruption risks. “Concurrently, population growth, industrialisation, and rapid data centre development are driving structural water demand, particularly across economic corridors in Selangor, Johor, and Penang,” it added. The stockbroking company said Malaysia’s water transition is seen broadening from purely building new infrastructure towards using existing water resources and assets more efficiently. It said sustainable NRW reduction requires physical rehabilitation alongside smart metering, leak detection, pressure management, telemetry, analytics, and intelligent asset-management systems. “These technologies can make water networks more visible, measurable, and manageable, improving the effectiveness of every ringgit spent on water infrastructure. “This is aligned with the Water Sector Transformation 2040 (WST2040), which promotes digitalisation, climate resilience, integrated water-resource management, and stronger sector governance,” it said. From an investment perspective, CIMB Securities said it favours companies positioned at either the efficiency or infrastructure-enablement layers of Malaysia’s water transition. “Insight Analytics Bhd is among the most direct listed proxies to water digitalisation and NRW management, while Gamuda Bhd offers exposure to large-scale treatment, transmission, and water security projects. “The key near-term risk remains the pace at which funding and policy commitments translate into tenders, project awards, and, ultimately, earnings,” it said. -- BERNAMA BERNAMA provides up-to-date authentic and comprehensive news and information which are disseminated via BERNAMA Wires; www.bernama.com; BERNAMA TV on Astro 502, unifi TV 631 and MYTV 121 channels and BERNAMA Radio on FM93.9 (Klang Valley), FM107.5 (Johor Bahru), FM107.9 (Kota Kinabalu) and FM100.9 (Kuching) frequencies. title: 'DNB completes RM5.2 bil syndicated Islamic financing ahead of ownership transition
body: 'DNB completes RM5.2 bil syndicated Islamic financing ahead of ownership transition KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, which it said will strengthen its financial position and support its next phase of growth. In a statement, DNB said the financing, the largest syndicated loan facility arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia, includes the refinancing of its Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on Sept 29, 2026, and provides longer-term funding. The exercise comes as DNB prepares to transition from a government-backed structure to equal ownership among its three mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders — CelcomDigi Bhd (KL:CDB) through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd (KL:YTLPOWR) — expected in early fourth quarter of 2026. Minister of Finance Inc will exit as an ordinary shareholder but retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and oversee key strategic matters. DNB said the financing was completed alongside the award of the full 100MHz of the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz (F0) spectrum and the conversion of its entire 240MHz spectrum holding into a spectrum assignment. The spectrum assignment takes effect from Oct 1, 2026, following its issuance by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission. DNB said the spectrum assignment will increase network capacity, efficiency and performance, while supporting technologies such as massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities. Chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said in the statement the financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate independently, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and make use of its expanded spectrum assets. DNB was established in March 2021 to accelerate Malaysia’s 5G roll-out and operate as the country’s sole wholesale 5G network provider. In May 2023, the government announced a shift to a dual 5G network model. U Mobile Sdn Bhd was selected to develop Malaysia’s second 5G network in November 2024 and was subsequently offboarded from DNB’s network on June 30, 2026. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger, with AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd as joint mandated lead arrangers for the financing. AmInvestment Bank was the financial adviser to DNB. title: 'End ongoing violations of Orang Asli land rights in Pahang – 19 NGOs
body: 'We, the undersigned civil society organisations and individuals, are deeply concerned by the situation confronting the Orang Asli of Pahang in general, and of the communities of Tasek Bera in particular, who are facing eviction, harassment and arrest and are being treated as a scapegoat for ongoing deforestation. Violations in Tasek Bera In June 2026, about 20 Orang Asli villages in the Tasek Bera area received eviction notices from the Pahang Forestry Department, ordering them to vacate their settlements and farmland. These kampungs, including Kampung Kuala Serting, Kampung Lubuk Tiang, Kampung Tambangan, Kampung Lenguin, Kampung Gakuyah, Kampung Pathir, Kampung Limbahan, Kampung Mahang, Kampung Ibam and Kampung Buloh Nipis, lie within the Tasek Bera permanent forest reserve (hutan simpan kekal). In response, the communities acted collectively, erecting blockades to protect their customary lands and monitoring activities within their territories. On 14 September, officers from the Pahang State Forestry Department and Department of Wildlife arrived at Kampung Pathir, stating their intention to conduct land surveying. The communities refused them entry pending a resolution on the eviction notices, with Tok Batin Amir Noor Tan of Kampung Pathir calling for the eviction notices to be withdrawn. This standoff escalated, resulting in the arrest of five Orang Asli, four of them women, on the same day. They were subsequently released on 16 September. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Another similar incident involving police and communities within Tasek Bera also took place in Kampung Kuala Serting on 23 September. These recent developments are not an isolated case and form part of a growing trend of land grabs in Pahang. For example, outside Tasek Bera, on 9 February, 21 Orang Asli villagers from Kampung Jemeri in Rompin, Pahang, were detained by police following a complaint from a company claiming rights to develop land allegedly owned by the sultan of Pahang. According to a community statement, the sultan had [allegedly] obtained title to the 718-hectare oil palm plantation, developed by Orang Asli smallholders, less than a month earlier, on 26 January. The land in question forms part of the traditional territories of Jakun smallholders who had opened their smallholdings there 10-13 years ago. Orang Asli not driving deforestation Since early 2026, we have observed the development of a narrative in Pahang portraying the Orang Asli as groups that are scheming with outsiders to convert forest reserves into agricultural land. For example, while the above events were occurring in Tasek Bera, mainstream and state media repeatedly circulated claims that more than 7,000 hectares of forest within the Tasek Bera Ramsar site, which spans 38,446 hectares, had been illegally converted. This conversion was attributed to six Orang Asli families who allegedly used outsiders to exploit customary land rights in carrying out the encroachment. This narrative fails to accurately depict the drivers of deforestation in the state. A recent article by RimbaWatch found that at least 72,000 hectares of forest are under threat in Pahang, driven primarily by the expansion of monoculture industrial timber plantations in forest reserves, a programme supported by both the state and federal governments. Measured against this scale, traditional forest utilisation carried out by Orang Asli communities is minor. Yet it is their communities, not state and corporate drivers of deforestation, that are being singled out and blamed. Orang Asli traditional territories have existed for generations, predating independence and their later gazettement as timber production areas. Research has continuously shown that safeguarded Indigenous territories exhibit remarkable ecological resilience and biodiversity outcomes. Arrests of Orang Asli community members, ongoing harassment and the undue stress of receiving eviction notices or discovering that their land now belongs to outsiders all point to a troubling reality: as rights to their traditional territories are denied, the Orang Asli in Pahang are becoming outsiders on their own territories and scapegoated as drivers of widespread deforestation. Apex courts’ consistent rulings The Federal Court and Court of Appeal have repeatedly recognised that Orang Asli possess native customary land rights – a form of proprietary right protected under Article 13 of the Federal Constitution, provided a substantial connection to the land in question can be proven [Rosli Jendut & Ors v Agrobest (M) Sdn Bhd & Ors (2026)]. These rights pre-date both the Aboriginal Peoples Act 1954 and the National Land Code, and do not depend on any document of title. The rights are not limited to settlement areas. As the Federal Court in Rosli Jendut makes clear, these rights also extend to lands which are central to the Orang Asli’s cultural way of life, such as tombstones and grave sites. As such, despite the lack of gazettement and formal documents of title, the proprietary rights of Orang Asli communities in Tasek Bera over their traditional territories should be recognised and respected according to the Federal Court. Call to action The gaps between the judiciary and the executive are glaring and deeply concerning. While the courts have, time and again, affirmed the proprietary rights of the Orang Asli to their traditional territories, this recognition is not reflected by executive action. Communities like the Orang Asli in Tasek Bera, while actively fighting to protect their territories, are bearing the cost of this disconnect through evictions, arrests and the destruction of their lands. We urge the federal government to intervene immediately to safeguard the rights and wellbeing of the Orang Asli, as recognised by our Federal Courts and the Constitution. We call for an end to the misleading and negative portrayal of the Orang Asli community. Furthermore, we call for the following measures. - The Pahang state government must withdraw all eviction notices issued to the Orang Asli communities in Pahang, particularly those grounded solely on the claim that the communities are residing within permanent forest reserves. - The Pahang state government and their agencies must conduct genuine free, prior and informed consent consultation with affected communities for any decisions that will affect them, in line with Malaysia’s commitments under the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP). - Suhakam must conduct an independent inquiry into the conduct of the Tasek Bera enforcement operations, and the findings made public and acted upon by the federal and Pahang state government without delay, vis-a-vis recommendations made in the 2013 National Inquiry on the Land Rights of Indigenous Peoples in Malaysia being adopted and implemented. - The Pahang state government and its agencies (eg Jakoa) must accelerate and make transparent the gazettement of Orang Asli traditional territories, with clear timelines for the villages still pending survey. - The federal government must halt the ongoing amendment process of the Orang Asli Act 1954 until legally binding recognition of traditional territories is guaranteed. Endorsed by the following organisations / Disokong oleh organisasi berikut: - RimbaWatch - Centre for Orang Asli Concerns (COAC) - Save Rivers - Pertubuhan Wanita Orang Asal Malaysia (PWOAM) - Alliance of River Three (Art!) - Gabungan Darurat Iklim Malaysia - Saya Anak Bangsa Malaysia (SABM) - University of Malaya Association of New Youth (Umany） - Amnesty International Malaysia - Greenpeace Malaysia - Teoh Beng Hock Association for Democratic Advancement (TBH-ADA) - SeDarjat - Persatuan Kesedaran Komuniti Selangor (Empower) - Parti Sosialis Malaysia (PSM) - Gabungan Marhaen - Kemban Kolektif - Greater Equitable Measures (Gem) – Malaysia - Center to Combat Corruption and Cronyism (C4 Center) - Centre for Independent Journalism (CIJ) upan rakyat - Galakkan pembangunan saksama, lestari serta tangani krisis alam sekitar - Raikan kerencaman dan keterangkuman - Selamatkan demokrasi dan angkatkan keluhuran undang-undang - Lawan rasuah dan kronisme Endorsed by the following individuals / Disokong oleh individu berikut: The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Orang Asli not driving deforestation Since early 2026, we have observed the development of a narrative in Pahang portraying the Orang Asli as groups that are scheming with outsiders to convert forest reserves into agricultural land. For example, while the above events were occurring in Tasek Bera, mainstream and state media repeatedly circulated claims that more than 7,000 hectares of forest within the Tasek Bera Ramsar site, which spans 38,446 hectares, had been illegally converted. This conversion was attributed to six Orang Asli families who allegedly used outsiders to exploit customary land rights in carrying out the encroachment. This narrative fails to accurately depict the drivers of deforestation in the state. A recent article by RimbaWatch found that at least 72,000 hectares of forest are under threat in Pahang, driven primarily by the expansion of monoculture industrial timber plantations in forest reserves, a programme supported by both the state and federal governments. Measured against this scale, traditional forest utilisation carried out by Orang Asli communities is minor. Yet it is their communities, not state and corporate drivers of deforestation, that are being singled out and blamed. Orang Asli traditional territories have existed for generations, predating independence and their later gazettement as timber production areas. Research has continuously shown that safeguarded Indigenous territories exhibit remarkable ecological resilience and biodiversity outcomes. Arrests of Orang Asli community members, ongoing harassment and the undue stress of receiving eviction notices or discovering that their land now belongs to outsiders all point to a troubling reality: as rights to their traditional territories are denied, the Orang Asli in Pahang are becoming outsiders on their own territories and scapegoated as drivers of widespread deforestation. Apex courts’ consistent rulings The Federal Court and Court of Appeal have repeatedly recognised that Orang Asli possess native customary land rights – a form of proprietary right protected under Article 13 of the Federal Constitution, provided a substantial connection to the land in question can be proven [Rosli Jendut & Ors v Agrobest (M) Sdn Bhd & Ors (2026)]. These rights pre-date both the Aboriginal Peoples Act 1954 and the National Land Code, and do not depend on any document of title. The rights are not limited to settlement areas. As the Federal Court in Rosli Jendut makes clear, these rights also extend to lands which are central to the Orang Asli’s cultural way of life, such as tombstones and grave sites. As such, despite the lack of gazettement and formal documents of title, the proprietary rights of Orang Asli communities in Tasek Bera over their traditional territories should be recognised and respected according to the Federal Court. Call to action The gaps between the judiciary and the executive are glaring and deeply concerning. While the courts have, time and again, affirmed the proprietary rights of the Orang Asli to their traditional territories, this recognition is not reflected by executive action. Communities like the Orang Asli in Tasek Bera, while actively fighting to protect their territories, are bearing the cost of this disconnect through evictions, arrests and the destruction of their lands. We urge the federal government to intervene immediately to safeguard the rights and wellbeing of the Orang Asli, as recognised by our Federal Courts and the Constitution. We call for an end to the misleading and negative portrayal of the Orang Asli community. Furthermore, we call for the following measures. - The Pahang state government must withdraw all eviction notices issued to the Orang Asli communities in Pahang, particularly those grounded solely on the claim that the communities are residing within permanent forest reserves. - The Pahang state government and their agencies must conduct genuine free, prior and informed consent consultation with affected communities for any decisions that will affect them, in line with Malaysia’s commitments under the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP). - Suhakam must conduct an independent inquiry into the conduct of the Tasek Bera enforcement operations, and the findings made public and acted upon by the federal and Pahang state government without delay, vis-a-vis recommendations made in the 2013 National Inquiry on the Land Rights of Indigenous Peoples in Malaysia being adopted and implemented. - The Pahang state government and its agencies (eg Jakoa) must accelerate and make transparent the gazettement of Orang Asli traditional territories, with clear timelines for the villages still pending survey. - The federal government must halt the ongoing amendment process of the Orang Asli Act 1954 until legally binding recognition of traditional territories is guaranteed. title: 'MyDebit CIMB bakal mengalami gangguan sementara pada 19, 22 dan 23 Septmber 2026
body: 'Perkhidmatan MyDebit CIMB bakal mengalami gangguan sementara berikutan kerja-kerja penyelenggaraan sistem berjadual. Gangguan tersebut bakal menjejaskan pengguna CIMB Bank Berhad dan CIMB Islamic Bank Berhad. Selain itu, semua pembelian menggunakan Kad Debit melalui MyDebit, Visa dan Mastercard secara fizikal atau dalam talian akan terjejas semasa waktu penyelenggaraan. Tujuan penyelenggaraan ini dibuat untuk memberikan pengalaman penggunaan yang lebih baik pada masa akan datang. Bagi mengelakkan sebarang gangguan, CIMB menyarankan pengguna untuk merancang perbelanjaan lebih awal.

title: 'Cover Story: How the AI tidal wave is reshaping the jobs market
body: 'Cover Story: How the AI tidal wave is reshaping the jobs market This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026 FOR engineering outfit owner John, using artificial intelligence (AI) in his work has been a game changer. He “trains” the AI to write codes in the company’s style and now merely checks to ensure that the codes are written correctly. “I use AI to write more routine codes and it has helped me cut down coding time significantly, where a few days of work can be accomplished in 20 minutes. But I still need a few employees because engineers need to be at the physical location to make sure hardware is properly installed and conduct test runs,” he says. These days, the use of AI is prevalent in all aspects of life, in various sectors of the economy and professions, and more so among white-collar workers. Early research has shown that AI has, by some measure, improved the productivity of workers, but it still depends on the complexity of tasks and the user’s ability in AI prompting. Even so, AI is increasingly becoming part of everyday life. As a result, companies will soon be able to achieve the same outcomes with fewer workers — or, in some roles, none at all. The concern among white-collar workers about AI displacing jobs is real. Jobstreet’s Workplace Happiness Index found that while only around one-third of Malaysian workers feel “very” or “extremely” concerned about AI affecting their job security, the score is even higher among professional services workers, coming in at 47%. While there is no evidence of massive job loss as a result of AI at this juncture, recruitment agencies observe that job postings for certain roles have been declining. Jobstreet by SEEK in Malaysia managing director Nicholas Lam says AI is certainly putting pressure on some forms of white-collar work, particularly roles involving repetitive, standardised or administrative tasks, many of which are being automated. Current data points, however, more towards roles being redesigned than entire professions being replaced. “The clearest early signs of pressure are in selected content and administrative roles. Job ads for positions such as content writer, copywriter, secretary and graphic designer declined between 2024 and 1H2026. We see these trends as directional indicators that automation may be changing how these roles are structured, rather than proof of one-for-one job replacement,” Lam says. This observation is consistent with a May report by the International Labour Organization (ILO), which found that studies using job postings and online labour-platform data show a significant decline in demand for skills associated with routine writing and translation, following the diffusion of generative AI (GenAI) tools, alongside increased demand for AI-related skills such as machine learning and natural language processing. PwC Malaysia managing partner Soo Hoo Khoon Yean argues that the gradual redesign of work does not necessarily imply that workers will be displaced. Instead, he says, it points to a gradual shift in the mix of capabilities and skills required in those roles. “There may be a growing divide between workers who are able to integrate AI into their workflows and adapt to evolving skill requirements, and those who are unable to,” Soo Hoo says. “As AI becomes more capable, competitive advantage will increasingly come from areas where human strengths like context, judgement and accountability matter most. This includes making high-stakes decisions, solving nuanced problems, managing stakeholder relationships, and bringing together insights from different disciplines to create solutions that AI alone cannot deliver.” Such expectations are starting to show up in the hiring landscape in Malaysia, with AI or digital tools becoming more common in the workplace. Randstad Malaysia associate director, emerging technology recruitment Dylan Long sees a clear shift in Malaysia’s hiring landscape, where employers are increasingly prioritising talent who are adept in AI and digital tools. “This trend is no longer confined to specialised tech departments; instead, having basic knowledge and practical experience with AI has rapidly evolved into a fundamental, baseline requirement for almost any professional role. There is an immense demand for individuals who demonstrate high digital agility,” Long says. He adds that a proactive willingness to embrace self-directed learning and integrate AI into one’s routine work has become a powerful, highly attractive differentiator in the current market. Statistics from Jobstreet confirm this change in the hiring landscape. According to Lam, the recruitment agency’s data shows that 70% of employers factor AI knowledge into hiring decisions, while one in three treat AI capability as a core hiring requirement. At the same time, demand for dedicated AI hiring is also increasing rapidly, notes Lam. AI-labelled job ads grew by 131% year on year in 2025. In 1H2026, the number of AI-labelled job ads was already 24% higher than the total for the whole of 2025, he says. One question that has often been raised is whether junior hiring will be reduced as a result of AI proliferation. A Gartner Inc survey carried out late last year found that 22% of chief human resources officers in the US reported that at least one business leader in their organisation has stopped hiring for entry-level roles as a result of AI automation. Some argue that removing the routine or repetitive tasks traditionally assigned to junior staff — often a training ground for developing judgement and gaining crucial experience — could ultimately hurt organisations by weakening their future talent pipeline. According to Soo Hoo, however, PwC’s global research shows that the bar is now higher for junior talent, with emotional quotient, judgement and leadership skills — qualities normally expected of senior hires — being prioritised. “Organisations will need to rethink how early-career talent is developed, including creating new pathways through which early-career employees can learn through application and experience,” he says. “Traditional apprenticeship models built largely around repetitive tasks may need to evolve into more structured experiences that accelerate the development of these broader capabilities.” Sufficient AI talent in Malaysia? While employers today want workers who can use AI in ways that help create value, there is also a need for AI developer roles in the country, notes Soo Hoo. “Malaysia needs to strengthen both the depth and breadth of its AI talent base. Findings from our 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer indicate that AI-related roles in Malaysia are currently concentrated in roles that apply AI in business functions (AI user roles) rather than roles focused on developing core AI technologies (AI developer roles),” he says. Soo Hoo cautions that the pipeline of specialised AI talent in Malaysia may not be sustainable for the country’s long-term ambitions, given the pace at which AI is evolving. “Malaysia needs both AI user and AI developer roles in our journey towards realising our AI Nation 2030 aspirations. We need to expand the pool of highly specialised engineers, data scientists and technical experts who can develop and commercialise homegrown digital innovation. At the same time, we must equip workers across sectors with AI literacy, applied skills and judgement to use these technologies productively and responsibly,” he explains. Having said that, every paradigm change will have its drawbacks. Human resources practitioners are reporting that, because of the speed at which the AI world is moving, employees are starting to experience AI fatigue, or “AI brain fry”, as they try to keep pace with the changes. “Companies need to think about the pace at which and direction in which they are adopting AI in their systems and processes. AI fatigue is a real issue and it’s not because employees are not eager to learn. This could result in a decrease, instead of an increase, in efficiency and productivity,” says an HR practitioner. A human resources director with a local company says some employees might not want to go down the AI rabbit hole. “We have reskilling programmes where we reassign certain affected roles to other areas in the company. But some of our employees, typically those who are closer to retirement, say they would rather opt for an early retirement plan, instead of reskilling,” notes the director. State of the labour market Minister of Economic Affairs Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said last Friday that a total of 68,177 workers lost their jobs from January to Sept 16, representing an increase of 15,196 over the same period last year. A recent report on the Social Security Organisation’s Employment Insurance Scheme (EIS) shows that professionals, managers, executives and technicians was the occupation category that saw the highest retrenchment rate, at 51% of the total loss of employment (LOE) benefit applications. It is not a new phenomenon, however, and has been in line with the data from 2021 to 2025. While some have attributed the higher retrenchment numbers partly to the increased adoption of AI or automation in companies, Maybank Investment Bank group chief economist Suhaimi Illias says it is still too early to determine the extent to which AI is driving retrenchments. He points out that Malaysia’s level of AI adoption, compared to other countries around the world, is still moderate. Citing the Microsoft AI Economy Institute’s Global AI Diffusion Scoring, he highlights that Malaysia ranked 51 out of 147 countries, with AI users accounting for 21.8% of the working-age population as at 1Q2026. Countries ranked among the top 20 have AI adoption rates ranging from more than 30% to 70%. “There are also other factors behind the higher share of skilled-worker retrenchments. Voluntary/Mutual Separation Schemes or Early Retirement Planning (VSS/MSS/ERP) have consistently ranked among the top three reasons for retrenchments and were the leading reason between 2023 and 2025. Higher-skilled employees may be more inclined to participate in such schemes, given attractive payouts,” Suhaimi says. He adds that the spike in total retrenchments may also reflect companies managing rising cost pressures through headcount reductions. This year, while the Consumer Price Index has remained moderate at 1.9% y-o-y in June, from 1.4% in February, the Producer Price Index has seen a spike to 9.2% y-o-y, from -3.4%, implying that companies have not passed down much of their higher cost to consumers so far. Interestingly, the country’s unemployment rate has held steady around 3% despite rising retrenchments. Suhaimi explains that because job placements continue to outpace layoffs, the economy is still net-positive for job creation. In 1H2026, placements reached 74,874, significantly higher than the 47,030 retrenchments. The way forward for employees With 620,000 jobs in Malaysia expected to be reshaped by AI, digitalisation and the green economy over the next three to five years, Jobstreet’s Lam warns that early-career professionals must learn to use these technologies both practically and responsibly. “AI literacy should increasingly be treated as a baseline capability,” he adds. Still, being literate in digital tools alone is not enough. Randstad’s Long points out the younger generation are naturally adept at using and eager to adopt new technology, but global employers still prefer “job-ready” candidates who have practical experience. “New graduates can prepare by actively seeking out structured internships, graduate trainee programmes, and on-the-job training opportunities that offer direct exposure to complex, real-world projects,” he says. “In fact, according to the Randstad 2026 Job Market Outlook and Salary Guide report, continuous learning has become such a non-negotiable for long-term career security that 56% of Gen Z talent in Malaysia would outright reject a job offer if it did not provide clear learning and development pathways to future-proof their skills.” Meanwhile, Long notes that mid- to late-career professionals must future-proof themselves by blending their vast experience with modern technological efficiency. Ultimately, Lam concludes, today’s workforce — regardless of seniority — should strive to work with AI while sharpening the human and commercial skills that technology cannot easily replicate. title: 'Ex-secretary to PM's graft case: Temporary passport release for Shamsul Iskandar
body: 'Ex-secretary to PM's graft case: Temporary passport release for Shamsul Iskandar KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin, a former senior political secretary to the prime minister, has obtained the Sessions Court’s approval for the temporary release of his international passport to enable him to attend several overseas programmes this month. The passport had been surrendered to the court as an additional bail condition after he was charged with five counts of corruption. According to his supporting affidavit obtained by the media, Shamsul Iskandar applied for the permanent return of his passport to facilitate overseas travel in connection with his duties. He said he intends to travel to Frankfurt, Germany, to attend the Frankfurt Book Fair organised by Rex Education from Oct 7 to Nov 11. “Based on my involvement with the Madani Community Leadership Academy, my participation in the book fair aims to foster synergy between organisations and provide mutual benefits to both entities. “Therefore, this participation will provide valuable international exposure to support and strengthen ongoing grassroots initiatives aimed at empowering civil society in line with the Madani principles, particularly through the promotion of literacy, leadership and knowledge,” he said in the affidavit. Shamsul Iskandar also said he had registered to attend the fifth AlBaraka Summit, themed Ethics in Action: Rebuilding Foundations and Advancing the Global Impact of the Islamic Economy, in London scheduled for Oct 13 and 14. He said the summit aims to strengthen ethical foundations for Islamic financial and non-financial institutions, governance systems and market practices. Shamsul Iskandar also said he plans to attend programmes in Ireland, as well as Bosnia and Herzegovina, in November and December. During Monday's proceedings, lawyer Yusmadi Yusoff, representing Shamsul Iskandar, told Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin that his client had filed an application on Sept 30 for the permanent return of his passport. He also sought its temporary release to enable Shamsul Iskandar to attend programmes in Frankfurt and London this month. title: 'Mesiniaga Wins Two-year RM32.3m Contract Extension From Customs Dept
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Mesiniaga Bhd (KL:MSNIAGA) has won a RM32.3 million contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider’s earlier MYGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. The new extension, which takes effect from Oct 16, 2026, will run until Oct 15, 2028. According to the company’s bourse filing on Tuesday, the agreement does not include an automatic renewal clause. The MyGST system is the Customs Department's legacy online system for administering goods and services tax (GST), which was Malaysia's broad-based consumption tax from April 2015 until its abolition in September 2018. Malaysia's current sales and service tax (SST) system is administered through MySST, but MyGST system remains in operation as the agency maintains it to support other tax administrative matters, fulfil statutory/legal requirements and work procedures. Mesiniaga said the contract is expected to contribute positively to the group’s earnings and net assets for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026) and subsequent periods until completion. For the first half of FY2026, Mesiniaga’s net loss narrowed to RM0.95 million from RM2.13 million in the previous period, while revenue was up by 22.4% to RM113.2 million. The group said it saw higher revenue from projects and services deliveries. Shares of Mesiniaga were down by one sen or 0.9% to RM1.16 at market close on Tuesday, giving the group a market value of RM70.1 million. title: 'AHB kekalkan agihan pendapatan lima sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan 2026
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan agihan pendapatan sebanyak lima sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 Sept 2026, yang memberi manfaat kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB) bersama pengurus dananya, PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM), berkata agihan pendapatan akhir bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 Sept 2026 adalah sebanyak 2.1 sen seunit, dengan tambahan agihan bonus sebanyak 0.4 sen seunit yang diisytiharkan PHB selaku penaja dana itu. “Edaran bonus itu akan diberikan bagi 1,000,000 unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit. Dengan mengambil kira agihan pendapatan interim sebanyak 2.5 sen seunit yang diisytiharkan pada April 2026, jumlah keseluruhan agihan pendapatan AHB bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 2026 adalah lima sen seunit,” menurut kenyataan itu. PHB berkata sebanyak RM120.13 juta akan diagihkan pada pusingan akhir, menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan agihan tahunan sebanyak RM236.41 juta. Pengarah Urusan kumpulan PHB Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad berkata agihan pendapatan bagi setahun penuh itu mencerminkan daya tahan AHB yang berterusan serta kekuatan portfolio hartanah asasnya, disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset dan pelaburan yang berdisiplin oleh PHB. “Prestasi AHB tahun ini membuktikan komitmen kami untuk terus memberikan pulangan yang kompetitif kepada pemegang unit. “Pada masa sama, kami kekal memberi tumpuan kepada usaha memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan pelabur Bumiputera menerusi pengurusan modal yang berhemat, strategi pelaburan yang dinamik serta pengoptimuman portfolio yang berterusan bagi memastikan pertumbuhan yang mampan danpenciptaan nilai jangka panjang,” katanya. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PHBAM Zulkifli Ishak berkata pengurus dana itu kekal fokus menguruskan AHB secara bertanggungjawab bagi memastikan dana berkenaan terus menjadi pilihan pelaburan yang mudah diakses oleh pelabur Bumiputera. PHB berkata agihan pendapatan itu akan dibayar dalam bentuk unit AHB yang dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun AHB pemegang unit selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Okt 2026. Agihan tersebut akan dilaburkan semula secara automatik, sekali gus membolehkan pemegang unit menambah pegangan unit serta berpotensi menikmati kesan pengkompaunan dalam jangka panjang. “Pelabur Bumiputera yang ingin melanggan AHB boleh berbuat demikian pada harga tetap RM1 seunit, dengan pelaburan minimum RM100 dan maksimum RM1 juta. “Langganan boleh dibuat melalui cawangan pengedar yang sah di seluruh negara, iaitu Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), AmBank Bhd, AmBank Islamic Bhd, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd dan Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd,” katanya. – BERNAMA

title: 'Bursa Malaysia dibuka rendah berikutan hasil bon AS lebih tinggi, ketegangan Asia Barat
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia dibuka rendah pada Khamis, menjejaki prestasi bercampur-campur Wall Street berikutan hasil bon Perbendaharaan AS yang lebih tinggi serta ketegangan berterusan di Asia Barat menjejaskan minat belian.  Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) susut 3.74 mata atau 0.22 peratus kepada 1,647.43 daripada paras 1,651.17 ketika ditutup pada Rabu.  Indeks penanda aras itu dibuka 1.30 mata lebih rendah pada 1,649.87.  Di pasaran meluas, kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung sebanyak 200 berbanding 142, manakala 307 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,124 kaunter tidak diniagakan dan 12 kaunter digantung.  Jumlah dagangan sebanyak 246.59 juta saham bernilai RM118.14 juta.  Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata Wall Street ditutup bercampur-campur apabila inflasi yang lebih rendah mengurangkan jangkaan terhadap satu lagi kenaikan kadar faedah oleh Rizab Persekutuan AS, meskipun hasil bon yang kekal tinggi terus menjejaskan sentimen.  Di peringkat domestik, beliau berkata indeks penanda aras pasaran mungkin cenderung diniagakan berhati-hati, dengan sentimen keseluruhan pasaran yang lemah dan jualan asing baru-baru ini menunjukkan pelabur terus mengambil pendekatan berhati-hati.  “Justeru, bagi hari ini, kami menjangkakan indeks kekal dalam mod pengukuhan dalam julat 1,640-1,660, dengan aktiviti pembelian ketika harga rendah dijangka mengehadkan penurunan,” katanya kepada Bernama.  Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Maybank dan IHH Healthcare masing-masing tidak berubah pada RM9.90 dan RM7.83. Public Bank susut tiga sen kepada RM4.67, CIMB berkurangan satu sen kepada RM7.78 dan Tenaga Nasional turun dua sen kepada RM12.94.  Dalam dagangan aktif, saham yang baru disenaraikan di Pasaran ACE, GB Bond susut setengah sen kepada 24.5 sen, manakala VS Industry tidak berubah pada 28 sen. Astro Malaysia menambah setengah sen kepada enam sen, Jaks Resources meningkat satu sen kepada 21.5 sen dan Divfex menokok dua sen kepada 11 sen.  Antara kaunter untung utama, Keck Seng meningkat 11 sen kepada RM5.14 dan Petron Malaysia menambah tujuh sen kepada RM3.47. Hengyuan Refining dan Spritzer masing-masing naik enam sen kepada RM3.62 dan RM3.67, manakala Jati Tinggi mengukuh lima sen kepada RM1.44.  Kuala Lumpur Kepong mendahului kaunter rugi apabila susut 18 sen kepada RM22.02. UWC pula berkurangan 15 sen kepada RM6.92, manakala Insights Analytics dan MISC masing-masing turun sembilan sen kepada RM1.20 dan RM7.55. Petronas Dagangan susut lapan sen kepada RM19.20.  Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 susut 42.26 mata kepada 17,532.41, Indeks FBM Emas berkurangan 26.32 mata kepada 12,265.69, manakala Indeks FBM Top 100 turun 27.82 mata kepada 12,056.62.  Indeks FBM Emas Shariah susut 22.09 mata kepada 12,154.26, manakala Indeks FBM ACE berkurangan 6.31 mata kepada 5,527.97.  Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian susut 0.10 mata kepada 180.31, manakala Indeks Tenaga meningkat 1.41 mata kepada 847.11. Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan turun 27.47 mata kepada 19,189.02, manakala Indeks Perladangan merosot 33.34 mata kepada 9,163.33.- Bernama

body: 'This article first appeared in Capital, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026 Banking POSITIVE BIMB SECURITIES RESEARCH (Sept 22): Global bond markets experienced higher yields amid tighter US monetary policy and higher-for-longer interest rates. On Sept 16, the Federal Open Market Committee raised the federal funds rate target by 25 basis points (bps) to 3.75%-4.00%. The 10-year Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yield stands at 4.15% as at Sept 21, and remains elevated by historical standards but is still below the peak of 4.57% recorded in October 2022. According to our economist’s assessment, the 10-year MGS yield is expected to hover around the 4.0% level in the near term before gradually moderating towards the 3.75%-3.90% range by year end. Current yield levels appear to reflect market expectations of close to two policy rate hikes in Malaysia. However, given our view that the Overnight Policy Rate will remain unchanged at 2.75% throughout 2026 and 2027, coupled with a contained domestic inflation outlook, the 10-year MGS yield is expected to ease from its current elevated level over time. Banks typically maintain an average securities portfolio duration of around five to six years, which is considered moderate rather than long term. As a result, their investment portfolios are generally less sensitive to interest rate movements and face lower interest rate risk compared with portfolios concentrated on longer-dated securities. The impact on fair value through other comprehensive income securities is expected to result in lower FVOCI reserves due to revaluation losses in 3Q26, as the 10-year MGS yield is likely to remain elevated in the near term. Nevertheless, the effect on ROE could be favourable, as the decline in shareholders’ funds reduces the equity base used in the ROE calculation. Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) (fair value: RM11.40), CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) (FV: RM8.75) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) (FV:RM8.50), which have exposure to the Singapore market, are likely to see improved net interest margins as the rise in three-month Singapore overnight rate change (SORA), in tandem with Fed rate hikes, lifts asset yields and helps mitigate fair value through profit and loss (FVTPL) mark-to-market losses in 3Q26. Banks’ funding profiles remain largely anchored by longer-tenor liabilities, including Medium Term Notes with maturities of at least two to three years, which help maintain robust Net Stable Funding Ratio positions and reduce near-term refinancing pressures. As such, banks are unlikely to rush into refinancing and are more likely to adopt a wait-and-see approach when considering the rollover of maturing papers. We do not expect deposit competition to become more aggressive from here, given that 1Q26 and 2Q26 had already witnessed intense competition, with banks offering promotional fixed deposit rates of up to 3.7%-3.8% for 10- to 12-month placements. Solarvest Holdings Bhd Target price: RM4.50 BUY AMINVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (Sept 21): We believe that Solarvest Holdings Bhd (KL:SLVEST) would benefit from the government’s CRESS Acceleration Package. Under the package, a System Access Charge (SAC) of 14 sen/kWh will be introduced. We think that the lower SAC would spur the rollout of CRESS projects, as under the previous CRESS scheme, the SAC were perceived as too high. The SAC under the previous CRESS were 20 sen/kWh for projects with battery systems and 40 sen/kWh for projects without battery systems. We reckon that battery and solar systems contracts are worth about RM3.5million/mw to RM4million/mw based on recently announced projects. There is incentive for data centres to do solar under the new CRESS. This is because the tariffs under the new CRESS package would come up to about 45 to 50 sen/kWh compared with their present electricity tariffs of 50 to 60 sen/kWh. Solarvest is bidding for 11,800mw worth of projects. Out of these, about 1,200mw are expected to come from battery projects. Gamuda Bhd Target price: RM5.42 BUY TA SECURITIES (Sept 22): Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA), via the Gamuda-BMD joint venture, has clinched the A$624 million (RM1.8 billion) Elizabeth Drive Upgrade — Mamre Road Upgrade Stage 2 Package from government agency Transport for New South Wales. Based on its 50% effective interest in the JV, Gamuda is entitled to roughly RM908 million in contract value. Given that the award also comes with cost-pass-through clauses, we believe this should limit Gamuda’s execution risk and exposure to volatile material prices. Based on the management-guided PBT margin of 5%, we estimate the project could generate approximately RM45.4 million in PBT over the contract period. Looking ahead, we expect Western Sydney’s rapid development to support sustained infrastructure spending, particularly across the road network. This should provide a healthy pipeline of replenishment opportunities for Gamuda. Gamuda’s FY2027 year-to-date new job wins have reached RM10.2 billion, lifting its unbilled construction order book to RM62.5 billion. We believe Gamuda’s near-term order book replenishment prospects remain healthy, with potential wins likely to come from data centre projects from new and repeat clients in Malaysia, renewable energy projects in Australia, particularly solar EPCCs (engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning) works, and railway infrastructure projects in Taiwan. QL Resources Bhd Target price: RM5.10 BUY HONG LEONG INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (Sept 23): QL Resources Bhd’s (KL:QL)’s 1QFY2027 marine products manufacturing (MPM) revenue rose 18.2% year on year while PBT jumped 51.5%, with management attributing the bulk of the circa RM30 million y-o-y earnings uplift to fishmeal driven by Peru’s lower catch quota and a temporary El Niño fishing ban. Peru, which supplies roughly a fifth of the world’s fishmeal, in August called off its main anchovy season having landed only 25% of an already reduced quota. That keeps global supply tight, and fishmeal prices in July were still running about 11% above where they averaged through QL’s 1QFY27. Grade C egg prices recovered from the low RM0.20s in April to May to RM0.33 by end-June and >RM0.40 at the farm gate by August We remain constructive on QL, given that MPM is delivering into a supply shock with further runway into FY27, and did so in a seasonally soft quarter with the stronger quarters still ahead. Clean energy under BM Greentech Bhd (KL:BMGREEN] now has a working commercial proof point inside QL’s own plant while Innofood will begin contributing from 2HFY28. Integrated livestock farming and convenience store chain segments have, in our view, both passed their respective troughs, with egg prices recovering off the April low and FamilyMart's top line turning after three quarters of decline.
