title: 'Ex-secretary to PM's Graft Case: Temporary Passport Release for Shamsul Iskandar
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin, a former senior political secretary to the prime minister, has obtained the Sessions Court’s approval for the temporary release of his international passport to enable him to attend several overseas programmes this month. The passport had been surrendered to the court as an additional bail condition after he was charged with five counts of corruption. According to his supporting affidavit obtained by the media, Shamsul Iskandar applied for the permanent return of his passport to facilitate overseas travel in connection with his duties. He said he intends to travel to Frankfurt, Germany, to attend the Frankfurt Book Fair organised by Rex Education from Oct 7 to Nov 11. “Based on my involvement with the Madani Community Leadership Academy, my participation in the book fair aims to foster synergy between organisations and provide mutual benefits to both entities. “Therefore, this participation will provide valuable international exposure to support and strengthen ongoing grassroots initiatives aimed at empowering civil society in line with the Madani principles, particularly through the promotion of literacy, leadership and knowledge,” he said in the affidavit. Shamsul Iskandar also said he had registered to attend the fifth AlBaraka Summit, themed Ethics in Action: Rebuilding Foundations and Advancing the Global Impact of the Islamic Economy, in London scheduled for Oct 13 and 14. He said the summit aims to strengthen ethical foundations for Islamic financial and non-financial institutions, governance systems and market practices. Shamsul Iskandar also said he plans to attend programmes in Ireland, as well as Bosnia and Herzegovina, in November and December. During Monday's proceedings, lawyer Yusmadi Yusoff, representing Shamsul Iskandar, told Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin that his client had filed an application on Sept 30 for the permanent return of his passport. He also sought its temporary release to enable Shamsul Iskandar to attend programmes in Frankfurt and London this month. Deputy public prosecutor Julaila Jamaludin objected to the application for the permanent return of the passport, saying the supporting documents consisted only of an invitation letter and that the discussions could be conducted online. However, she did not object to the application for its temporary release. Suzana subsequently allowed the temporary release of Shamsul Iskandar’s passport, effective from Monday, on condition that it be returned to the court on or before Oct 16. The court also ordered the prosecution to file an affidavit in reply to the application for the permanent return of the passport by Oct 19, with the decision on the application set for Dec 8. Shamsul Iskandar, 51, faces two charges of agreeing to accept RM140,000 in cash from businessman Tei Jiann Cheing, also known as Albert Tei, as an inducement to assist a company owned by Tei in obtaining approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah. He also faces two charges of obtaining furniture and electrical appliances worth RM14,580.03 and RM22,249 respectively, from Tei for the same purpose. The offences were allegedly committed at premises in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, and a hotel car park in Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin, as well as at Jalan P14A 1/1, Precinct 14, Putrajaya, between Nov 24, 2023, and March 5, 2024. In a separate charge, Shamsul Iskandar is accused of obtaining gratification amounting to RM64,924 from Tei, allegedly deposited into a CIMB Bank account belonging to Rahmalidya Buyong to cover the rental of a house in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, in exchange for assisting Tei's company in securing approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah. All five charges were brought under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 (Act 694) and are punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and a fine of at least five times the amount or value of the gratification, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction. title: 'Asteel names ex-IGP Razarudin chairman, Clifford Hii executive deputy chairman in board revamp
body: 'Asteel names ex-IGP Razarudin chairman, Clifford Hii executive deputy chairman in board revamp KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Asteel Group Bhd (KL:ASTEEL) has appointed former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid as independent non-executive chairman and new controlling shareholder Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong as executive deputy chairman. The boardroom reshuffle follows Clifford securing a 53.08% stake in Asteel at the closing of a mandatory offer on Monday via investment vehicle Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd. Clifford emerged as Asteel’s controlling shareholder in August with the acquisition of an initial 52.94% stake in the company via a RM20.75 million cash deal at 7.5 sen apiece. This triggered a mandatory offer for the remaining 47.06% stake in Asteel, also at 7.5 sen apiece. Clifford, 43, the son of the journalist-turned-businessman Tan Sri Clement Hii Chii Kok, who is the founder and executive chairman of property developer HCK Capital Group Bhd (KL:HCK) and group managing director and major shareholder of private education group SEG International. Clement is also the founder of Gambit Group Sdn Bhd, whose subsidiaries are involved in information technology services, investment, business management consultancy and is a registered digital asset custodian under the Securities Commission Malaysia. Clifford, a former non-independent, non-executive director at HCK Capital, has more than 20 years of experience in the education, property and financial technology sectors. He had held senior management and board positions covering corporate strategy, business development, corporate deals and investments, corporate governance and project management. Razarudin, 63, who is also independent non-executive chairman of Advancecon Holdings Bhd (KL:ADVCON), brings more than four decades of experience in national security and law enforcement. He was Malaysia’s 14th police chief until his retirement in June 2025. In separate filings, the steel manufacturer announced the appointment of Esther Teh Oun Pheng and Datuk Dr Lor Chee Leng as independent non-executive directors, while former executive chairman Tan Sri (Dr) Soh Thian Lai has been redesignated as executive director cum chairman emeritus. At the same time, non-independent non-executive director Christopher Hii Lu Ming, and independent non-executive directors Yan Ying Chieh, Khor Hun Nee and Wee Hiang Chyn have resigned, all citing personal reasons. Teh, 47, is head of internal audit and risk management at Usaha Tegas Sdn Bhd and an independent director of Nasdaq-listed OMS Energy Technologies Inc. She has more than 20 years of experience in internal and external audit, risk management, management consulting, shared-services implementation and operations and controllership. Her previous roles include group head of internal audit and compliance at Singapore-listed fintech company Silverlake Axis Ltd, head of risk management and assurance for group digital at Petroliam Nasional Bhd, and senior manager of management consulting at Accenture. Lor, 62, meanwhile, currently serves as an adviser to the Global ESG Leadership Organization and to Cambodia’s Ministry of Economy and Finance. He brings more than 35 years of experience in financial services, including banking transformation and strategy, corporate governance, risk management, credit oversight and consumer banking. His previous positions include independent director of Mizuho Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, chief executive officer and executive director of Canadia Bank PLC in Cambodia, group CEO of EON Bank Bhd, director of banking solutions at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, group head of consumer banking at RHB Bank Bhd and managing director of consumer banking at DBS Bank Ltd. At Tuesday's market close, Asteel shares rose a sen or 10.5% to 10.5 sen, valuing the group at RM50.9 million. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'Govt dividend receipts up 1.4% to RM39.55b in 2025 on higher BNM, Khazanah payouts — AG’s report
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The federal government received RM39.55 billion in dividends from its investments in 2025, up by 1.4% from RM39.01 billion a year earlier, as higher payouts from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and Khazanah Nasional Bhd outweighed lower receipts from other entities. The dividends came from 20 companies and two statutory bodies, compared with 21 companies and two statutory bodies in 2024. The increase was RM535.06 million compared to last year, according to the latest auditor general’s report released on Monday. Petroliam Nasional Bhd (PETRONAS) paid RM32 billion, unchanged from 2024. BNM paid RM5.25 billion, up from RM2.85 billion, an increase of RM2.4 billion or 84.2%. Khazanah's dividend doubled to RM2 billion from RM1 billion. Bank Simpanan Nasional paid RM25 million, down from RM52 million. Dividends from statutory bodies rose 81.8% to RM5.28 billion, while those from companies fell 5.1% to RM34.27 billion. In all, nine companies and one statutory body paid RM7.43 billion, against RM3.98 billion in 2024, an increase of RM3.45 billion or 86.7%. Twelve companies and one statutory body paid less compared to 2024, as three companies paid the same amount in both years. Piramid Pertama Sdn Bhd, which paid RM2.73 billion in 2024, made no payment in 2025. Dividends from Prokhas Sdn Bhd fell to RM5.6 million from RM56.24 million. Three companies, Perbadanan Nasional Bhd, Malaysia Debt Ventures Bhd and Malaysia Digital Economy Corp Sdn Bhd paid dividends in 2025 after paying none in 2024. title: 'IOI Properties Now Agrees to Buy Shenton House From Group CEO for S$1 and Settle S$217m Advance
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) has agreed to acquire Shenton 101 Pte Ltd, which owns Singapore's Shenton House, from its group chief executive officer and major shareholder Datuk Lee Yeow Seng for a nominal S$1.00. Under the deal, announced in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Thursday, IOI Properties will also settle S$217.06 million (RM696.43 million) worth of shareholder advances that Yeow Seng injected into Shenton 101 — the vehicle he incorporated to acquire the property. It will also consolidate the vehicle’s S$376.23 million borrowings into its accounts upon completion of the deal. Both figures were as of July 31, 2026. The transaction marks a reversal by the group’s non-interested directors, who rejected Yeow Seng's proposal to sell Shenton 101 to IOI Properties in August 2024, citing heavy capital commitments from several acquisitions at the time. Yeow Seng had proposed the sale to avoid a potential conflict of interest as he acquired the property in his personal capacity. To mitigate that, IOI Properties entered into project and property management agreements for the building instead. Shenton 101 won the tender to acquire Shenton House — a 25-storey strata-titled commercial development completed in the mid-1970s sitting on a 3,377-sq-metre site — for S$538 million in November 2023, with the purchase completed in June 2024. The acquisition, which will be funded through IOI Properties’ internal funds, does not require shareholder approval as it makes up just 3.79% of IOI Properties’ total assets, below the 5% materiality threshold under listing rules that would require a shareholder vote. However, it will require Bank Negara Malaysia's green light as the foreign currency investment exceeds the group's permissible limit, as well as consent from Shenton 101's lenders and the Singapore Land Authority. IOI Properties said the acquisition will allow it to strengthen its presence in Singapore's Marina Bay precinct and unlock synergies with its existing asset portfolio, given Shenton House's walking distance to IOI Central Boulevard Towers and the recently acquired Asia Square Tower 2. The group said it is revisiting the deal, on Yeow Seng's request, after its "circumstances and strategic position have evolved". It pointed out that IOI Central Boulevard Towers has achieved over 95% committed occupancy and is self-sustaining in debt servicing. It has also completed the acquisitions of the remaining 50.1% stake in Scottsdale Properties Pte Ltd — which owns South Beach Tower, South Beach Avenue and JW Marriott Hotel Singapore South Beach — and Asia Square Tower 2. It noted that its acquisitions in Malaysia have also continued to perform satisfactorily, and that shareholders had, on Sept 30, approved injecting W Kuala Lumpur hotel and Courtyard by Marriott Penang hotel into the upcoming IOI Properties REIT, in support of the group's capital recycling strategy. “Although the group’s gearing has increased, the increase is largely attributable to acquisitions of income-generating assets in Singapore that have enhanced the quality of the group's investment property portfolio and strengthened its position in key gateway markets,” it said. IOI Properties' net gearing, which stood at 0.70 times as at June 30, 2025, is projected to hit 1.03 times after its recent acquisitions and REIT listing, and rise further to 1.10 times following the Shenton 101 deal. The group plans to redevelop Shenton House into a 35-storey mixed-use landmark featuring 12 floors of Grade-A offices, a 10-storey luxury hotel (165 keys), a retail basement and three carpark levels. This will expand its total net lettable area from 20,276 sq metres (218,246 sq ft) to 36,528 sq metres (393,185 sq ft). The underlying land tenure, which has a remaining lease of about 42 years, is expected to be renewed to a fresh 99-year term. Savills appraised the market value of Shenton House as a redevelopment site at S$585 million, with an estimated gross development value of S$1.61 billion against total redevelopment costs of S$973.65 million. Maybank Investment Bank is the principal adviser for the exercise, which is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026. Although not mandated by listing rules, IOI Properties also appointed Affin Hwang Investment Bank as an independent adviser to advise non-interested directors on the deal's fairness and reasonableness. Yeow Seng and his brother Datuk Lee Yeow Chor, who is a non-independent non-executive director, are deemed interested parties and have abstained from all board deliberations and voting on the proposal. The Lee family's private vehicle, Vertical Capacity Sdn Bhd, holds a controlling 65.673% stake in IOI Properties, while Yeow Seng directly holds 3.768% and Yeow Chor has 0.012%. The Employees Provident Fund is the largest institutional shareholder in IOI Properties, with a 7.496% stake. Shares of IOI Properties closed six sen or 1.73% lower at RM3.40 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM18.72 billion. title: 'Passwords no longer supported: CIMB Bank only accepts biometrics or passcode for SecureTAC approvals from 19 September
body: 'CIMB Bank will officially phase out password verification for SecureTAC approvals on CIMB Clicks Web and online merchant transactions starting 19 September 2026.  Under this new security mandate, all web transfers and online card payments must be authenticated exclusively through the CIMB OCTO mobile app.  Users will now be required to verify their identity using biometrics such as Face ID and fingerprint scanning, or their custom 6 digit OCTO App passcode.  Why is CIMB removing password verification?  CIMB states that removing password verification within the OCTO app aims to strengthen security and protect accounts against unauthorised access and fraud.  In line with industry security standards, web transactions will no longer accept traditional account passwords for SecureTAC approvals.  Once the policy takes effect, every web purchase or Clicks Web transaction will strictly require Face ID, fingerprint scanning, or your personal 6 digit OCTO App passcode.  How online transaction approvals will work  Initiating a payment on Clicks Web or a merchant site will trigger a SecureTAC push notification to your primary phone.  Tapping the notification or manually opening the SecureTAC menu in the OCTO app displays the transaction details.  Upon selecting “Approve”, the app prompts for your phone security credentials, where a quick facial scan, fingerprint check, or your set OCTO App passcode completes the verification.  What happens if security is turned off?  For users who do not have biometrics or an in-app passcode enabled on the OCTO app, web transfers will fail.  You can still initiate a transaction on the web portal and receive the push notification on your phone.  However, selecting Approve in the app will trigger an immediate error stating that security is not set up, rejecting the payment until you configure biometrics or a passcode inside the OCTO app settings.  OCTO App passcode acts as the primary backup for biometrics  If your fingerprint scanner glitches or your front camera fails, your custom 6-digit OCTO App passcode serves as the primary fallback option.  This is the personal PIN configured directly inside the OCTO app settings rather than your phone screen lock or main Clicks password.  If you cancel the prompt or enter an incorrect passcode multiple times, the app displays an error message before closing and rejecting the web payment.  Account safety and self service troubleshooting  CIMB reassures customers that failed SecureTAC attempts will not lock your CIMB Clicks ID, nor will any funds be deducted from your account.  If a transaction fails, the recommended troubleshooting step is to ensure your OCTO app security settings are properly configured and retry the payment on Clicks Web.  The bank advises customers to contact their support centre only if approval issues persist after making a second attempt.

title: 'Maybank, Ageas meterai perjanjian ambil alih MAHB bernilai RM4.38 bilion
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR - Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) memeterai perjanjian jual beli saham (SPA) tanpa syarat dengan Ageas Insurance International NV yang berpangkalan di Belgium untuk mengambil alih baki 30.95 peratus kepentingan ekuiti dalam Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd (MAHB) dengan nilai RM4.83 bilion.  Dalam makluman kepada Bursa Malaysia hari ini, Maybank berkata perjanjian itu melibatkan pengambilalihan 78 juta saham MAHB daripada Ageas.  Kumpulan perbankan itu berkata SPA berkenaan ditandatangani hari ini selepas menerima kelulusan daripada Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) pada 1 Sept 2026, manakala balasan pembelian akan dibiayai sepenuhnya melalui dana yang dijana secara dalaman.  Maybank berkata cadangan pengambilalihan itu bertujuan membolehkannya memiliki MAHB sepenuhnya serta memberikan kumpulan itu fleksibiliti strategik yang lebih besar.  “Pengambilalihan itu juga bertujuan mengukuhkan kedudukan MAHB sebagai pemain insurans dan takaful nasional, menyokong pengembangan di seluruh Asia Tenggara, meningkatkan nilai jangka panjang yang mampan dan berdaya tahan bagi kumpulan Maybank, serta meningkatkan kecekapan pengurusan modal merentasi francais insurans dan takafulnya.  “Pemilikan penuh MAHB dijangka memberikan Maybank dan MAHB ketangkasan strategik yang lebih besar untuk mempercepat inovasi produk, memperluas penembusan bancassurance, mengembangkan penawaran takaful serta meningkatkan kecekapan modal dan operasi merentasi francais insurans dan takaful,” katanya.  Maybank berkata, sekiranya tiada keadaan tidak diduga, cadangan pengambilalihan itu dijangka selesai pada 11 Sept 2026.  Maybank Investment Bank Bhd dilantik sebagai penasihat utama, manakala Morgan Stanley Asia (Singapore) Pte dilantik sebagai penasihat kewangan antarabangsanya.  — BERNAMA

title: 'Restock Sambal Nyet Bilis, Khairul Aming Sekali Lagi Capai ‘Sales’ RM2 Juta
body: 'Sekilas  Khairul Aming berjaya mencatat jualan sebanyak RM2 juta untuk produk terbaharunya, Sambal Nyet Bilis. Beliau berkongsi pencapaian tersebut di Threads dengan memaparkan angka jualan RM2,181,558.73 sambil mengucapkan terima kasih kepada peminat. Jualan produk ini sebelum ini juga pernah mencapai RM2 juta dalam masa kurang dua minit semasa pelancaran di Menara Merdeka Maybank.  Pempengaruh dan usahawan, Khairul Aming sekali lagi mencatatkan pencapaian membanggakan apabila mencatat jualan sebanyak RM2 juta menerusi penjualan produk terbaharunya iaitu Sambal Nyet Bilis.  Menerusi perkongsian di Threads, Khairul Aming berkongsi foto dirinya sambil memegang komputer riba yang memaparkan angka sebanyak RM2,181,558.73.  Malah, anak jati Kelantan ini turut meluahkan rasa syukur selepas jualan tersebut berjaya mencapai angka yang memberangsangkan.  “Alhamdulillah kita capai jualan 2 juta ringgit untuk restock Sambal Bilis tadi  “Terima kasih guys,”kongsinya.  Perkongsian itu kemudiannya meraih perhatian ramai yang rata-ratanya menzahirkan ucapan tahniah buat Khairul Aming.  Sebelum ini, Khairul Aming mencatat jualan RM2 juta dalam masa kurang dua minit bagi produk terbaharunya itu melalui platform TikTok ketika pelancaran produk berkenaan di Menara Merdeka Maybank (sebelum ini dikenali sebagai Merdeka 118).

title: 'HLB Islamic Berjaya Lonjak Pendapatan Usahawan Berpendapatan Rendah Langkawi Sebanyak 94%
body: 'Kuala Lumpur, 23 September 2026 – Selaras dengan komitmen untuk memperkasakan ekosistem perantaraan berasaskan nilai (“Value-based Intermediation” atau “VBI”), HLB Islamic (atau “Bank”) telah menyalurkan pembiayaan sebanyak RM138,600 kepada perusahaan sosial SURI Inspirasi (“SURI”) di bawah kerangka iTEKAD Bank Negara Malaysia (“BNM”). Inisiatif ini secara langsung menyumbang kepada peningkatan purata pendapatan bulanan sebanyak 94% serta menjana jumlah pendapatan baharu melebihi RM14,000 bagi usahawan yang menyertai program “Sustainable Reliable Income” (“SRI”) anjuran SURI. Program SRI memperkasakan komuniti berpendapatan rendah untuk mengitar semula sisa fabrik menjadi barangan fesyen yang unik, yang secara langsung mewujudkan peluang pekerjaan dan memupuk semangat keusahawanan di samping mempromosikan fesyen sifar sisa serta pemerkasaan komuniti. Usahawan yang terlibat, yang majoritinya ibu tunggal berpendapatan rendah, telah menghasilkan 1,000 pasang pakaian seragam sekolah untuk pelajar di lima buah sekolah di Langkawi, sekali gus menjana penjimatan sebanyak RM30,000 bagi keluarga tempatan. HLB Islamic meraikan pencapaian ini menerusi penyerahan mesin jahit berkualiti tinggi kepada para usahawan yang terlibat, menandakan peralihan daripada pembelajaran di dalam bilik darjah kepada pemilikan perniagaan secara aktif. Menurut Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif HLB Islamic, “Visi kami tentang pengurusan kewangan berteraskan Hayat @ HLB Islamic, di mana pengurusan harta dilihat sebagai satu perjalanan yang bermula dengan Penciptaan Harta. Melalui kerjasama dengan SURI, kami menyediakan alat dan latihan asas yang diperlukan oleh komuniti untuk mencungkil potensi keusahawanan mereka. Kami berharap usaha ini akan menjadi pemangkin kepada perjalanan pembinaan kekayaan yang berterusan ke arah kebebasan kewangan yang bakal memperkayakan komuniti untuk generasi akan datang.” Kejayaan ini menandakan satu pencapaian penting dalam kerjasama berterusan antara HLB Islamic dan SURI, yang mula menyertai ekosistem Bank ini sebagai peserta inisiatif HLB Jumpstart. Diperkenalkan bagi memupuk perusahaan sosial Malaysia yang berimpak tinggi menerusi bimbingan komersial, penjenamaan, serta pembinaan kapasiti digital, HLB Jumpstart telah menyediakan kerangka awal kepada SURI untuk memperluas operasinya. Hal ini membuktikan strategi jangka panjang Bank dalam memupuk usaha sosial menjadi rakan pelaksana berdikari yang mampu memberikan impak yang lebih meluas. title: 'AAGB Rejects Bailout Talk After 64% Share Rout; Analysts Retain Bullish Calls with Over 100% Upside
body: 'AirAsia Group has rejected reports questioning its financial solvency, saying at a press conference chaired by co-founder and adviser Tony Fernandes that it had neither sought nor received a government bailout. It also denied that aircraft had been repossessed over unpaid leases or that the government had approached other airlines to take over its routes. Management said its fundraising efforts were primarily intended to refinance expensive debt rather than raise rescue capital. The clarification came after AirAsia Group’s share price fell 46% over one month, 61% over three months and 64% over the past year. Maybank Investment Bank analyst Yin Shao Yang maintained his “Buy” rating but cut the target price by 33% to RM1.22 in a report today, still implying 126% upside. Yin remains positive because he views AirAsia Group’s valuation as distressed. Its R M1.8 billion market capitalisation is below the approximately RM2 billion combined trough valuation of AirAsia Group and Capital A during the Covid-19 period, despite the airline currently being operational. The stock also trades at 1.9 times 2027E price-to-book value, below the 2.0-times average of global low-cost carriers. Successful refinancing could provide further support by generating approximately RM200 million in annual interest savings. Nevertheless, Yin’s “Buy” call depends heavily on jet-fuel prices moderating to US$115 per barrel in 2027E. He widened his 2026E core net-loss forecast to RM797.9 million from RM335.0 million, but expects earnings to rebound to core net profits of RM730.9 million in 2027E and RM772.1 million in 2028E. Yin estimates that every US$1-per-barrel increase in jet-fuel prices would reduce the group’s earnings by approximately RM75 million. Yin Shao Yang, currently ranked No.6 among 44 analysts covering the consumer products & services sector on StockTipRatings (based on data since 2023), holds a 65% expert rating with a 7% average return and a 65% success rate across the stocks he covered over a 1-year period following his calls. Separately, Capital A’s Move Digital has proposed a court-supervised scheme to restructure approximately RM292 million in net liabilities through a potential BigPay divestment, the sale of its Tune Protect stake and recovery of related-party receivables. Despite Capital A falling 47.2% over three months, Public Investment Bank analyst Denny Oh maintained “Outperform” with a RM0.55 target price, implying 124% upside. He expects no material impact from the exercise and believes BigPay’s eventual deconsolidation could strengthen Capital A’s balance sheet, although the scheme remains subject to creditor engagement and court approval. According to StockTipRatings, Denny Oh currently ranks No.6 among 12 analysts at Public Investment Bank, with a 41% expert rating and a 36% success rate. As of 12:06 p.m. on September 21, AirAsia Group's share price rose 1.9% to RM0.54, while Capital A rose 4.3% to RM0.245. title: 'DNB raises RM5.2bil from Islamic loan for next 5G phase
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, one of the largest syndicated loan facilities arranged for an unlisted Malaysian company. DNB said the financing comes as it prepares for the next phase of Malaysia's dual 5G network framework. The financing is expected to support the planned exit of the Ministry of Finance Inc (MoF Inc) as an ordinary shareholder, it said today. It will also facilitate the transition to equal ownership among DNB's mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders - CelcomDigi Bhd through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd - expected in early fourth quarter of this year. MoF Inc will retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and oversee key strategic matters. The RM5.2 billion facility also refinances DNB's government guarantee revolving credit facility, which expired on Sept 29. It provides the company with a long-term funding structure for its operations and network investments. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger. AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd were joint mandated lead arrangers. AmInvestment Bank also acted as financial adviser to DNB. The financing comes as DNB receives the full 100MHz of the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz (F0) spectrum and converts its entire 240MHz spectrum holding to a spectrum assignment. The assignment, issued by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, takes effect today. DNB said the expanded spectrum holding would increase network capacity, efficiency and performance, supporting faster speeds, lower latency and improved customer experience. It would also enable the deployment of technologies such as Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and artificial intelligence-driven network capabilities. DNB chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said the successful financing reflected confidence in the company's business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia's digital economy. "This financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate on its own, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and leverage our expanded spectrum assets," he said. Azman said DNB remained committed to providing digital infrastructure as Malaysia moved towards a dual network framework. "With strong financing, enhanced spectrum resources and a proven nationwide 5G platform, DNB is well positioned to support the government's AI Nation aspirations and help power Malaysia's next phase of digital growth," he said. DNB said the financing and spectrum assignment would strengthen its ability to improve network quality and resilience, cater to future demand and support Malaysia's digital economy ambitions.

title: 'El Niño could worsen Malaysia’s power, water stress, says CIMB Securities
body: 'El Niño could worsen Malaysia’s power, water stress, says CIMB Securities KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 7): Hotter and drier conditions from El Niño could put greater pressure on Malaysia’s electricity and water systems into 2027, according to CIMB Securities. The research house said El Niño is expected to persist into early 2027 and peak between March and May, potentially lifting electricity demand for cooling while worsening water shortages. It said Malaysia is particularly exposed as electricity demand is already rising, while about 37% of treated water is lost through non-revenue water (NRW). “Hotter and drier conditions could further strain both systems, strengthening the need for cooling efficiency, water conservation, and better infrastructure management,” CIMB said. Malaysia’s peak electricity demand is projected to increase to 33.5 gigawatts (GW) by 2035 from 21.3GW in 2026, while data centres could account for 31% of Peninsular Malaysia’s electricity demand by then. CIMB said hotter weather could further increase cooling demand across commercial buildings, industrial facilities and data centres, adding to the country’s underlying electricity load growth. On the water side, Malaysia’s NRW rate remained high at 37.1% in 2024, meaning more than one-third of treated water was lost before reaching consumers. The losses are estimated to cost more than RM2 billion annually. Water stress is already visible in some areas, with two of the 49 dams monitored nationwide at critical levels as at Aug 31, namely the Muda Dam in Kedah and Sungai Pagar Dam in Labuan. CIMB said the government’s RM2.5 billion National NRW Programme and RM1.7 billion allocation under the 13th Malaysia Plan to replace about 1,800km of critical water pipes should support efforts to improve water efficiency. The research house named KJTS Group Bhd (KL:KJTS) and Insights Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB) as its preferred beneficiaries of the theme. KJTS offers direct exposure to rising cooling demand through its cooling energy and energy-efficiency businesses, while Insights Analytics provides digital water solutions including leak detection, pressure management and smart metering. CIMB maintained “buy” calls on both companies, with target prices of RM1.35 for KJTS and RM1.95 for Insights Analytics. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'MOF Backs AirAsia Fundraising Drive Led by Alton, Sources Say
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Global aviation advisory firm Alton Aviation Consultancy has launched a campaign to help low-cost carrier AirAsia Group Bhd (KL:AAGB) raise as much as US$1 billion (RM4.1 billion), according to people familiar with the matter. The fundraising effort is backed by Malaysia’s Ministry of Finance (MOF), which is helping Alton attract lenders and investors as banks and other financiers become more selective in funding airlines amid tougher market conditions and surging jet fuel prices, the sources told The Edge. AirAsia has reportedly said it is seeking as much as US$1 billion primarily to support debt restructuring, refinancing, balance sheet consolidation, with the rest for operational needs. The move follows the MOF’s appointment of Alton to assess AirAsia’s funding requirements. The Edge, in its Aug 24 weekly, reported that the specialist advisory firm had been engaged to help the airline secure the proposed US$1 billion financing from international debt markets. title: 'Life Water Poised for Further Growth as Capacity and Distribution Expand
body: 'Life Water Berhad (“Life Water”, Bursa: LWSABAH, 5328) is positioned for continued growth, backed by spare production capacity, an expanding distribution network in Sabah and rising demand for its bottled water and carbonated drinks. The Sabah-based beverage maker reported a 19.9% increase in revenue to RM207.31 million for the financial year ended 30 June 2026, while net profit grew 23.8% to RM37.15 million. Momentum strengthened towards the year-end, with fourth-quarter revenue up 28% year on year to RM57.01 million and net profit up 21% to RM10.95 million. The growth was driven by higher drinking water sales volumes, a price revision implemented in May 2026, seasonally stronger demand during hot weather and wider distribution. Gross margin reached 49.3% in the second quarter, supported by better operational efficiency and lower raw material costs. Life Water is the leading bottled water and carbonated drinks brand in Sabah and held about 11% of Malaysia’s bottled water market at the time of its Main Market listing in November 2024. Since then, its share price has risen from the IPO price of RM0.65 to around RM1.66, giving it a market capitalisation of about RM785 million. A key factor behind the group’s growth outlook is its available capacity. Following new production lines funded by its IPO, including the expansion of the Sandakan Sibuga Plant 1 completed in June 2025, annual drinking water capacity stands at about 626 million litres, with utilisation of around 60%. This allows the group to meet higher demand without major new investment. The group is also investing in reaching more customers. Its truck fleet has grown from 70 to 90 units, and new distribution centres are being established in Tawau, Lahad Datu and Keningau, extending coverage to Sabah’s east coast and interior. In December 2025, Life Water began supplying Sabah’s largest mini-market chain, which operates about 280 outlets. Its products are also included in the government’s Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) programme. External conditions are supportive. Visit Malaysia Year 2026 is drawing more visitors to Sabah, lifting demand from hotels, food service outlets and retailers, while bottled water demand during the dry season typically runs about 30% above normal. Beyond Sabah, the group has been building its presence in Sarawak and Brunei through local distributors. CIMB Securities has a Buy call on Life Water with a target price of RM2.05, and forecasts core net profit to grow at a compound annual rate of 22.9% from FY2025 to FY2028.

title: 'KLIA T2 Retail Occupancy Holds Steady Despite Airline Capacity Cuts
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 29): Visitors walking through Kuala Lumpur International Airport's Terminal 2 (KLIA T2) will notice hoardings — temporary boards and barricades put up around shops that are empty or under renovation — at several areas of its retail section. While these appear just as airlines trim flight capacity to counter soaring fuel costs, the boarded-up spaces do not necessarily signal a broader downturn in the terminal's retail performance. Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB), which operates KLIA and 38 other airports in the country, said tenant occupancy at KLIA T2 remained resilient despite a decline in passenger traffic. Commercial occupancy stood at 93% currently, up from 92% a year earlier. “Some of the hoardings currently visible within the terminal are part of a planned reconfiguration of space to improve passenger processing and circulation,” MAHB said in an email response to questions from The Edge Malaysia. The airport operator said some commercial areas were being repurposed for this purpose, with several outlets in the affected areas scheduled to be progressively phased out by the end of the year. MAHB declined to disclose tenant level sales or passenger spending, citing commercial sensitivity. It said commercial performance depended on factors beyond passenger volumes, including passenger profiles, outlet locations, retail categories and the performance of individual businesses. The clarification comes as airlines operating from KLIA T2 contend with a sharp rise in fuel costs and weaker capacity on some routes since the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February. Global average jet fuel prices reached US$194.90 per barrel in the week ended Sept 18 — up 116.5% from a year earlier — according to data from Platts and S&P Global. Airlines have been particularly exposed to the increase because fuel typically accounts for between 30% and 50% of their operating costs. Budget carriers such as AirAsia Group Bhd (KL:AAGB) and Batik Air Malaysia, which remain largely unhedged, have been hit by the volatility in the jet fuel market. In response, some airlines have cut capacity by as much as 30% since April to limit fuel consumption and contain costs. AirAsia is the largest airline tenant at KLIA T2. Other carriers operating from the terminal include Scoot, Spring Airlines, Cebu Pacific Airways, Lucky Air, Qingdao Airlines and Shandong Airlines. On Sept 18, AirAsia said it had reduced capacity by 20% to 25% in the third quarter, traditionally a weaker travel period. It expects to restore capacity towards pre-Iran war levels in the fourth quarter, when year-end travel demand typically strengthens. The impact of the capacity cuts have been reflected in KLIA T2's footfall. While total passenger traffic across KLIA rose 2.1% year-on-year to 41.95 million between January and August this year, the headline growth masks a clear divergence between its two terminals. Traffic at Terminal 1 climbed roughly 8% y-o-y to 24.46 million passengers, but T2 saw numbers fall 5% y-o-y to 17.48 million over the same period. Still, MAHB said traffic had begun to recover from June. Total KLIA passenger movements increased from 4.7 million in June to five million in July and 5.2 million in August, with both terminals recording improvements. At T2, passenger numbers rose from 1.83 million in June to 1.86 million in July, and 1.98 million in August. “While T2 traffic remains below the corresponding period in 2025, the recent trend shows a gradual recovery following the capacity reductions experienced during the middle of the year,” MAHB said. The airport operator said it would continue to monitor airline capacity, passenger traffic and commercial performance. It added that the recent recovery in passenger movements provides a more balanced picture of conditions at both KLIA terminals than the weaker traffic figures recorded earlier in the year. For airlines, however, fuel remains a significant pressure point. In a Sept 21 report, Maybank Investment Bank Research estimated that every US$1 increase in the price of jet fuel could reduce AirAsia’s earnings by RM75 million. AirAsia shares closed half a sen or 0.94% lower at 52.5 sen on Monday, valuing the group at RM1.76 billion. The stock has fallen about 70% since the start of the year. title: 'Food Waste Forms Nearly 40% of Nation’s Daily Solid Waste, Says Minister
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Nearly 40% of the total 40,000 metric tonnes of solid waste generated in the country daily consists of food waste, according to Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. He said efforts to address this waste issue require the cooperation of all parties through a "whole-of-nation approach" involving both businesses and consumers to collectively change their attitudes and practices. “This is a form of waste. Food waste is not a crime, but it is a sin. It is a grave sin when edible food is simply thrown away,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat Monday. Nga said this when replying a question from Datuk Mumtaz Md Nawi (PN-Tumpat) regarding the latest developments in efforts to reduce waste sent to landfills and to increase recycling rates. Meanwhile, he expressed confidence that the ministry would achieve its target of exceeding a 40% recycling rate by the end of this year. Nga noted that under the "Trash to Cash" recycling programme, the total collection of recyclable materials between January and August exceeded 7.86 million kilogrammes (kg), with a sales value of over RM2.85 million. “Secondly, the zero-waste community initiative involving the establishment of 17 active zero-waste community centres during the same period has collected over 111,504kg of recyclable materials,” he said. Additionally, Nga said a school-based recycling competition, involving 1,680 schools, successfully collected 4.95 million kilogrammes of recyclable materials, which were sold for RM2.98 million. “Based on calculations of the total collected from 2018 to last year, we managed to gather nearly 20 million kilogrammes of recyclable items, generating proceeds exceeding RM10.22 million,” he said. Responding to a supplementary question from Mumtaz regarding the specific controls and enforcement actions implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government concerning cable theft including penalties imposed on third parties or buyers, he said the Cabinet views this issue seriously. “We constantly collaborate and engage with the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN), including examining the need to amend relevant laws to ensure harsher penalties are imposed on cable theft offenders in the country. “There have been several instances where LRT (Light Rail Transit) operations were disrupted due to cable theft by syndicates; therefore, this matter (amending laws for heavier penalties) is crucial to ensuring we continue to safeguard public safety and the well-being of the people,” he said. title: 'Bjak Founder Weighs IPO as Malaysian Insurtech Expands Abroad
body: '(Dec 16): Bjak Sdn Bhd, Malaysia’s largest online insurance aggregator, is mulling an initial public offering (IPO) within the next two years as it seeks to enter Europe. Bjak is eyeing new markets in Spain and Germany in 2026 following its recent expansion in Japan, Taiwan and Thailand, Wei Low, the firm’s founder said in his first-ever media interview. The firm’s gross written premiums increased 20% to 30% this year and are set to grow at a faster pace in the future as Bjak expands into new markets, the 36-year-old told Bloomberg News. The business has been profitable since its inception in 2019 and has “very minimal” debt, he said, declining to disclose further financial details. “We are still very young as a company,” Low said. “If you look at our other peers in other markets that are large, in China or the UK, it takes about 20 years to really maximise the potential or increase the penetration.” The IPO will help fund further overseas expansion and provide employees with liquidity through stock grants. Bjak is shifting its focus to Spain and Germany, which have well-established auto insurance markets, Low said. Low plans to double his team across the world by the end of 2026 from almost 200 people currently. The success of Ant Group Co, the operator of China’s ubiquitous financial services app Alipay, inspired Low to start Bjak in 2019. While insurance technology is well established in markets like the UK, it is at different stages of maturity across Asia, he said. In Malaysia, RAM Ratings forecasts moderating growth this year in new business for both life and non-life insurers, including those that comply with Islamic principles. Non-life premium gains are seen slowing to 5% in 2025 from 7.3% last year. Still, the potential upside for the nation’s insurance industry “remains healthy”, according to RAM Ratings analyst Loh Kit Yoong. Increasing awareness of the importance of coverage protection and significant numbers of Malaysians who are uninsured and underinsured, especially among lower income households, underpin business opportunities, she said. Online insurance platforms improve insurers’ reach to some of these segments, given the high smartphone and internet access rates in the country, the analyst said. Bjak has seven million users and 16 insurance brands, including Germany’s Allianz SE and Japan’s Tokio Marine, on its platform. Low’s entrepreneurial journey began at age 20 when his family’s financial woes forced him to drop out of a pre-university programme. Before founding Bjak, he was involved in aluminium trading and two other e-commerce ventures that stalled. He cited Warren Buffett as his idol and has read all of Berkshire Hathaway Inc’s annual letters the billionaire investor has written since 1965. Like Buffett, Low wants to embrace a business philosophy focused on more than just monetary success. “He has this quote that he emphasised a lot that I practice: You find out who your role models are and copy them,” he said. title: 'Bursa Rebounds As Investors Turn To Budget 2027 Plays
body: 'The FBM KLCI rebounded in early trade on Friday, gaining 5.37 points or 0.33% to 1,635.73 at 9.27am as investors tracked Wall Street’s overnight recovery and looked for opportunities ahead of Budget 2027, The Star reported.  The local market remained cautious, however, with elevated US bond yields and oil prices continuing to weigh on sentiment.  Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd rose 58 sen to RM41.70, while IHH Healthcare Bhd gained 20 sen to RM7.90 and UWC added 17 sen to RM7.27.  Hengyuan Refining Co Bhd advanced 19 sen to RM3.83 after appointing Erkki Tapio Ranta as its chief executive officer effective Oct 1.  On the losing side, MISC Bhd fell 14 sen to RM7.54, Hong Leong Industries Bhd shed 12 sen to RM16.02, while RHB Bank Bhd and AMMB Holdings Bhd eased five sen and four sen to RM7.42 and RM6.35 respectively.  Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.04% to 50,926.74, while the S&P 500 gained 0.20% to 7,666.48 and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.04% as the global bond selloff eased.  Berjaya Research expects the FBM KLCI to remain cautious as investors monitor US bond yields and oil prices.  The research house said softer US unemployment data due later could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy and provide some relief to equities.  “With the key index slipping into oversold territory, potential mild bargain hunting may resurface amid the easing US 10-year Treasury yield as well as the pullback in oil prices,” it said.  Berjaya Research placed immediate resistance at 1,657 to 1,663 points, with support at 1,625 followed by 1,620.  Meanwhile, Malacca Securities expects sentiment to improve alongside Wall Street but said investors would remain selective, particularly towards potential beneficiaries of Budget 2027, which is due to be tabled next Friday.  It highlighted ViTrox Corp Bhd on stronger demand for high-precision inspection solutions linked to AI infrastructure and advanced packaging, while QES Group Bhd could benefit from its expansion into China’s X-ray semiconductor inspection market.  Hartanah Kenyalang Bhd was also highlighted, with its RM851 million order book equivalent to about 6.8 times FY25 revenue and potentially positioning it to benefit from infrastructure-related initiatives in East Malaysia under Budget 2027.

title: 'Umumkan minit lembaga pengampunan / Make pardons board’s minutes public – 37 NGOs
body: '[ENGLISH VERSION BELOW] Pada ketika negara masih menanggung beban kewangan yang amat besar akibat berbilion ringgit yang diselewengkan dalam skandal 1MDB dan SRC International, persepsi bahawa seorang pegawai tertinggi yang telah disabitkan kesalahan, khususnya bekas Perdana Menteri Najib Razak, iaitu melalui pemberian pengurangan hukuman serta layanan penahanan istimewa (contohnya, diberikan hukuman tahanan rumah yang belum pernah berlaku sebelum ini) telah menjejaskan kepercayaan rakyat. Beban akibat rasuah peringkat tinggi akhirnya ditanggung oleh rakyat, yang menanggung kesan melalui kehilangan hasil negara, beban pembayaran hutang negara, serta pengurangan dana untuk infrastruktur awam dan pembangunan ekonomi yang penting. Terdapat kebimbangan kritikal yang menjejaskan negara kita. Keputusan berkaitan hasil perundangan Najib – daripada pengurangan separuh hukuman penjara asal 12 tahun dan pengurangan denda daripada RM210j kepada RM50j, hinggalah kepada peralihan bersyarat kepada tahanan rumah – menimbulkan persoalan mendalam mengenai ketelusan, akauntabiliti dan kedaulatan undang-undang di Malaysia. Bagi menegakkan integriti sistem keadilan Malaysia dan memenuhi tanggungjawab kepada rakyat, lembaga pengampunan mesti mendedahkan sepenuhnya minit serta justifikasi yang direkodkan dalam proses membuat keputusan. Pendedahan menyeluruh adalah penting untuk menjelaskan bagaimana kes yang melibatkan penyelewengan institusi berskala besar boleh berakhir dengan pelbagai pengurangan hukuman dan kini membolehkan Najib yang telah disabitkan kesalahan menikmati keistimewaan tahanan rumah. Ketelusan penuh daripada lembaga pengampunan bukan sekadar satu permintaan – ia merupakan langkah penting untuk memastikan prinsip layanan sama rata di bawah undang-undang tanpa wujudnya diskriminasi dalam pelaksanaannya (antara dua darjat) ditegakkan dan membuktikan bahawa tiada individu yang berada di atas undang-undang. English version - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Make pardons board’s minutes public for accountability and transparency At a time when the nation continues to bear the immense financial burden of billions of ringgit stolen through the 1MDB and SRC International scandals, the perception that a convicted high-level official, specifically former Prime Minister Najib Razak, receives sentence reductions and preferential confinement arrangements (ie given an unprecedented house arrest sentence) undermines public trust. The burden of high-level corruption ultimately falls upon the people, who pay the price through lost public revenue, national debt servicing, and reduced funding for essential public infrastructure and economic development. There are critical concerns that affect our nation. The decisions surrounding Najib’s legal outcome – from the halving of his original 12-year prison sentence and the reduction of his fine from RM210m to RM50m, to his conditional transition to house arrest – raise profound concerns regarding transparency, accountability and the rule of law in Malaysia. To uphold the integrity of Malaysia’s justice system and satisfy its obligation to the public, the pardons board must release the full minutes and recorded justifications of its decision-making process. Complete disclosure is essential to explain how a case involving massive institutional embezzlement resulted in multiple sentence reductions and the convicted Najib now given house arrest privileges. Full transparency from the pardons board is not merely a request – it is a vital measure to ensure that the principle of equal treatment under the law, without discrimination in its application (antara dua darjat or double standards) is upheld and to prove that no individual stands above the law. title: 'Existing taxes key to 2027 Budget, expect few major changes: Expert
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is likely to focus on improving tax collection and fine-tuning existing taxes rather than introducing major new levies in 2027 Budget, according to KPMG senior tax policy adviser Dr Veerinderjeet Singh. He said stronger enforcement, better use of tax agency analytics and broader tax bases could provide additional revenue while supporting the government's fiscal consolidation efforts. Speaking at a forum hosted by CIMB Securities, Veerinderjeet said the government should "sweat our assets". This is by improving collection efficiency, with scope to gradually raise Malaysia's tax-to-gross domestic product ratio towards 15 per cent through stronger personal, corporate and indirect tax bases. He expects few major tax changes in the upcoming budget, given the continued focus on cost-of-living support and social spending. Recent measures such as the dividend and capital gains taxes reflect a more progressive tax system, although he does not expect the two per cent dividend tax to be raised or capital gains tax extended to listed shares in the budget. A further increase in the 30 per cent top personal income tax rate also appears unlikely. On the sales and service tax (SST), Veerinderjeet estimates coverage has reached about 78-80 per cent of goods and services, bringing it closer to the breadth of the former goods and services tax (GST). He sees scope for broader input exemptions under SST to reduce cascading effects and business costs, although this would mean some revenue loss. GST reinstatement is not expected in thr 2027 Budget, with improving SST efficiency likely to take precedence. Wider e-invoicing participation could also help uncover unreported taxable activity, although exemptions for smaller businesses may be gradually reduced as economic conditions improve. On other measures, Veerinderjeet expects limited additional revenue from the global minimum tax until the first filing cycle provides clearer evidence of collections. A carbon tax remains on the policy agenda but could be delayed to 2028 or later amid business cost pressures. The budget may reaffirm the government's intention to introduce it, potentially at a low initial rate. He also sees only a slight possibility of modest excise duty increases on alcohol and tobacco, while no new windfall levy is expected. For real estate investment trusts, he does not expect the former 10 per cent final withholding tax on distributions to return, although he supports withholding mechanisms to reduce filing and monitoring costs.

title: 'Maybank Turned Its Cash Back Card Perks Into A Playground At Mid Valley
body: 'Last week, we dropped by Mid Valley Megamall to check out the Maybank Cash Back Mastercard Platinum showcase. Held at Centre Court from 23 to 27 September, the five-day event had a little bit of everything, from interactive activities to a closer look at the card’s features.  Five Stops To Explore The Card  The showcase was set up like a stamp-card journey. We picked up a journey card at the start and worked our way through five stations. The first four were More To Discover, Stream For More, More To Enjoy and More To Unwind. Once we had collected all four stamps, we could head to the final stop, Maybank Cafe, and redeem either a ZUS Coffee or a Krispy Kreme doughnut.  The activities at each station were also designed around the card’s benefits. One had a touchscreen game where you had to catch groceries in a basket, a playful take on the card’s 8% cash back on digital lifestyle spending. There were also photo spots with airplane window backdrops featuring destinations like Singapore, Thailand, Japan and South Korea, which are among the countries where the card charges no foreign exchange mark-up fee.  Visitors who applied for the card on-site could unlock three additional activities. These included a Flight Simulator and a Merchandise Redemption station with goodies such as a Maybank tumbler and Lilo & Stitch tote bag. Applicants could also try their luck at a giant Gashapon machine for prizes including a Nintendo Switch 2, Setel vouchers and Grab vouchers. title: 'Fire safety managers, officers mandatory for 9,451 buildings from April 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises.   Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK).   "From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises," he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank today.

title: 'Bursa Ends Lower, FBM KLCI Sheds 20.81 Points As Selling Pressure Persists
body: 'Bursa Malaysia closed broadly lower on Oct 1, with the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) falling 20.81 points, or 1.26%, to 1,630.36 as continued selling pressure tracked a mixed and cautious Wall Street session overnight.  The benchmark index, which closed at 1,651.17 on Sept 30, traded between 1,630.10 and 1,649.87 during the day.  Weakness extended across the broader market. The FBM 70 dropped 215.69 points, or 1.23%, to 17,358.98, while the F4GBM fell 12.12 points, or 1.22%, to 984.34.  The FBM Emas declined 148.49 points, or 1.21%, to 12,143.53, while the FBM Shariah lost 163.34 points, or 1.34%, to 12,013.01.  Heavyweight counters were mostly lower. Maybank slipped four sen to RM9.95, Public Bank fell three sen to RM4.67 and CIMB shed 10 sen to RM7.69. Tenaga Nasional declined six sen to RM12.90, while IHH Healthcare lost 13 sen to RM7.70.  Among the most actively traded stocks, Zetrix AI Bhd added 0.5 sen to 16.5 sen on 188.38 million shares, while VS Industry Bhd fell one sen to 27 sen.  JAKS Resources Bhd dropped 2.5 sen to 18 sen, newly ACE Market listed GB Bond Holdings Bhd slid 4.5 sen to 20.5 sen, while HHRG Bhd gained 0.5 sen to 16.5 sen.  Trading activity eased, with turnover falling to 3.1 billion units worth RM2.7 billion, from 3.63 billion units valued at RM3.62 billion on Sept 30.

title: 'Rights-based approach needed to support longer, dignified lives for older people – Suhakam
body: 'The Malaysian human rights commission, Suhakam, commemorates the International Day of Older Persons 2026 under the theme ‘The age of longevity: Rethinking systems for longer lives’. The theme highlights the need to rethink policies, institutions and systems in response to longer life expectancy and ensure that older people can continue to enjoy their rights with dignity, equality and independence. Malaysia is experiencing a significant demographic shift. According to the Department of Statistics Malaysia, people aged 60 years and above accounted for an estimated 4.1 million people or 12% of Malaysia’s population in 2025, compared with 3.9 million or 11.6% in 2024. The DoS projects that Malaysia will become an ageing nation by 2036, when the proportion of people aged 60 years and above is expected to exceed 15% of the total population. This demographic change underscores the need for Malaysia to strengthen its preparedness for an ageing society and ensure that policies, services and systems remain responsive to the changing needs of its population. Suhakam stresses that preparing for an ageing society requires more than providing care and welfare assistance. Older people must have meaningful access to economic security, employment, affordable and accessible healthcare, adequate housing and social protection. They must also be protected from abuse, neglect, exploitation and discrimination and have access to public spaces and services. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member As digitalisation increasingly shapes access to information and essential public services, efforts towards digital inclusion should also be strengthened to ensure that older people are not left behind by technological changes. Meaningful participation must remain central to policies and decisions affecting older people. Their experiences, knowledge and contributions should be recognised and valued, with opportunities for them to participate in family, community, economic and social life according to their abilities and choices. The protection and wellbeing of older people also form part of Malaysia’s broader human rights commitments, including recommendations made during Malaysia’s fourth universal periodic review in 2024 to enhance the rights, protection and wellbeing of older people. Suhakam has continued to advance discussions on the rights of older people through forums and engagements focusing on economic, social and cultural rights, including social protection, healthcare, housing, employment and other aspects of wellbeing. These engagements have also examined the implications of an ageing population and Malaysia’s preparedness to respond to the needs and rights of older people at the national and state levels. At the regional level, Suhakam in its capacity as chair of the South East Asia National Human Rights Institutions Forum for 2026, has also brought the rights of older people into regional discussions as an emerging and cross-cutting human rights issue. Suhakam also reiterates its long-standing support for the development of specific legislation to protect the rights of older people in Malaysia. As early as 2018, Suhakam fully supported the development of an older people’s bill following efforts by the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development to address gaps in existing laws, including in relation to elder abuse and neglect. Suhakam maintains that a dedicated legal framework would strengthen the protection of older people and help ensure that their rights, dignity and wellbeing are upheld as Malaysia transitions towards an ageing society. In conjunction with the International Day of Older Persons 2026, Suhakam will also commemorate Older Persons’ Day on 7 October at Rumah Seri Kenangan Cheras under the theme ‘Celebrating our older persons!’. This will honour the wisdom, experience and contributions of older people to our communities and nation. The programme reflects Suhakam’s commitment not only to advocate for the rights of older people but also to engage with them meaningfully, recognise their contributions and affirm their place as valued members of society. On this International Day of Older Persons, Suhakam calls on the government, relevant institutions, civil society, communities and families to strengthen collective efforts towards an inclusive society where people can age with dignity, remain active and independent according to their abilities and choices, participate meaningfully in decisions and communities, and continue to enjoy their human rights throughout all stages of life. – Suhakam The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. title: 'Takaichi Pledges Fiscal Discipline as Japan's Debt Bill Rises
body: 'TOKYO (Oct 5): Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday pledged to "control" bond issuance and act swiftly against market turbulence, seeking to reassure investors worried about Japan's worsening public finances that have pushed up bond yields. She said the government would pursue fiscal sustainability even as it ramps up spending to bolster growth potential, including by reviewing existing tax breaks and subsidies. "Fiscal sustainability is obviously a prerequisite in pursuing our 'responsible and proactive' fiscal policy," Takaichi said in a policy speech to parliament. The remarks reflect mounting concern in Tokyo over rising Japanese government bond (JGB) yields, which would boost the cost of funding the premier's ambitious spending plans. The 30-year JGB yield hit a record high of 4.235% on Monday on jitters over the risk of increased debt issuance and inflation worries fuelled by the Middle East war. Japan's public debt, at roughly twice the size of its economy, is the largest in the developed world. Funding costs are climbing as the Bank of Japan raises interest rates and tapers bond purchases in an effort to wean the economy off decades of massive stimulus. Takaichi said the government will seek to draw in private investment in growth areas through "massive, long-term fiscal expenditure deployed in a well-planned, predictable manner." At the same time, it would keep a lid on annual bond issuance, calibrating borrowing to tax revenues, interest rates, debt-financing costs and economic and market developments, the premier said in the speech to an extraordinary parliament session that convened on Monday. "If the economy and markets make unexpected moves, we will scrutinise their impact and respond nimbly as needed," she added without elaborating. Fiscal policy is set to take centre stage in parliamentary debate in Japan as rising concerns over the fiscal health of advanced economies fuel a broader rise in global bond yields. The administration's immediate priority is passing legislation backing Takaichi's plan for a two-year tax cut on food items from next April, which sparked a bond selloff due to a lack of detail on how the revenue shortfall will be filled. The government is also preparing next year's budget, with ministries seeking record levels of spending. Separately, Takaichi said Tokyo will set aside multi-year funds for strategically important economic security initiatives. "We will implement policies steadily, get things done one by one, and communicate them carefully to the public and markets," Takaichi said. Keen to soothe market jitters, the administration has moved to dispel perceptions that its fiscal policy is reflationary or that it has leaned on the BOJ to refrain from hiking rates. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Saturday that the government has begun refining its messaging to reassure investors that Takaichi is not pursuing reflationary policies. But not all are on board. Former BOJ deputy governor Masazumi Wakatabe, a reflationist academic who is currently a private member of the government's key economic panel, said the recent rise in JGB yields was due to expectations of further BOJ rate hikes rather than concern over Japan's finances, minutes of the panel's recent meeting showed on Monday. Wakatabe also said the government had ultimate responsibility in guiding economic policy and stressed the need for close coordination between the BOJ and the administration on monetary policy, according to the minutes of the meeting which debated the central bank's rate-hike decision last month. title: 'Maybank Supports Digital Learning At SMK Santubong | Sarawak Tribune
body: 'KUCHING: SMK Santubong received four Smart TVs from Maybank Sarawak to support digital learning and enhance teaching and learning at the school. The contribution was made in conjunction with Maybank Group’s 14th Global Corporate Responsibility (CR) Day 2026 and Cahaya Kasih Challenge 2026-2027 programme held at the school today. Santubong Member of Parliament, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri, said the initiative was in line with the changing needs of education, particularly as technology continued to play a greater role in learning. She said such support was especially important for schools located away from urban centres, where students could benefit from greater access to digital learning facilities. “This event is to ensure that students are able to gain the knowledge they need through education. Especially for schools far from the city, they really need education like this,” she said. Nancy emphasised that education remained a key priority as it could open pathways to employment, improve incomes, and help families build better lives. “Do not let your place of residence or family backgrounds become a barrier. I believe that with knowledge and continuous effort, all of you can achieve the aspirations you dream of,” she said. Nancy said the collaboration between Maybank and the Santubong parliamentary constituency was not new, with the bank having previously supported Pusat Aktiviti Kanak-Kanak (PAKK) Bandar Baru Samariang in 2024 and 2025. Maybank Sarawak’s Regional Director, Abang Jamili Abang Julai, said the initiative reflected the bank’s role in contributing to the community through education and knowledge-sharing. “This is our opportunity in the banking sector to contribute to the children in school. We hope to share our knowledge in financial literacy, business planning and digital technology to help the community,” he said. More than 60 Maybank employees from its regional office, branches and centres in Sarawak took part in the programme, which also featured sharing sessions on financial literacy and scam awareness. The initiative, guided by the theme ‘Impacting Society Positively: Enabling Well-being For All’, focuses on education, community empowerment and environmental sustainability.
